value_domain: Census Australian Defence Force service, detailed
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Australian Defence Force service, detailed (ADCP)
variable_description: Whether a person is in the Australian Defence Force now, has served before, or has done both, kept separate for regular and reserve service. The ABS says the ADF "consists of regulars and reservists, and this variable provides a detailed breakdown of current and previous service for both" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021), so it distinguishes a current regular who once served in the reserves from one who has only ever been a regular. ADFP on the same person row is the four-category collapse of the same answer, and both columns are new to the 2021 Census person table.
value_definition: A single digit 1 to 8: four codes for people still serving (regular only, reserves only, and the two mixed histories), three for people who have left (regular only, reserves only, both), and 8 for never served. Not stated is '&', not applicable '@' and overseas visitor 'V'. Scope is persons aged 15 years and over.
limitation: It carries no rank, service branch, length of service, deployment or discharge date, so it cannot identify veterans by war service or by eligibility for Department of Veterans' Affairs support. It is a self-report at one Census night in August 2021 and there is no equivalent column on the 2011 or 2016 person tables, so a service history cannot be assembled across Censuses.
rationale: The variable is an ABS Census output variable and the ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for it, giving the definition, the eight-way category split and the scope.
evidence_quote: The Australian Defence Force (ADF) consists of regulars and reservists, and this variable provides a detailed breakdown of current and previous service for both.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Australian defence force service detailed', with the value domain given as 'finite source-defined values' and the limitation as 'The source defines the value domain. Frequency information is not included.', so nothing on the page said how it differed from ADFP.

value_domain: ASGS Australian Drainage Division code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Non ABS Structures, Australian Drainage Divisions
variable_description: The river basin the dwelling sits in, coded from where the dwelling was enumerated. The ABS defines these divisions as "an ABS Mesh Block approximation of drainage divisions provided through the Bureau of Meteorology's Australian Hydrological Geospatial Fabric" (ASGS Edition 3), so this is a hydrological region rather than an administrative one. It sits with the other geography codes on the 2021 dwelling row - SA1UCD to SA4UCD, STEUCD, LGAD, POAD and CEDD - and is the one that places a dwelling in a catchment rather than in an administrative area.
value_definition: A three-character ASGS Non ABS Structure code: the letter D followed by a two-digit division number, for example D03 Murray-Darling Basin. There are 17 Australian Drainage Divisions covering the whole of Australia without gaps or overlaps, and that count already includes the three non-spatial special purpose codes D94 No usual address, D97 Migratory - Offshore - Shipping and DZZ Outside Australia. D91 Unclassified (Aust.) carries Christmas Island, the Cocos (Keeling) Islands and Norfolk Island.
limitation: A drainage division is not nested inside a state - the Murray-Darling Basin crosses four states and territories - so division totals and state totals are different groupings and the two cannot be treated as a hierarchy. Because the boundary is a Mesh Block approximation of the Geofabric rather than a surveyed catchment line, a dwelling close to a divide can be allocated to the neighbouring division.
rationale: The '(en)' suffix in the PLIDA item name and the dwelling table it sits on identify this as the enumeration-based ASGS coding of the dwelling, and the ASGS Edition 3 Non ABS Structures page defines the division, its coding and its count.
evidence_quote: Australian Drainage Divisions are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of drainage divisions provided through the Bureau of Meteorology's Australian Hydrological Geospatial Fabric.
supersedes_rationale: The value domain read 'not specified' and the sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' stood as both the value definition and the limitation, so the page never said what a drainage division is or that the codes come from the ASGS.

value_domain: ASGS Australian Drainage Division code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Non ABS Structures, Australian Drainage Divisions
variable_description: The river basin containing the person's usual address, coded from place of usual residence rather than from where they were counted on Census night. The ABS defines the divisions as "an ABS Mesh Block approximation of drainage divisions provided through the Bureau of Meteorology's Australian Hydrological Geospatial Fabric" (ASGS Edition 3). Where a person was away from home in August 2021 this can differ from ADDIVD on the dwelling record they were enumerated in, which is the enumeration-based coding of the same classification.
value_definition: A three-character ASGS Non ABS Structure code: D followed by two digits, for example D03 Murray-Darling Basin. The 17 divisions cover the whole of Australia without gaps or overlaps and that count already includes the three non-spatial special purpose codes D94, D97 and DZZ; D91 Unclassified (Aust.) holds the Other Territories.
limitation: Living in a division does not mean drawing on its water, since most urban supply is piped across catchments, so this is a location code rather than a measure of exposure to a basin's water resources. It is also one snapshot of usual residence, so a move between divisions during the year leaves no trace here.
rationale: The '(ur)' suffix and the person table identify this as the usual-residence coding of the ASGS drainage division, and the ASGS Edition 3 page defines the division and its codes.
evidence_quote: Australian Drainage Divisions are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of drainage divisions provided through the Bureau of Meteorology's Australian Hydrological Geospatial Fabric.
supersedes_rationale: The value domain read 'not specified' and 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' was printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so the page never explained the classification or that this is the usual-residence coding of it.

value_domain: Census Australian Defence Force service
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Australian Defence Force service (ADFP)
variable_description: Whether a person has ever served in the Australian Defence Force and, if so, whether they are still serving. The ABS says it "describes whether a person is currently serving or has previously served in the Australian Defence Force (ADF)" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021), covering the Army including NORFORCE, the Navy and the Air Force, and also National Service and the Second Australian Imperial Force. ADCP on the same row splits the same answer eight ways; this column is the four-way version used for headline veteran counts.
value_definition: Codes 1 currently serving in the regular service, 2 currently serving in the reserves, 3 not currently serving but has previously served, and 4 has never served, plus '&' not stated, '@' not applicable and 'V' overseas visitor. Scope is persons aged 15 years and over.
limitation: The four categories merge the mixed histories that ADCP keeps apart, so a current regular who once served in the reserves cannot be told from one who has only ever been a regular. Service in the ADF is all that counts, so police, emergency services and service in an allied country's military fall into 'has never served'.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition, the four categories, the supplementary codes and the scope.
evidence_quote: This variable describes whether a person is currently serving or has previously served in the Australian Defence Force (ADF).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Australian defence force service', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values' and the limitation as a note about frequency information, so it never said what the ADF covers or how the column relates to ADCP.

value_domain: Census age in ten-year groups
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age in ten year groups (AGE10P)
variable_description: The person's age at Census night placed in ten-year bands, the coarsest of the three age columns on the 2021 person table. The ABS says it "collects each person's age in ten-year groups. If age is not reported, it is imputed" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021), so the bands are built from the same reported date of birth or stated age that AGEP holds in single years. AGE5P sits between the two at five-year bands.
value_definition: Eleven codes, 01 for 0-9 years through 10 for 90-99 years, with 11 for 100 years and over. There is no not stated category, because an unreported age is imputed rather than left blank.
limitation: The bands cut across the ages that decide eligibility and scope - 15, 16, 18, 25 and 65 all fall inside a band - so labour force scope, income support eligibility or pension age cannot be worked out from this column. Use AGEP where a threshold matters, and note that a mean age from banded data depends on the midpoint assumed for the open top group.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition and the full eleven-category list.
evidence_quote: This variable collects each person's age in ten-year groups. If age is not reported, it is imputed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Age in ten year groups', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so the page never listed the bands, said the top band is open at 100, or noted that missing age is imputed rather than coded not stated.

value_domain: Census age in five-year groups
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age in five year groups (AGE5P)
variable_description: The person's age at Census night placed in five-year bands, the age column used for standard population pyramids and for age-standardising Census counts. The ABS says it "collects each person's age in five-year groups. If age is not reported, it is imputed" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). It is derived from the same answer as AGEP, so it never disagrees with the single-year column, and AGE10P is the coarser version of it.
value_definition: Twenty-one groups running from 0-4 years to 100 years and over. Imputed ages are included in the bands, so there is no not stated code.
limitation: Five-year bands still straddle the ages that decide scope: 16, 18 and 21 all sit inside the 15-19 and 20-24 bands, so a school-leaving, voting or drinking-age population cannot be built here. The top group is open, so it cannot separate the very old and any mean age depends on the midpoint chosen for it.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition and the full twenty-one-group list.
evidence_quote: This variable collects each person's age in five-year groups. If age is not reported, it is imputed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Age in 5-year groups', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values' and no statement of the bands or of the open top group.

value_domain: Census age in completed years
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age (AGEP)
variable_description: Age in completed years at Census night, and the age column to use whenever an analysis needs an exact threshold. The ABS says it "collects each person's age. If age is not reported, it is imputed" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021); age is derived from date of birth where that was given and from stated age otherwise. It appears on the 2011, 2016 and 2021 person tables, so it is the one demographic column that supports the same cut across all three Censuses, and IFAGEP, which sits on all three of those person tables, flags which records were imputed.
value_definition: Whole years from 0 to 115, with 0 recorded for infants aged less than one year. Age is output in whole years only, so there are no months or fractions and no not stated code.
limitation: A missing age is filled in rather than flagged in this column - IFAGEP is the flag - so a record with an age is not necessarily a record where age was reported. Imputation reached 4.4% of persons nationally in 2021 and more than 20% in some remote communities, which means an age distribution for a small area can be partly modelled rather than reported.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition, the derivation from date of birth, the 0 to 115 range and the national non-response and imputation rates.
evidence_quote: This variable collects each person's age. If age is not reported, it is imputed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Age of respondent', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so it never said that age is derived from date of birth, that it is output in whole years, or that missing age is imputed rather than coded not stated.

value_domain: ASCCEG 2019 cultural and ethnic group code
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Ancestry 1st response (ANC1P)
variable_description: The first of up to two ancestries a person reported, coded to the ABS cultural and ethnic groups classification. The ABS says the variable "indicates how a person identifies their ancestry. Respondents are able to provide up to two responses. The first ancestry provided is output into Ancestry 1st response (ANC1P)" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). ANC2P holds the second response and ANCRP says how many were given; ancestry is asked of everyone and is a separate question from country of birth in BPLP and from Indigenous status in INGP.
value_definition: A code from the Australian Standard Classification of Cultural and Ethnic Groups (ASCCEG), 2019: 321 categories at the four-digit level, 41 at two digits and 12 at one digit, with supplementary codes for inadequately described, not stated (&&&&) and overseas visitor (VVVV).
limitation: First and second are processing order, not preference, so treating ANC1P as a person's main or strongest ancestry overstates what was asked. Only two responses are kept, so a person identifying with three or more has the rest dropped, and the 6.2% non-response in 2021 falls into the not stated code rather than being spread across groups.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition, the ASCCEG 2019 classification and its category counts, the supplementary codes and the non-response rate.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates how a person identifies their ancestry. Respondents are able to provide up to two responses. The first ancestry provided is output into Ancestry 1st response (ANC1P).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Ancestry 1st Response', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so it never named ASCCEG, said how many categories there are, or warned that the first response is not ranked.

value_domain: ASCCEG 2019 cultural and ethnic group code
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Ancestry 2nd response (ANC2P)
variable_description: The second ancestry a person reported, populated only for the people who gave two. The ABS says "the second ancestry provided is output into Ancestry 2nd response (ANC2P)" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021), using the same classification as ANC1P. Because a person who reported one ancestry is coded not applicable here rather than not stated, this column is what distinguishes single-ancestry identification from a missing answer.
value_definition: The same ASCCEG 2019 codes as ANC1P, with 321 four-digit categories. There is no not stated category: a person who gave one ancestry is coded not applicable, and a person who answered nothing appears as not stated in ANC1P.
limitation: Not applicable is not proof of a single ancestry - it means only one was written down, and the form accepts at most two, so the column cannot measure how many ancestries a person actually claims. Adding counts from ANC1P and ANC2P also double-counts people rather than ancestries unless the responses are combined, which is what the ABS variable ANCP does; the PLIDA Census tables do not carry ANCP.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition, the difference in treatment of not stated against not applicable, and the shared classification.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates how a person identifies their ancestry. Respondents are able to provide up to two responses. The second ancestry provided is output into Ancestry 2nd response (ANC2P).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Ancestry 2nd Response', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so it never said that the column has no not stated code or that a blank means one ancestry was given.

value_domain: Census ancestry response count indicator
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Ancestry one or two response indicator (ANCRP)
variable_description: Whether the person gave one ancestry or two, held as a count rather than as the ancestries themselves. The ABS says it "indicates whether a person provided one response or two responses to the ancestry question" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). It saves a user from having to infer multiple identification by testing whether ANC2P is not applicable, and it is on the 2021 person table only.
value_definition: Codes 1 one response and 2 two responses, plus '&' not stated and 'V' overseas visitor.
limitation: It counts what was written down, not what a person identifies with: the form takes at most two ancestries, so a person with three is coded the same as a person with exactly two. It exists only for 2021, so the same measure of multiple ancestry cannot be made on the 2011 or 2016 person tables.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition and the four categories.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates whether a person provided one response or two responses to the ancestry question.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Ancestry one or two response indicator', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values' and no statement of the codes or of the two-response cap.

value_domain: Census core activity need for assistance
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Core activity need for assistance (ASSNP)
variable_description: Whether the person needs help with self-care, mobility or communication because of a long-term condition, a disability or old age - the Census's proxy for profound or severe disability. The ABS says it "records the number of people with a profound or severe core activity limitation", who are "those needing assistance in their day to day lives in one or more of the three core activity areas of self-care, mobility and communication" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). It is on the 2011, 2016 and 2021 person tables, which makes it the only measure of a person's own disability in the Census that spans all three.
value_definition: Codes 1 has need for assistance with core activities and 2 does not, plus '&' not stated and 'V' overseas visitor. There is no not applicable code, because the question is asked of all persons.
limitation: It is a threshold and not a scale: it finds the profound and severe end only, so people with a moderate or mild limitation, and people who need help with tasks outside self-care, mobility and communication, are coded as having no need. It is also not a diagnosis and will not agree with NDIS participation or with the disability estimates from the Survey of Disability, Ageing and Carers.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition of the profound or severe core activity limitation concept, the three core activity areas and the four categories.
evidence_quote: People with a profound or severe core activity limitation are those needing assistance in their day to day lives in one or more of the three core activity areas of self-care, mobility and communication.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Core Activity Need for Assistance', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so it never named the three core activities or the severity threshold the measure sets.

value_domain: ASGS Australia (AUS) level of place of usual residence
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence (PURP)
variable_description: The top level of the geographic coding of the person's usual address: whether that address is in geographic Australia at all. The ABS defines place of usual residence as "the geographic area in which a person usually lives. It may or may not be the place where the person was counted on Census Night" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021), and AUSTP is the Australia (AUS) level of that coding, the coarsest of the geography columns on the 2021 person table alongside STEUCP, SA4UCP down to MBUCP for the same address. Its practical job is to isolate the overseas visitor, no usual address and migratory, off-shore and shipping cases before any finer geography is analysed.
value_definition: The Australia (AUS) level of the ASGS Main Structure, the top of the hierarchy that Mesh Blocks, SA1s to SA4s and states and territories aggregate into, together with the extra categories the usual residence coding carries: no usual address, migratory, off-shore and shipping, and overseas visitor (VVVV). There is no not stated code: an incomplete usual address is imputed, and IFPURP records that it was.
limitation: Being the top of the hierarchy, it separates almost nobody: nearly every person counted has a usual address in Australia, so a cross-tabulation on this column alone will look empty. It also records the address as at Census night 2021, not a residency test, so a person on a short overseas posting who kept an Australian usual address is coded in Australia.
rationale: The '(ur)' suffix and the person table identify this as the Australia level of the ASGS coding of place of usual residence; the ABS Census Dictionary defines that concept and the ASGS Main Structure page defines the AUS level.
evidence_quote: This variable records the geographic area in which a person usually lives. It may or may not be the place where the person was counted on Census Night.
supersedes_rationale: The value domain read 'not specified' and 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' stood as both the value definition and the limitation, so the page never said that '(ur)' means usual residence or that AUST is a level of the ASGS.

value_domain: ASGS Australia (AUS) level of place of usual residence one year ago
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence one year ago (PUR1P)
variable_description: Whether the person's usual address one year before the Census was in Australia. The ABS defines the underlying concept as "the geographic area in which a person usually lived one year before the Census" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021), and this column is the Australia (AUS) level of that coding, with AUSTU5P doing the same job for five years earlier. Read against AUSTP it is what identifies people who arrived from overseas in the year to August 2021.
value_definition: The Australia (AUS) level of the ASGS coding of place of usual residence one year ago, so in practice a split between in Australia and the overseas category the ABS codes at 9299 in the SA2-level output, with not stated for people who did not answer and not applicable for children under one year.
limitation: It compares two points and nothing in between, so a person who went overseas and came back within the year is coded exactly like a person who never left, and there is no arrival date. Non-response was 6.0% in 2021, which is large relative to the overseas group this column is usually used to find.
rationale: The '(ur1y)' suffix and the person table identify this as the Australia level of the ASGS coding of place of usual residence one year ago, which the ABS Census Dictionary defines and for which it publishes the overseas and not stated codes.
evidence_quote: This variable records the geographic area in which a person usually lived one year before the Census.
supersedes_rationale: The value domain read 'not specified' and the same sentence stood as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that '(ur1y)' means usual residence one year before Census night.

value_domain: ASGS Australia (AUS) level of place of usual residence five years ago
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence five years ago (PUR5P)
variable_description: Whether the person's usual address five years before the Census was in Australia. The ABS defines the concept as "the geographic area in which a person usually lived five years before the Census" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021), which for the 2021 Census means the position at 10 August 2016. It is the coarsest of the five-year mobility columns on the person table, sitting above STEU5P, LGAU5P and MBU5P for the same address.
value_definition: The Australia (AUS) level of the ASGS coding of place of usual residence five years ago, giving an in Australia against overseas split, with additional categories for no usual residence, migratory, off-shore and shipping, not stated, and not applicable.
limitation: Scope is persons aged five years and over, so every younger child is not applicable and cannot be counted as a mover or an arrival. The five-year gap hides everything between the two dates: someone who spent four of those years overseas and returned before Census night is coded the same as someone who never left. Non-response was 6.9% in 2021.
rationale: The '(ur5y)' suffix and the person table identify this as the Australia level of the ASGS coding of place of usual residence five years ago; the ABS Census Dictionary defines that concept, its scope and its supplementary categories.
evidence_quote: This variable records the geographic area in which a person usually lived five years before the Census.
supersedes_rationale: The value domain read 'not specified' and 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' was printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said that this is the five-years-ago usual residence coding or that under-fives are out of scope.

value_domain: Census count of bedrooms in an occupied private dwelling
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of bedrooms in private dwelling (BEDD)
variable_description: The number of bedrooms in the occupied private dwelling, held as a number rather than as a range. The ABS says it "records the count of bedrooms in each occupied private dwelling" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021), and the form asks respondents to include any room built as a bedroom even where it is now a study, office, computer room or sewing room. BEDRD on the same dwelling row is the banded version, and this column is one of the inputs to housing suitability (HOSD) on that row.
value_definition: Two digits: 00 for none, which includes studio apartments and bedsitters, through 29, with 30 meaning 30 or more bedrooms. Not stated is '&&' and not applicable '@@'.
limitation: It counts the dwelling's rooms, not how the household uses them, so it cannot say how many people sleep in a room or whether a household is crowded - HOSD combines it with household composition to answer that. Unoccupied private dwellings and all non-private dwellings are not applicable, so a bedroom count is missing precisely where institutional and group living is.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition, the 00 to 30 code range, the treatment of bedsitters and the form's instruction about rooms used for other purposes.
evidence_quote: This variable records the count of bedrooms in each occupied private dwelling.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Number of Bedrooms in Private Dwelling', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so nothing said that studios count as zero, that the top code is 30 or more, or that non-private dwellings are excluded.

value_domain: Census count of bedrooms in an occupied private dwelling, in ranges
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of bedrooms in private dwelling (ranges) (BEDRD)
variable_description: The dwelling's bedroom count collapsed into seven groups, topping out at six or more. The ABS says it "records the number of bedrooms in each occupied private dwelling in ranges" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). It is a recode of BEDD on the same row, so the two never disagree, and it is the version used in most published Census housing tables.
value_definition: A single digit: 0 none, which includes studio apartments and bedsitters, 1 through 5 for one to five bedrooms, and 6 for six bedrooms or more. Not stated is '&' and not applicable '@', the latter covering unoccupied private dwellings, non-private dwellings and migratory, off-shore and shipping SA1s.
limitation: The open top group means large dwellings cannot be separated and any mean bedroom count from this column is biased down. It is not an independent measurement either: because it is derived from BEDD, using both columns adds no information and cannot be used to cross-check the answer.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition, the seven categories, and what the not applicable code covers.
evidence_quote: This variable records the number of bedrooms in each occupied private dwelling in ranges.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Number of Bedrooms in Private Dwelling (ranges)', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values' and no statement of where the ranges cut or that the top group is open.

value_domain: SACC 2016 country code, mother's country of birth
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Country of birth of mother (BPFP)
variable_description: The country the person's mother was born in, as reported on the person's own Census form. The ABS says it "indicates the country in which a person's mother was born" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). With BPMP for the father it feeds the derived summary BPPP, and together with BPLP it is what identifies second-generation Australians.
value_definition: A four-digit Standard Australian Classification of Countries (SACC), 2016 code, 293 categories grouped into nine regions such as Oceania and Antarctica and South-East Asia, with supplementary codes 0000 inadequately described and 0001 at sea, '&&&&' not stated and 'VVVV' overseas visitor.
limitation: It is a birthplace reported on the respondent's form, not a link to the mother's own Census record, so it can be unknown or wrong where the respondent did not grow up with her - the 2021 non-response rate was 5.6%. It is answered whether or not the mother is alive or in Australia, so it cannot be used to identify a resident parent; RLHP and FPIP are the columns for that.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition, the SACC 2016 classification, the supplementary codes and the non-response rate.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates the country in which a person's mother was born.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Country of Birth of Mother', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so it never named SACC 2016 or warned that this is not a link to the mother's own record.

value_domain: SACC 2016 country of birth code
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Country of birth of person (BPLP)
variable_description: The country the person was born in, the Census's base measure of migrant status. The ABS says it "indicates in which country a person was born" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). It sits on the person table with YARP year of arrival, CITP citizenship and LANP language used at home, and those companions are what turn a birthplace into a migration history.
value_definition: A Standard Australian Classification of Countries (SACC), 2016 code with 293 categories at the four-digit level, 39 at two digits and 12 at one digit, plus supplementary codes for inadequately described, at sea, not stated and overseas visitor.
limitation: Country of birth is neither migration status nor ancestry: an Australian citizen born overseas, a temporary visa holder and a permanent migrant share the same code, and only CITP, YARP or linked visa data separate them. SACC is a present-day country list, so a birthplace is coded to the country as the 2016 classification defines it rather than to the state that existed at the person's birth. Non-response was 5.3% in 2021.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition, the SACC 2016 classification and its three levels, the supplementary codes and the non-response rate.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates in which country a person was born.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Country of Birth of Person', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so it never named the classification or its 293 categories.

value_domain: SACC 2016 country code, father's country of birth
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Country of birth of father (BPMP)
variable_description: The country the person's father was born in, carried under the older PLIDA label 'Birthplace of Male Parent'. The ABS says it "indicates the country of birth of each person's father" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021), and the 2021 Census Dictionary now names it country of birth of father. It is the companion to BPFP for the mother, and the two are the only inputs to the derived generational summary BPPP.
value_definition: A four-digit Standard Australian Classification of Countries (SACC), 2016 code with 293 categories across nine regions, plus 0000 inadequately described, 0001 at sea, '&&&&' not stated and 'VVVV' overseas visitor.
limitation: A not stated father's birthplace pushes the whole record into the not stated category of BPPP, so the 5.7% non-response here propagates into any first- or second-generation Australian count built from that derived column. The column also says nothing about whether the father is alive, in Australia, or living with the person.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition, the SACC 2016 classification, the supplementary codes and the non-response rate; the PLIDA label is the earlier Census name for the same item.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates the country of birth of each person's father.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Birthplace of Male Parent', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so a reader searching the current Census Dictionary for that phrase would find nothing and the page never named the classification.

value_domain: Census country of birth of parents summary
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Country of birth of parents (BPPP)
variable_description: Whether each of a person's parents was born in Australia or overseas, reduced to one code. The ABS says it "indicates if a person's father and/or mother was born in Australia or overseas" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). It is derived from BPFP and BPMP on the same row and is the column that supports first- and second-generation Australian analysis once it is crossed with the person's own country of birth in BPLP.
value_definition: Six categories: both parents born overseas, father only born overseas, mother only born overseas, both parents born in Australia, not stated where the birthplace of either or both parents was not stated, and overseas visitor.
limitation: It collapses everything to Australia against overseas, so it cannot say which country a parent came from - BPFP and BPMP are needed for that. It is also not generational status on its own: an Australian-born person with an overseas-born parent is second generation, but an overseas-born person with the same parents is first, and only BPLP tells them apart.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition and the six categories, and stating that it is used to identify first and second generation Australians.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates if a person's father and/or mother was born in Australia or overseas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Country of Birth of Parents', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so it never said the column is a four-way Australia against overseas summary rather than a country code.

value_domain: Synthetic 2011 Census person identifier
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The key that ties a 2011 Census person record to the family and dwelling records collected with it. All three 2011 Census tables carry it, which is why a person identifier appears on tables that otherwise look like family and dwelling tables: a person's own characteristics, their family's composition and their dwelling's attributes all join on this column. It is an identifier created for the integrated asset, which the ABS describes as "a secure data asset combining information on health, education, government payments, income and taxation, employment, and population demographics (including the Census) over time", and links out to other PLIDA sources run through the person linkage spine rather than through this column. The 2016 Census tables and the 2021 person table carry SYNTHETIC_AEUID as the person key in its place, while DWELLING_ID and FAMILY_ID - which are on the 2011 tables as well - are the dwelling and family keys.
value_definition: An opaque identifier with no internal meaning: it does not encode a name, a date of birth or a location, and there is no finite list to publish.
limitation: It is unique within the 2011 Census only. It does not carry across to the 2016 or 2021 Census tables and it is not the spine identifier, so a person cannot be followed between Censuses on this column - the spine link is what does that. It is not a dwelling or family key either: the 2011 dwelling and family tables carry DWELLING_ID and FAMILY_ID for that, so a distinct count of this column on those tables counts people.
rationale: No published page defines this column. The registry shows it on all three 2011 Census tables while the person key on the 2016 tables and the 2021 person table is SYNTHETIC_AEUID, which identifies it as the within-Census person key for the 2011 vintage; the ABS PLIDA page is cited for the asset's de-identified construction.
evidence_quote: PLIDA is a secure data asset combining information on health, education, government payments, income and taxation, employment, and population demographics (including the Census) over time.
supersedes_rationale: The domain was inferred from the variable name as an 'Opaque identifier (inferred)' with the limitation saying only that the values 'are of the right shape but are not a confirmed mapping', so the page never said what the identifier joins or that it is confined to the 2011 Census.

value_domain: Census Certificate III attainment or current non-school study indicator
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Attainment of Certificate III or higher or working towards a non-school qualification (C3SP)
variable_description: Whether a person aged 15 and over holds a Certificate III or higher, or is currently studying towards a non-school qualification. The ABS says it "indicates whether a person has attained a Certificate III or higher or is currently studying a non-school qualification" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). It is a national reporting variable, created by combining the non-school qualification column QALLP with the current attendance column TYPP, and it exists so that Closing the Gap Target 7 on youth engagement can be measured directly from the Census.
value_definition: Four categories: attained Certificate III or higher or studying for a non-school qualification; has not attained and is not studying; not applicable, covering persons under 15 years and those with incomplete qualification data; and overseas visitor.
limitation: It is one threshold with a yes or no answer, so a Certificate III and a doctorate are the same value, and it mixes stock with flow by counting a person enrolled in their first course alongside a graduate. The not applicable category combines people out of scope by age with people whose qualification data was incomplete, so it is not a clean denominator for a rate.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable under national reporting, giving the definition, the categories, the scope and the Closing the Gap purpose.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates whether a person has attained a Certificate III or higher or is currently studying a non-school qualification.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Attainment of certificate iii or higher or working towards a non-school qualification', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so nothing said why the threshold sits at Certificate III or that the column exists for Closing the Gap reporting.

value_domain: Census count of all children in a family
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of all children in family (CACF)
variable_description: How many children of any age and any dependency status belong to the family, up to six or more. The ABS says it "counts the number of dependent and non-dependent children in the family. It includes up to three children who were temporarily absent from the household on Census Night" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). It is the total that CDCF, CDCUF, CDSF and CNDCF break apart by dependency, and unlike them it does not encode family type in the code.
value_definition: Codes 1 to 5 for one to five children and 6 for six or more, plus '@' not applicable. Not applicable covers couple families with no children, other families, non-family and non-classifiable households, unoccupied private dwellings, non-private dwellings and migratory, off-shore and shipping SA1s.
limitation: It counts children usually resident in this family, so a child who lives with the other parent is absent from the count and a parent's total number of children cannot be recovered - TISP, number of children ever born, is the column for that. Only three temporarily absent children can be reported per dwelling, so a family with four away on Census night is understated.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition, the six categories, what the not applicable code covers and how temporarily absent children are treated.
evidence_quote: This variable counts the number of dependent and non-dependent children in the family. It includes up to three children who were temporarily absent from the household on Census Night.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Count of All Children in Family', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so it never said the top code is open at six or that temporarily absent children are capped at three.

value_domain: Census count of adults with a selected long-term health condition in the household
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of adults (15 years and over) with selected long-term health condition(s) in household (CALTHD)
variable_description: How many people aged 15 and over in the household reported at least one of the ten selected long-term health conditions. The ABS says it "counts the number of adults aged 15 years and over in a household who reported they had at least one of the selected long-term health conditions" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). CCLTHD is the same count for children under 15 and CPLTHD covers everyone, so the three together give the household's illness profile by age group; the person-level counterpart is CLTHP.
value_definition: A single digit: 0 to 4 for no adults through four adults, 5 for five or more, and 6 where some adults in the household did not state a condition. '&' means all adults in the household did not state, and '@' is not applicable.
limitation: It counts people, not conditions, so an adult with four of the ten conditions adds one to the total - CLTHP on the person row is what counts conditions. 'Any other long-term health condition' is excluded, so a household whose only illness falls outside the ten named conditions is coded 0 rather than missing.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition, the ten conditions in scope, the exclusion of other conditions and the full code list including the partial and complete not stated codes.
evidence_quote: This variable counts the number of adults aged 15 years and over in a household who reported they had at least one of the selected long-term health conditions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Count of adults (15 years and over) with selected long-term health condition(s) in household', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so it never listed the ten conditions or explained the separate partial and complete not stated codes.

value_domain: Census count of children with a selected long-term health condition in the household
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of children with selected long-term health condition(s) in household (CCLTHD)
variable_description: How many children under 15 in the household reported at least one of the ten selected long-term health conditions. The ABS says it "counts the number of children under 15 years in a household who reported they had at least one of the selected long-term health conditions" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). It is the under-15 companion to CALTHD, and both are new to the 2021 dwelling table.
value_definition: A single digit: 0 to 4 for no children through four children, 5 for five or more, and 6 where some children in the household had a not stated condition. '&' means all children in the household not stated, and '@' is not applicable.
limitation: A child's conditions are reported by whoever filled in the household form, not by the child, so this is a household member's account rather than a clinical record. The list is the same ten adult conditions, which suits childhood asthma but omits the developmental, congenital and behavioural conditions that dominate childhood illness, so a zero is weak evidence that no child in the household is unwell.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition, the ten conditions and the full code list including the partial and complete not stated codes.
evidence_quote: This variable counts the number of children under 15 years in a household who reported they had at least one of the selected long-term health conditions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Count of children with selected long-term health condition(s) in household', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so it never listed the ten conditions or noted that the answers come from the household form rather than from the child.

value_domain: Census count of dependent children under 15 temporarily absent from the family
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of dependent children under 15 in family temporarily absent (CDCAF)
variable_description: How many of the family's dependent children under 15 were away from home on Census night but still counted as part of the family. The ABS says it "counts the number of dependent children aged under 15 years that were reported as temporarily absent from the family" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). The answer comes from the persons temporarily absent question on the household form, and those same children are already included in the family totals CDCF, CDCUF and CACF.
value_definition: Codes 0 to 3, since at most three people can be reported as temporarily absent from a dwelling, plus '@' not applicable for families with no children under 15 and for non-family, unoccupied and non-private dwellings.
limitation: The cap is three people per dwelling and it is shared with CDSAF and CNDAF, so a family with several members away on Census night has its absences truncated and the family counts understated. A temporarily absent child has no person record in the Census, so nothing but the count exists - their age, sex and other characteristics are unavailable.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition, the 0 to 3 code range and what the not applicable category covers.
evidence_quote: This variable counts the number of dependent children aged under 15 years that were reported as temporarily absent from the family.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Count of Dependent Children Under 15 Temporarily Absent', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so nothing said that the count caps at three or that absent children have no person record.

value_domain: Census count of dependent children in a family, by family type
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of dependent children in family (CDCF)
variable_description: How many dependent children the family has, with the family type built into the same code. The ABS says it "counts the number of dependent children in the family. A dependent child is a person who is either a child under 15 years of age, or a dependent student aged 15-24 years" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). It is the sum of the under-15 count in CDCUF and the dependent student count in CDSF, and it includes up to three dependent children temporarily absent on Census night.
value_definition: A two-digit code carrying two facts at once: 00 to 06 are couple families with none through six or more dependent children, 07 to 13 are one parent families over the same range, and '@@' is not applicable.
limitation: Because family type is embedded in the code, reading it as a plain number is wrong - a one parent family with no dependent children takes the value 07, not 0. Dependency here is set by age and student status rather than by financial support, so a 26-year-old still supported at home is not a dependent child while a 24-year-old full-time student is.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition of a dependent child, the split of the code range between couple and one parent families, and the treatment of temporarily absent children.
evidence_quote: This variable counts the number of dependent children in the family. A dependent child is a person who is either a child under 15 years of age, or a dependent student aged 15-24 years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Count of Dependent Children in Family', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so nothing warned that the code encodes family type as well as a count.

value_domain: Census count of dependent children under 15 in a family, by family type
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of dependent children under 15 in family (CDCUF)
variable_description: How many dependent children aged under 15 the family has, with couple and one parent families coded on separate ranges. The ABS says it "counts the number of dependent children aged under 15 years in a family" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). It is the under-15 part of CDCF; the 15 to 24 year old dependent students are counted separately in CDSF.
value_definition: Two digits: 00 to 06 for couple families with no children under 15 through six or more, 07 to 13 for one parent families over the same range, and '@@' not applicable.
limitation: A family whose only dependants are students aged 15 to 24 is coded as having none here even though CDCF and CDSF both show them, so this column alone will misclassify families with older teenagers as childless. Reading the code as a count fails again at the family-type break at 07.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition and the full two-part code list.
evidence_quote: This variable counts the number of dependent children aged under 15 years in a family.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Count of dependent children under 15 in family', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so nothing said that couple and one parent families use different code ranges.

value_domain: 2011 Census Community Development Employment Projects participation
value_source: ABS, Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Community Development Employment Projects (CDEP)
variable_description: Whether the person was taking part in the Community Development Employment Projects scheme, the remote Indigenous employment programme that was reformed into the Remote Jobs and Communities Program and then replaced by the Community Development Program from 1 July 2015. The ABS says "participation in CDEP is asked as a separate question only on the Interviewer household form. CDEP participation is not applicable to people enumerated on mainstream forms" (Census Dictionary 2011). It appears on the 2011 person table only; CDPP on the 2021 person table asks the parallel question about the successor Community Development Program.
value_definition: A short categorical flag separating participants from non-participants, with a not applicable code for everyone counted on a mainstream Census form and a not stated code for interviewer-form respondents who did not answer.
limitation: A not applicable value records which form the person filled in, not that they were outside the scheme, so this column cannot count CDEP participants nationally - only those enumerated in discrete Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities. In 2011 CDEP participants were also counted as employed in LFSP, so the two columns describe the same people differently from how the 2021 Census treats CDP.
rationale: The 2011 Census Dictionary chapter for CDEP describes the programme, states that the question is asked only on the interviewer household form, and records that participants are included in the employed category of LFSP. The exact code labels are not published on that page, so the value definition is described in prose rather than enumerated.
evidence_quote: Participation in CDEP is asked as a separate question only on the Interviewer household form. CDEP participation is not applicable to people enumerated on mainstream forms.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Community Development Employment Projects Participation', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so nothing said the question was asked only in discrete communities or that it has no 2016 or 2021 counterpart of the same name.

value_domain: Census Community Development Program participation
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Community Development Program participation (CDPP)
variable_description: Whether the person was taking part in the Community Development Program, the remote employment and community activity programme that replaced CDEP. The ABS says it "indicates whether a person participated in the Community Development Program (CDP)" and gives the scope as "all persons aged 15 years and over who responded on an Interviewer household form" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). It is on the 2021 person table only, and CDEP on the 2011 person table is the earlier question about the earlier scheme.
value_definition: Codes 1 participant in the Community Development Program and 2 not a participant, plus '&' not stated, '@' not applicable and 'V' overseas visitor.
limitation: Not applicable is almost everyone, because the question appears only on the interviewer household form used in discrete Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities, so a CDP participant counted on a mainstream form is invisible here rather than coded 2. CDP participants receive income support rather than wages and are not counted as employed in LFSP unless they also hold a non-CDP job, so this column and labour force status disagree by design.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition, the scope restricted to the interviewer household form, the five codes and the labour force treatment of participants.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates whether a person participated in the Community Development Program (CDP).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Community development program participation', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so nothing said that the question is asked only on the interviewer form or that participants are not counted as employed.

value_domain: Census count of dependent students aged 15-24 temporarily absent from the family
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of dependent students (15-24 years) in family temporarily absent (CDSAF)
variable_description: How many of the family's dependent students aged 15 to 24 were away from home on Census night but still counted in the family. The ABS says it "counts the number of dependent students aged 15-24 years that were reported as temporarily absent in a family" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). These students are already included in CDSF and CDCF, so this column identifies the part of those totals that was reported rather than enumerated.
value_definition: Codes 0 to 3, capped by the three-person limit on temporarily absent reporting per dwelling, plus '@' not applicable for families with no dependent students and for non-family, unoccupied and non-private dwellings.
limitation: A student who has moved away for university is not temporarily absent: they are usually resident somewhere else and form part of another household, so this column catches short absences only and is not a measure of students living away to study. Nothing but the count is available for an absent student - there is no person record with their age, sex or field of study.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition, the 0 to 3 code range and the not applicable category.
evidence_quote: This variable counts the number of dependent students aged 15-24 years that were reported as temporarily absent in a family.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Count of Dependent Students (15-24 years) Temporarily Absent', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so nothing said the count caps at three or that students living away to study are excluded.

value_domain: Census count of dependent students aged 15-24 in a family, by family type
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of dependent students (15-24 years) in family (CDSF)
variable_description: How many dependent students aged 15 to 24 the family has, coded separately for couple and one parent families. The ABS says it "counts the number of dependent students aged 15-24 years in a family. It includes up to three dependent students aged 15-24 years who were temporarily absent from the household on Census Night" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). With CDCUF for the under-15s it makes up the dependent child total in CDCF.
value_definition: Two digits: 00 to 06 for couple families with no dependent students through six or more, 07 to 13 for one parent families over the same range, and '@@' not applicable. A person counts only if aged 15 to 24, attending an educational institution, and coded in the household relationship as a natural or adopted dependent student, a student step child or a student foster child.
limitation: Study is what makes a 15 to 24 year old dependent here, so a young person who works instead of studying is a non-dependent child in CNDCF rather than a zero in this column, and a family can move between the two counts without anyone moving house. The column is on the 2021 family table only, so the same split cannot be made for 2011 or 2016.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition, the code structure split between couple and one parent families, and the relationship categories a person must hold to be counted.
evidence_quote: This variable counts the number of dependent students aged 15-24 years in a family. It includes up to three dependent students aged 15-24 years who were temporarily absent from the household on Census Night.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Count of dependent students (15-24 years) in family', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so nothing said what makes a student dependent or that the code encodes family type.

value_domain: ASGS Commonwealth Electoral Division code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Non ABS Structures, Commonwealth Electoral Divisions
variable_description: The federal electorate the dwelling sits in, coded from where the dwelling was enumerated. The ABS builds these as "an ABS Mesh Block approximation of Australian Electoral Commission (AEC) federal electoral divisions" (ASGS Edition 3), so the boundary is fitted to Mesh Blocks rather than taken from the AEC directly. It sits with SEDD and SED22D for state electorates and with LGAD, POAD and SALD on the same dwelling row.
value_definition: A three-digit ASGS Non ABS Structure code: one digit for the state or territory and two for the division, assigned alphabetically within each state and territory. In ASGS Edition 3 there were 169 Commonwealth Electoral Divisions covering the whole of Australia without gaps or overlaps, a count that includes 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: It is an approximation, not the electoral roll boundary, so dwellings near a division edge can be placed in the neighbouring division and a Census count for a division will not match the AEC's enrolment figure. Divisions are also redistributed between elections, so a code only means something against the ASGS vintage it was assigned on.
rationale: The '(en)' suffix and the dwelling table identify this as the enumeration-based ASGS coding of the dwelling; the ASGS Edition 3 Non ABS Structures page defines Commonwealth Electoral Divisions, their count and their code structure.
evidence_quote: There are 169 Commonwealth Electoral Divisions covering the whole of Australia without gaps or overlaps.
supersedes_rationale: The value domain read 'not specified' and 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' stood as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said the codes come from the ASGS or that they approximate rather than reproduce the AEC boundary.

value_domain: ASGS Commonwealth Electoral Division code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Non ABS Structures, Commonwealth Electoral Divisions
variable_description: The federal electorate containing the person's usual address, not the one where they happened to be counted. The ABS builds the divisions as "an ABS Mesh Block approximation of Australian Electoral Commission (AEC) federal electoral divisions" (ASGS Edition 3). Because it is coded from place of usual residence, it can differ from CEDD on the dwelling record a person was enumerated in, and it is the column to use for describing an electorate's resident population.
value_definition: A three-digit ASGS Non ABS Structure code, one digit for state or territory and two for the division, over the 169 divisions that cover Australia in ASGS Edition 3, a count that includes 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: The people counted in a division are not its voters: children, non-citizens and adults who are not enrolled are all included, so a Census population is a poor proxy for enrolment or for turnout. Because the code follows the ASGS vintage, comparing an electorate's Census population across 2016 and 2021 compares two different boundaries wherever a redistribution has occurred.
rationale: The '(ur)' suffix and the person table identify this as the usual-residence coding of the ASGS Commonwealth Electoral Division, which the ASGS Edition 3 page defines along with its count and code structure.
evidence_quote: ABS Commonwealth Electoral Divisions are based on the AEC electoral division boundaries available prior to publication.
supersedes_rationale: The value domain read 'not specified' and the same generic sentence stood as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said this is coded from usual residence rather than from where the person was counted.

value_domain: Census unpaid child care in the two weeks before Census night
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Unpaid child care (CHCAREP)
variable_description: Whether the person looked after a child under 15 without pay in the two weeks before Census night, and whether that child was their own. The ABS says it "records people who, in the two weeks prior to Census Night, spent time caring for a child or children aged under 15 years without pay" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). It covers care of a person's own children whether or not they live together, and of grandchildren, relatives' children and friends' or neighbours' children, but not organised care through an institution or club. It is on the 2011, 2016 and 2021 person tables, alongside UNCAREP for unpaid care of a person with a disability.
value_definition: Codes 1 did not provide child care, 2 cared for own child or children, 3 cared for other child or children, and 4 cared for both, plus '&' not stated, '@' not applicable and 'V' overseas visitor. Scope is persons aged 15 years and over.
limitation: It records that care happened, not how much: an hour of babysitting and full-time sole care of three children are the same code, so it cannot measure caring load or be converted into hours. The child cared for need not live with the carer, so a code of 2 is not evidence of a resident child, and a two-week reference period will miss a parent who was away or unwell in that fortnight.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition, the reference period, the scope, the four substantive categories and the inclusions and exclusions.
evidence_quote: This variable records people who, in the two weeks prior to Census Night, spent time caring for a child or children aged under 15 years without pay.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Unpaid Child Care', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so nothing said the reference period is two weeks or that own and other children are separated.

value_domain: Census Australian citizenship indicator
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Australian citizenship (CITP)
variable_description: Whether the person says they are an Australian citizen. The ABS says the variable "records whether a person has Australian citizenship" and that the data "is used to understand the tendency of different migrant groups to take up citizenship and to measure the size of the groups eligible to vote" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). It is asked of everyone and is on the 2011, 2016 and 2021 person tables, so with BPLP and YARP it supports a take-up-of-citizenship analysis across three Censuses.
value_definition: Codes 1 Australian citizen and 2 not an Australian citizen, plus '&' not stated and 'V' overseas visitor.
limitation: It is self-reported and not checked against the citizenship register, and it says nothing about what a non-citizen holds instead: permanent residence, a temporary visa and no visa at all share the single code 2. Citizenship is also not voting eligibility, since age and enrolment decide that as well.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition, its stated purpose and the four categories.
evidence_quote: This variable records whether a person has Australian citizenship.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Australian Citizenship', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so nothing said that non-citizens are a single undifferentiated category.

value_domain: Census count of selected long-term health conditions
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of selected long-term health conditions (CLTHP)
variable_description: How many of the ten selected long-term health conditions the person reported, capped at three or more. The ABS says it "describes the number of selected long-term health conditions a person has reported" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). It is derived from the individual condition flags HARTP, HASTP, HCANP, HDEMP, HDIAP, HHEDP, HKIDP, HLUNP, HMHCP and HSTRP on the same person row, and it is the person-level counterpart to the household counts CALTHD, CCLTHD and CPLTHD.
value_definition: Codes 0 none of the selected conditions, 1 one, 2 two and 3 three or more, plus '&' not stated and 'V' overseas visitor. The ten conditions are arthritis, asthma, cancer including remission, dementia including Alzheimer's, diabetes excluding gestational diabetes, heart disease including heart attack or angina, kidney disease, lung condition including COPD or emphysema, mental health condition including depression or anxiety, and stroke.
limitation: 'Any other long-term health condition' is excluded from the count, so a person whose only illness falls outside the ten is coded 0 while HOLHP on the same row says they have a condition. The top code is open at three, so multimorbidity beyond three conditions cannot be measured, and every answer is a self-report on a checklist rather than a diagnosis.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition, the four counts, the ten conditions in scope and the exclusion of other conditions.
evidence_quote: This variable describes the number of selected long-term health conditions a person has reported.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Count of selected long-term health conditions', with the domain given as 'finite source-defined values', so nothing said which conditions are counted, that the top code is open at three, or that other conditions are excluded.

value_domain: Census count of non-dependent children temporarily absent from the family
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of non-dependent children in family temporarily absent (CNDAF)
variable_description: How many of the family's non-dependent children were away from home on Census night but still counted as part of the family. The ABS says it "counts the number of non-dependent children reported as temporarily absent from the family on Census Night. A maximum of three people can be reported and coded as temporarily absent from the dwelling" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). These people are adult children still usually resident with a parent, and they are already included in CNDCF and CACF.
value_definition: Codes 0 to 3, plus '@' not applicable, which covers families with no non-dependent children as well as non-family households, unoccupied private dwellings and non-private dwellings.
limitation: The three-person cap applies to the dwelling as a whole, so this count competes with CDCAF and CDSAF rather than adding to them, and a dwelling with several members away has its absences truncated. An adult child who has actually moved out is not temporarily absent: they form their own household and never appear in this column.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 publishes a page for this variable giving the definition, the definition of a non-dependent child, the 0 to 3 code range and the not applicable category.
evidence_quote: This variable counts the number of non-dependent children reported as temporarily absent from the family on Census Night. A maximum of three people can be reported and coded as temporarily absent from the dwelling.

variable_description: Whether this private dwelling stands inside a large communal setting such as a caravan park, a marina, a manufactured home estate or a self-contained retirement village. ABS defines it as describing "the location of dwellings" and classifying them "into large communal locations, such as caravan parks and marinas". Unlike almost every other Census column it is not answered by the household: it comes from the ABS Address Register and is confirmed by field officers during collection. It sits beside STRD, dwelling structure, which describes the dwelling itself rather than the site it stands on, and appears in the 2011, 2016 and 2021 dwelling tables.
value_definition: A single character: 1 caravan, residential park or camping ground, 2 marina, 3 manufactured home estate, 4 self-contained retirement village, 5 other, @ not applicable to non-private dwellings and migratory, off-shore and shipping areas.
limitation: Code 5 is not a clean residual. It is both a genuine category and the fallback ABS assigns when the location cannot be determined, so a count of code 5 is not a count of ordinary suburban dwellings. Retirement living is also split across two columns: a self-contained unit is code 4 here, while a hostel-style aged care facility is a non-private dwelling and coded @.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 page for DLOD gives the definition, the five-value code list, the Address Register provenance and the rule that undetermined locations default to 'Other'.
evidence_quote: This variable describes the location of dwellings. It classifies them into large communal locations, such as caravan parks and marinas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Dwelling Location' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it did not say the column is about communal sites rather than geography, nor that it comes from the Address Register.

value_domain: Calendar month of birth (1 to 12)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age (AGEP)
variable_description: The month of the year in which the person was born, as reported on the 2011 or 2016 Census form. The Census collects a date of birth rather than an age directly, and ABS states that "Age is calculated from date of birth when provided, otherwise stated age is used"; the PLIDA Census tables keep the month and year components as DOBMP and DOBYP so a record carries a birth date that can be used for linking and for age at a date other than Census night. It sits beside AGEP, which is the ABS-derived age in completed years at Census night, and IFAGEP, which flags where age was imputed. The column is present in the 2011 and 2016 person tables only.
value_definition: A month number from 1 to 12, held as a component of a date rather than as a classification with meaning of its own.
limitation: It is not a date of birth. No day of the month is carried, so an exact age cannot be computed and two people born in the same month cannot be ordered, which matters for any eligibility rule with a birthday cutoff. Where age was imputed rather than reported, the birth month cannot be a value the person supplied; ABS puts the age non-response rate at 5.6% in 2016, and IFAGEP on the same row marks those records.
rationale: No Census Dictionary variable page exists for DOBMP, because it is not a published Census output variable; it is the month component of the date of birth response that ABS uses to derive AGEP, and the AGEP page is the authority on how that response is collected, used and imputed.
evidence_quote: Age is calculated from date of birth when provided, otherwise stated age is used.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Month of birth' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, and did not connect the column to the Census date of birth question, to AGEP or to the imputation flag beside it.

value_domain: Four-digit year of birth
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age (AGEP)
variable_description: The year in which the person was born, as reported on the 2011 or 2016 Census form. It is the year component of the date of birth the Census collects to derive age: ABS states that "Age is calculated from date of birth when provided, otherwise stated age is used", and that where both a date of birth and a stated age are given, the date of birth wins unless it is identified as wrong. With DOBMP on the same row it gives a birth month and year that can be used for linking or for age at a reference date other than Census night. The column is present in the 2011 and 2016 person tables only.
value_definition: A four-digit calendar year. The range is open at the older end and bounded by the Census year at the younger end.
limitation: Subtracting this year from the Census year does not give the person's age. A person born in December 2000 was 15 on 2016 Census night, 9 August, not 16, so AGEP is the ABS measure of age and this column will disagree with it for roughly the second half of each birth year. It also carries no day of the month, so it cannot serve as a complete date of birth for exact-match linking.
rationale: No Census Dictionary variable page exists for DOBYP, because it is not a published Census output variable; it is the year component of the date of birth response the AGEP page documents, and that page states the precedence of date of birth over stated age.
evidence_quote: Where both sets of information are provided, date of birth is used to derive an age in years, except in circumstances where errors in the date of birth are identified.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Year of birth' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never warned that a year-difference calculation overstates age for people whose birthday falls after Census night.

value_domain: Banded hours of unpaid domestic work in the previous week
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Unpaid domestic work: number of hours (DOMP)
variable_description: How much unpaid housework the person did in the week before Census night, reported in bands. ABS defines it as recording "the number of hours people spent in the previous week doing domestic work without pay", answered by ticking one of five boxes rather than writing a number. It is one of three unpaid work columns on the person row: CHCAREP covers unpaid child care and UNCAREP covers unpaid care for a person with a disability or an older person, and a person can report all three. The column appears in the 2011, 2016 and 2021 person tables and applies to persons aged 15 and over.
value_definition: A single character: 1 nil hours, 2 less than 5 hours, 3 five to 14 hours, 4 fifteen to 29 hours, 5 thirty hours or more, & not stated, @ not applicable, V overseas visitor.
limitation: The bands are wide and open at the top, so a person doing 30 hours and a person doing 70 hours are the same value and no mean can be computed without assuming a midpoint.
