The reference week is the week before Census night, so illness, holidays or shift patterns in that one week carry straight into the answer; ABS reports a 6.6% non-response rate in 2021, down from 8.8% in 2016.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 page for DOMP gives the definition, the five-band code list, the applicable population and the non-response rates for 2021 and 2016.
evidence_quote: This variable records the number of hours people spent in the previous week doing domestic work without pay.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so a reader would reasonably have expected an hours count rather than five bands.

value_domain: Census dwelling record identifier
value_source: ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Census of Population and Housing
variable_description: The dwelling a Census record belongs to, used to attach a person or a family to the household they were counted in. In the 2021 tables it appears on the person, family and dwelling rows, so it is the key that carries tenure, dwelling structure and household income onto a person; in 2011 and 2016 it appears on the dwelling row only. ABS builds its Census microdata the same way, releasing dwelling, family and person records with identifiers "available across levels: ABSFID and the related ABSHID on each family record; ABSPID and the related ABSFID and ABSHID on each person record". In fplida the values are synthetic and are minted separately for each Census year.
value_definition: An arbitrary record key. The digits carry no information about the dwelling, its address or its geography, and there is no finite list to publish.
limitation: It is not stable across Census years. A dwelling enumerated in 2016 and again in 2021 carries two unrelated identifiers, so the column cannot follow an address or a household over time; the Address Register identifier ARID, carried on the PLIDA Core address tables with start and end dates, is the key that does that. It also identifies the dwelling and not the household, so it gives no signal when the occupants change.
rationale: No ABS page names the PLIDA column DWELLING_ID, so the mapping is an inference from the registry's own table layout, where the identifier appears on the dwelling, family and person tables. The ABS Census microdata page is the published authority on the three-level record structure and on what the dwelling identifier is for.
evidence_quote: To enable users to link records, the following identifiers are available across levels: ABSFID and the related ABSHID on each family record; ABSPID and the related ABSFID and ABSHID on each person record.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Dwelling ID' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said what the key joins to or warned that it does not persist between Censuses.

value_domain: Census dwelling type classification
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Dwelling type (DWTD)
variable_description: Whether this dwelling is an occupied private dwelling, an unoccupied private dwelling, a non-private dwelling or a migratory, off-shore or shipping record. ABS defines the variable as classifying dwellings into "Private dwellings (occupied and unoccupied), Non-private dwellings, Migratory, off-shore and shipping areas". It is sourced from the ABS Address Register or set by field staff during enumeration, and it is the column that decides which other dwelling variables apply: income, tenure and family columns are coded @ for anything that is not an occupied private dwelling. The column appears in the 2011, 2016 and 2021 dwelling tables.
value_definition: A single digit: 1 occupied private dwelling, 2 unoccupied private dwelling, 3 non-private dwelling, 4 migratory, 5 off-shore, 6 shipping.
limitation: Code 3 does not say what kind of non-private dwelling it is; NPDD carries hotel, hospital, prison, aged care and the rest. "Unoccupied" is partly a modelled outcome rather than an observation, because where contact could not be made ABS settles occupancy with the Census Occupancy Model, and ABS reports that a small number of people were wrongly coded to migratory, off-shore or shipping in 2021.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 page for DWTD gives the definition, the six-value code list, the Address Register and field enumeration provenance, the role of the Census Occupancy Model, and the 2021 migratory coding error.
evidence_quote: This variable classifies dwellings into the following types: Private dwellings (occupied and unoccupied), Non-private dwellings, Migratory, off-shore and shipping areas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Dwelling Type' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not distinguish this column from dwelling structure (STRD) or from type of non-private dwelling (NPDD).

value_domain: Census engagement in employment, education and training classification
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Engagement in employment, education and training (EETP)
variable_description: Whether the person was working, studying, doing both or doing neither, on a four-level engagement scale. ABS defines it as indicating "whether a person is engaged or not engaged in work and/or study", and derives it by crossing three columns that also sit on the person row: labour force status and hours worked not stated (LFHRP), full-time or part-time student status (STUP) and age (AGEP). Full engagement means full-time work, full-time study, or a part-time combination of both; partial engagement means only one of the two, part-time. The column appears in the 2016 and 2021 person tables and applies to persons aged 15 and over.
value_definition: A hierarchical code with seven one-digit values and twelve two-digit values beneath them: 1 fully engaged (11 to 15), 2 partially engaged (21 to 22), 3 at least partially engaged (31), 4 not engaged (41), plus & not stated and @ not applicable.
limitation: Code 3, at least partially engaged, is a residual for records with too little information rather than a middle rung on the scale, so treating the codes as ordered puts unclassifiable people between the partially and the not engaged. Study means enrolment at an educational institution, so a person doing unaccredited training, unpaid care or job search only is coded not engaged.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 page for EETP gives the definition, the hierarchical code structure, the three source variables and the meaning of each engagement level.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates whether a person is engaged or not engaged in work and/or study.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Engagement in Employment Education and Training' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never revealed that code 3 is an information-shortfall category.

value_domain: Binary employment flag for national reporting
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Employment flag (EMFP)
variable_description: A two-way split of the person into employed against everyone else, built for national reporting. ABS defines it as flagging "whether a person is employed or unemployed/not in the labour force", collapsing the full-time, part-time and away-from-work categories of labour force status (LFSP) into code 1 and the rest into code 2. It sits in the national reporting group of 2021 Census variables alongside UEFP, the unemployment flag, and LFFP, the labour force participation flag. It appears in the 2021 person table only and applies to persons aged 15 and over.
value_definition: A single character: 1 employed, 2 unemployed or not in the labour force, @ not applicable, V overseas visitor.
limitation: Code 2 merges unemployed people with people outside the labour force, so no unemployment rate can be built from this column alone; UEFP and LFSP make that distinction. ABS says the variable was designed for national reporting and that other uses need care, and that the @ and V codes should be excluded from national reporting extracts. Its quality follows LFSP, which had a 5.8% non-response rate in 2021.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 page for EMFP gives the definition, the code list, the derivation from LFSP, the caution about non-reporting uses and the underlying non-response rate.
evidence_quote: This variable flags whether a person is employed or unemployed/not in the labour force.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Employment flag' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not warn that the non-employed category mixes unemployment with non-participation.

value_domain: Banded count of employees of an owner manager's business
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of employees (EMPP)
variable_description: How many people the person's own business employs, asked only of owner managers. ABS defines it as recording "the number of employees (in ranges) employed by owner managers (excluding the owner managers themselves)", so the respondent is not counted in their own figure. It applies to persons aged 15 and over who are owner managers of an incorporated or unincorporated enterprise, which makes status in employment (SIEMP in 2016 and 2021, EMTP in 2011) the column that decides who is in scope. The column appears in the 2011, 2016 and 2021 person tables.
value_definition: A single character: 1 nil employees, 2 one to 19 employees, 3 twenty or more employees, & not stated, @ not applicable, V overseas visitor.
limitation: It is not the size of the person's workplace. An employee at a firm of 500 is coded @, so a size distribution built from this column describes small business owners rather than jobs, and the top band cannot separate a 25-person business from a 2,000-person one. The 0.4% non-response rate in 2021 is low precisely because the column applies to so few people, not because the measure is precise.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 page for EMPP gives the definition, the three bands, the exclusion of the owner manager from the count, the applicable population and the 2021 and 2016 non-response rates.
evidence_quote: This variable records the number of employees (in ranges) employed by owner managers (excluding the owner managers themselves).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Number of Employees' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, which invited the reading that it describes every employed person's workplace size.

value_domain: Census employment type classification (employee, owner manager, contributing family worker)
value_source: ABS, 2011 Census of Population and Housing, Employment Type (EMTP) data quality statement
variable_description: Whether the person worked as an employee, ran their own business, or worked unpaid in a family business, in the 2011 Census. ABS defines the variable as classifying "all employed people to either employees, owner-managers of incorporated enterprises, owner-managers of unincorporated enterprises, or contributing family workers, on the basis of their main job". It applies only to people whose labour force status is employed, and it sits with GNGP, which splits employees between the public and private sectors, and EMPP, which counts an owner manager's employees. The column appears in the 2011 person table only; from 2016 the same concept is carried by status in employment (SIEMP).
value_definition: A four-category classification of employed persons: employee, owner manager of an incorporated enterprise, owner manager of an unincorporated enterprise, contributing family worker, with not-stated and not-applicable codes.
limitation: It describes the main job only, so a person who is an employee by day and runs a business at night appears once and their second role is invisible. It says nothing about permanency, casual status or hours, which are in HRSP, and because the mnemonic stops after 2011, any series across Census years has to switch to SIEMP rather than treat the two as the same column.
rationale: The ABS data quality statement for the 2011 Census variable EMTP gives the definition, the four categories, the applicable population and the 0.9% non-response rate, and the ABS microdata documentation records that status in employment replaced it from 2016.
evidence_quote: This variable classifies all employed people to either employees, owner-managers of incorporated enterprises, owner-managers of unincorporated enterprises, or contributing family workers, on the basis of their main job.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Employment Type' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it neither listed the four categories nor said the column is 2011-only and is continued by SIEMP.

value_domain: Census proficiency in spoken English classification
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Proficiency in spoken English (ENGLP)
variable_description: How well the person says they speak English, on a scale that also carries whether they use only English at home. ABS defines the 2021 version as classifying "a person's self-assessed proficiency in spoken English where they have identified they use a main language other than English at home", while the 2011 and 2016 version, then titled Proficiency in Spoken English/Language, was "applicable to all persons". It is built from two form questions, the language used at home question that feeds LANP and the follow-up proficiency question, so code 1 answers the first question and codes 2 to 5 answer the second. The column appears in the 2011, 2016 and 2021 person tables.
value_definition: A single character: 1 speaks English only, 2 to 5 uses another language and speaks English very well, well, not well or not at all, 6 neither language nor proficiency stated, & language stated but proficiency not stated, V overseas visitor.
limitation: It is a self-rating of speaking, not a test and not a measure of literacy: a person who rates themselves "very well" may still read English poorly or need an interpreter in a clinical setting. Code 1 is a language answer rather than a rung on the proficiency scale, so treating the column as an ordinal scale across all persons mixes two different questions into one ranking.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 page for ENGLP gives the definition, the full code list, the two-question derivation and the 5.5% non-response rate, and the 2016 Census Dictionary entry gives the earlier, wider scope statement for the same mnemonic.
evidence_quote: This variable classifies a person's self-assessed proficiency in spoken English where they have identified they use a main language other than English at home.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Proficiency in Spoken English/Language' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it gave no scale, and it hid that code 1 records English-only speakers rather than a proficiency level.

value_domain: Census proficiency in spoken English classification, restricted to speakers of a language other than English
value_source: ABS, Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, ENGP Proficiency in Spoken English
variable_description: How well the person says they speak English, asked only of people who reported using a language other than English at home. ABS defines it as classifying "a persons self assessed proficiency in spoken English", and says it is applicable to people who gave a language other than English in the language spoken at home question, or who did not state a language at all. It is the narrower twin of ENGLP on the same person row: ENGLP covers everyone and puts English-only speakers in its own category, whereas ENGP leaves them out entirely. The column appears in the 2011 and 2016 person tables only, and ABS removed it from the 2021 Census.
value_definition: A four-level self-rating of spoken English, from very well to not at all, with not-stated and not-applicable codes. English-only speakers are outside the applicable population rather than being a value.
limitation: Its denominator is not the population. A proficiency share computed on ENGP is a share of people who use another language at home, whereas the same share on ENGLP is a share of everyone, and mixing the two was common enough that ABS dropped ENGP after 2016. People who did not state a language also fall inside its scope, so the base is not a clean count of other-language speakers either.
rationale: The ABS 2016 Census variable entry for ENGP gives the definition, the applicable population that separates it from ENGLP, and the 1.1% non-response rate for 2016; the 2021 ENGLP page records that ENGP was removed for 2021.
evidence_quote: This variable classifies a persons self assessed proficiency in spoken English.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Proficiency in Spoken English' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing on the page distinguished it from ENGLP, which is the exact confusion ABS retired the variable to avoid.

value_domain: Census family record identifier
value_source: ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Census of Population and Housing
variable_description: The family a Census record belongs to, used to attach a person to the family row describing their family type and family income. It is on the family rows in 2011, 2016 and 2021 and on the 2021 person row, so it is the key that brings FMCF, FINF and HCFMF onto a person. ABS releases its own Census microdata with the same three-level design, where identifiers are "available across levels: ABSFID and the related ABSHID on each family record; ABSPID and the related ABSFID and ABSHID on each person record". A household holds at most three families, and FNOF says whether a family row is the primary, second or third; this column says which particular family it is. In fplida the values are synthetic.
value_definition: An arbitrary record key. It carries no information about the family's size, type or composition, and there is no finite list to publish.
limitation: Not everyone has one. Unrelated persons living in a family household, and everyone in a group or lone person household, have no family row at all, so a join on this key silently drops them rather than returning a zero or a null family. It is also minted per Census year, so a family present in both 2016 and 2021 carries two unrelated values.
rationale: No ABS page names the PLIDA column FAMILY_ID, so the mapping is an inference from the registry's own layout, where the identifier appears on the family tables in all three years and on the 2021 person table. The ABS Census microdata page is the published authority on the family record level and on what a family identifier links.
evidence_quote: To enable users to link records, the following identifiers are available across levels: ABSFID and the related ABSHID on each family record; ABSPID and the related ABSFID and ABSHID on each person record.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Family ID' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say which rows can be joined on it or warn that people outside a family have no value.

value_domain: Census family blending classification (intact, step, blended)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Family blending (FBLF)
variable_description: Whether a couple family with children is intact, a step family or a blended family, and whether other children are also present. ABS defines it as classifying "couple families with children living in private dwellings, based on the parent-child relationships within them", using the relationship and persons temporarily absent responses. It refines FMCF on the same family row: FMCF says the family is a couple family with children, and this column says how the children are related to the two parents. The column appears in the 2011, 2016 and 2021 family tables.
value_definition: A single character across eight values: 1 to 3 intact, step and blended families with no other children present, 4 to 6 the same three with other children present, 7 other couple family with other children only, @ not applicable.
limitation: Only couple families with children are in scope, so a one-parent step family is coded @ and cannot be found here at all. ABS also found that step children were overcounted in the 2021 Census in Western Australia, New South Wales, Queensland, the Northern Territory and Other Territories, and partly in Victoria, where a spouse was temporarily absent, which shifts families from intact into the step and blended categories.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 page for FBLF gives the definition, the eight-value code list, the derivation from the relationship and temporary absence questions, and the states affected by the 2021 step child overcount.
evidence_quote: This variable classifies couple families with children living in private dwellings, based on the parent-child relationships within them.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Family Blending' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it defined nothing and did not flag the known 2021 step child error that bears directly on this column.

value_domain: Census family income derivation quality indicator
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Family income derivation indicator (FIDF)
variable_description: Why a family's income total may be incomplete, flagging temporary absence, unstated income and negative income. ABS defines it as identifying "families where one or more family members were temporarily absent, did not state their income or stated a negative income", built from family composition (FMCF), total personal income (INCP) and the counts of absent persons and dependent children. It is the quality companion to FINF and FINASF on the same family row, and it is the column to check before using either as a family income measure. It appears in the 2011, 2016 and 2021 family tables.
value_definition: Nine categories crossing three conditions: whether members aged 15 and over were temporarily absent, whether incomes were stated, and whether any negative income was reported. Codes 1 to 8 cover applicable families and @ marks not applicable households.
limitation: It is a warning, not a correction: it says a family income figure may be understated and why, but not by how much, so it cannot be used to adjust FINF or FINASF. A family flagged for temporary absence can also have a complete set of stated incomes for everyone who was present, so a flag here is not evidence that anyone failed to answer.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 page for FIDF gives the definition, the structure of the nine categories, the source variables and the caution about family definitions differing across collections.
evidence_quote: This variable identifies families where one or more family members were temporarily absent, did not state their income or stated a negative income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Family Income Derivation Indicator' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell that it flags three separate problems at once or which income columns it qualifies.

value_domain: Banded weekly total family income, as stated
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total family income as stated (weekly) (FINASF)
variable_description: The family's weekly income band, computed from whichever members actually stated an income. ABS defines the variable as recording "the total family income by summing the Total personal income (weekly) (INCP) of each family member aged 15 years and over present in the household on Census Night". It differs from FINF on the same family row in what it does with partial non-response: FINASF still bands a family whose members did not all answer, using the incomes that were given, whereas FINF sets that family aside in its own "partial income stated" category. It appears in the 2011, 2016 and 2021 family tables.
value_definition: A two-digit band: 22 codes running from 01, negative income, to 22, $8,000 or more per week, plus && where no member aged 15 and over stated an income and @@ not applicable.
limitation: It cannot be read as a dollar figure. The Census collects personal income in ranges, so each member is first assigned the median of their range from the Survey of Income and Housing and those medians are summed, which makes the total a modelled band rather than a measurement. Members under 15 and members who were temporarily absent contribute nothing, so a family whose earner was away on Census night can be banded far too low.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 page for FINASF gives the definition, the 22-band code list, the Survey of Income and Housing median imputation step, and the rule for families where no income was stated; the FINF page supplies the contrasting partial-response code.
evidence_quote: This variable records the total family income by summing the Total personal income (weekly) (INCP) of each family member aged 15 years and over present in the household on Census Night.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Total Family Income as Stated (weekly)' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it did not say the figure is banded, is built from imputed range medians, or differs from FINF only in its treatment of partial non-response.

value_domain: Banded weekly total family income
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total family income (weekly) (FINF)
variable_description: The family's weekly income band, with families that did not all answer set aside rather than banded. ABS defines the variable as recording "the total family income by summing the Total personal income (weekly) (INCP) of each family member aged 15 years and over present in the household on Census Night", and codes any family where a member aged 15 or over left income blank to a partial or all-not-stated category. That is the whole difference from FINASF on the same family row, which bands those families using the incomes that were given. It appears in the 2011, 2016 and 2021 family tables.
value_definition: A two-digit code across 25 categories: 22 income bands running from 01, negative income, to 22, $8,000 or more per week, then 23 partial income stated, && all incomes not stated and @@ not applicable for non-family households.
limitation: The partial income stated code is not a small residual and it is not an income band, so dropping it as missing biases the distribution toward families who answered in full; FINASF is the column that keeps them. ABS also warns that part of the rise in family income between Censuses reflects new higher ranges being added to the personal income question rather than higher incomes.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 page for FINF gives the definition, the 23-value code list including the partial and all-not-stated codes, the median imputation step and the note about new income ranges.
evidence_quote: This variable records the total family income by summing the Total personal income (weekly) (INCP) of each family member aged 15 years and over present in the household on Census Night.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Total Family Income (weekly)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said how it differs from FINASF or that the income ranges themselves changed between Censuses.

value_domain: Census family composition classification
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Family composition (FMCF)
variable_description: What kind of family this is: a couple with no children, a couple with children, a one parent family or another family type. ABS defines it as classifying "families into different family types" and says it "uses a single family reference person and classifies each member around that person", usually the first person listed on the form. Coding takes couple relationships first, then parent-child relationships, then child dependency, then other family ties, and surname and marital status help settle complex households. It is the main family variable, feeding FIDF, HCFMD and HCFMF, and appears in the 2011, 2016 and 2021 family tables.
value_definition: A four-digit code within four groups: 1 couple family with no children, 2 couple family with children, 3 one parent family, 9 other family, with 17 detailed categories in total and @@@@ for non-family households and unoccupied dwellings.
limitation: It labels a family, not a household: a dwelling holding two families produces two rows with two different values and no single household family type, which is what HCFMD is for. It also cannot tell you a couple's sex composition, which is in SSCF, and a child reported as temporarily absent only counts toward "with children" when the absence was recorded, which the form caps at three people.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 page for FMCF gives the definition, the reference-person method, the order of coding preference, the four groups and 17 detailed categories, and the not-applicable population.
evidence_quote: This variable classifies families into different family types. It uses a single family reference person and classifies each member around that person.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Family Composition' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never mentioned the family reference person, which is the thing that decides every code in the column.

value_domain: Census grandparent family classification
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Grandparent families (FMGF)
variable_description: Whether this family is a grandparent family, and whether the grandparent is partnered or alone. ABS defines the variable as classifying "families into different family types depending on the composition of the family" and says it "recognises grandparent-grandchild relationships"; a family qualifies where a grandparent-grandchild relationship exists and no parent-child relationship does. It sits beside FMCF, which would code the same family as a couple family or a one parent family, and beside CTGP on the person row, which marks the grandchildren. The column appears in the 2016 and 2021 family tables.
value_definition: A one- or two-digit code: 1 couple family with grandchildren, split into 11 under 15, 12 dependent students aged 15 to 24 and 13 non-dependent; 2 lone grandparent, split into 21, 22 and 23 the same way; @@ not applicable to every other family.
limitation: It is not a count of children being raised by grandparents. The classification requires that no parent was counted in the family, so a three-generation household where a parent is present is coded @@ even when the grandparents do the caring, and ABS notes that a parent who happened to be temporarily absent on Census night can turn an ordinary family into a grandparent family by mistake.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 page for FMGF gives the definition, the no-parent-present rule, the full code list with its dependency splits, and the nominal parent and temporary absence caveats.
evidence_quote: This variable classifies families into different family types depending on the composition of the family
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Grandparent Families' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not state the no-parent-present rule that decides whether a family appears in this column at all.

value_domain: Family sequence within the household (primary, second, third)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Family number (FNOF)
variable_description: Whether this family is the first, second or third family coded in its household. ABS defines it as categorising "multiple families in a household as either the primary, second or third family", and sets the primary family as the one containing dependent children where any are present, otherwise the first family on the form. It is what makes HCFMD, which reports only the primary family's composition, differ from HCFMF, which reports every family. The column appears in the 2011, 2016 and 2021 family tables.
value_definition: A single character: 1 primary family, 2 second family, 3 third family, @ not applicable to non-family and non-classifiable households, unoccupied dwellings, non-private dwellings and migratory, off-shore and shipping areas.
limitation: "Primary" is a coding label and nothing more. ABS says it should not be read as ownership, headship or dominance in the household, so a second family is not a subordinate one. A household with four or more families cannot be coded, since only three families per household can be identified, which bites hardest in multigenerational and large extended households.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 page for FNOF gives the definition, the code list, the rule for choosing the primary family, the three-family maximum and the explicit warning against reading 'primary' as precedence.
evidence_quote: This variable categorises multiple families in a household as either the primary, second or third family.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Family Number' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so a reader had no way to know the values are ordinal by coding convenience rather than by any property of the families.

value_domain: Parent indicator (male parent, female parent)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Parent indicator (FPIP)
variable_description: Marks this person as a parent in the family they were counted in, and says whether they are the male or the female parent. ABS defines it as recording "the usually resident parent in a family household" and says it "identifies parents of children in family households, provided the parent and child were counted in the same family, or were reported as temporarily absent on Census Night". It is built from the sex and relationship questions, and it is the person-row counterpart to the child columns CTPP and CTGP. The column appears in the 2021 person table only and covers same-sex as well as opposite-sex parents.
value_definition: A single character: 1 male parent, 2 female parent, @ not applicable, V overseas visitor.
limitation: It marks parenthood inside one household, not parenthood in general: a parent whose children live elsewhere is coded @, so the column cannot count parents in the population. A child under 15 with no parent present is given a nominal parent, which may be a sibling, grandparent, aunt or uncle, and that person is then flagged here. ABS also found an error affecting 97,359 parents in couple families in 2021 where all children were reported temporarily absent, and publishes corrected counts of 3,062,913 male parents and 3,788,471 female parents.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 page for FPIP gives the definition, the code list, the nominal parent rule and the size and direction of the 2021 misclassification with corrected totals.
evidence_quote: This variable records the usually resident parent in a family household. It identifies parents of children in family households, provided the parent and child were counted in the same family, or were reported as temporarily absent on Census Night.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Parent indicator' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the flag is scoped to the household, that nominal parents are included, or that a published correction exists for 2021.

value_domain: Census relationship between families in a household
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Relationship between families (FRLF)
variable_description: How a second or third family in a household is related to the primary family. ABS defines it as describing "the relationship between families within a household", coded from the relationship in household question with temporarily absent persons taken into account. It applies only to two- and three-family households, and it works with FNOF on the same family row, which says whether the family is the primary, second or third. The column appears in the 2011, 2016 and 2021 family tables.
value_definition: A single character: 1 mother's or father's family, 2 grandparent's family, 3 son's or daughter's family, 4 grandchild's family, 5 brother's or sister's family, 6 other related family, 7 unrelated family, @ not applicable.
limitation: The primary family in a multi-family household is coded @, so the column describes each other family's link back to the primary one rather than a symmetric relationship between all pairs. ABS notes the categories come in complementary pairs, so counting only mother's or father's families without also counting son's or daughter's families halves the true number of households holding that relationship.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 page for FRLF gives the definition, the seven-value code list, the two- and three-family scope and the explicit instruction to combine complementary categories.
evidence_quote: This variable describes the relationship between families within a household.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Relationship Between Families' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it did not warn that the categories are directional and have to be paired before counting.

value_domain: Census form type (paper, online, other)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Form type (FTCP), and ABS Microdata and TableBuilder: Census of Population and Housing
variable_description: Whether the person's 2016 Census record came in on a paper form or online. ABS describes the variable as indicating "the type of form a person used to submit their" Census responses, set from what the ABS Data Capture Centre received rather than from anything the respondent reported. The same variable continues in 2021 under a different mnemonic: ABS records that "The mnemonic for the Form type variable has changed in the 2021 product to FTCP. This previously was FTPP in earlier detailed microdata products." It is a processing attribute, useful mainly for assessing response mode effects on other columns. The column appears in the 2016 person table.
value_definition: A single digit: 1 personal or household paper form, 2 personal or household eForm, 3 other form types.
limitation: It describes the channel a form arrived by, not who filled it in or how carefully, so it cannot identify proxy responses or records completed by a field officer. Category 3 covers everything that is not a standard personal or household form, so it mixes special forms and administrative returns into one residual and will not support a clean paper-against-online comparison on its own.
rationale: ABS publishes a Census Dictionary page for the 2021 continuation of this variable, giving its definition and code list, and states in the Census microdata documentation that the mnemonic FTPP used in earlier products became FTCP in 2021, which ties the 2016 column to that definition.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates the type of form a person used to submit their 2021 Census responses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Form type (person)' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it neither listed the three channels nor connected the 2016 mnemonic to the 2021 one.

value_domain: ASGS Greater Capital City Statistical Area code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Greater Capital City Statistical Areas
variable_description: The greater capital city region, or the rest-of-state balance, that this dwelling stood in on 2021 Census night. ABS defines Greater Capital City Statistical Areas as "Geographic areas built from Statistical Areas Level 4 (SA4s)" whose "boundaries represent labour markets and the functional area of Australian capital cities". The "(en)" in the custodian's label marks place of enumeration, which the ABS Census geography glossary describes as "where a person was on Census night", as against place of usual residence. It is the coarsest of the dwelling geography columns, sitting above SA4UCD, SA3UCD, SA2UCD, SA1UCD and MBUCD on the same dwelling row.
value_definition: A five-character alphanumeric ASGS code: a one-digit state or territory identifier then a four-character GCCSA identifier, for example 1GSYD for Greater Sydney. Edition 3 has 16 spatial GCCSAs covering Australia without gaps and 19 non-spatial special purpose codes for migratory, off-shore, shipping, no usual address and outside Australia.
limitation: Greater Sydney is not the City of Sydney and Greater Melbourne is not the built-up area. A GCCSA is drawn to a labour market, so it reaches well past the urban edge and takes in commuter towns, which makes it unsuitable as an urban-rural split; remoteness areas (RAD, RAND) or section of state (SOSD) do that job. Boundaries are also redrawn each ASGS edition, so the 2021 codes on Edition 3 are not directly comparable with earlier Census geography.
rationale: The ASGS Edition 3 page is the classification authority behind this Census column, giving the definition, the building block, the code structure with an example, the count of regions and the special purpose codes; the Census geography glossary supplies the enumeration against usual residence distinction that the '(en)' suffix carries.
evidence_quote: Geographic areas built from Statistical Areas Level 4 (SA4s). GCCSA boundaries represent labour markets and the functional area of Australian capital cities respectively.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label 'Greater capital city statistical areas (en)' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it explained neither the code shape nor what '(en)' means.

value_domain: ASGS Greater Capital City Statistical Area code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Greater Capital City Statistical Areas
variable_description: The greater capital city region, or the rest-of-state balance, of the person's usual residence at the 2021 Census. The "(ur)" in the custodian's label marks place of usual residence, which the ABS Census geography glossary describes as "where a person usually lives", as against place of enumeration, "where a person was on Census night". ABS defines the regions themselves as "Geographic areas built from Statistical Areas Level 4 (SA4s)" whose "boundaries represent labour markets and the functional area of Australian capital cities". It is the top of the person's usual residence geography hierarchy, above SA4UCP, SA3UCP, SA2UCP, SA1UCP and MBUCP, and is distinct from POWGCCSA, which is the region of the person's workplace.
value_definition: A five-character alphanumeric ASGS code: a one-digit state or territory identifier then a four-character GCCSA identifier, for example 1GSYD for Greater Sydney. Edition 3 has 16 spatial GCCSAs plus 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: It is not where the person was on Census night. Someone enumerated in a hotel in Greater Brisbane while usually living in Rest of NSW carries the Rest of NSW code here while the dwelling row they attach to carries Greater Brisbane in GCCSAD, so the two columns will disagree by design. People with no usual address are given a special purpose code rather than being left missing, so those records are present in the column but not locatable on a map.
rationale: The ASGS Edition 3 page defines the classification, its building block, the code structure and the special purpose codes; the ABS Census geography glossary defines place of usual residence against place of enumeration, which is the distinction the '(ur)' suffix carries.
evidence_quote: Greater Capital City Statistical Areas (GCCSAs) are geographic areas built from Statistical Areas Level 4 (SA4s). GCCSA boundaries represent labour markets and the functional area of Australian capital cities respectively.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Greater capital city statistical areas (ur)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the column is on a usual residence basis and will differ from the dwelling-level GCCSAD for visitors.

value_domain: Census public or private sector of employer
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Public/private sector (GNGP)
variable_description: Whether the person's employer is a government body and at what level of government, or a private business. ABS defines the variable as classifying "employed people according to whether they are employed in the government (public) or non-government (private) sector", coded from the written employer business name and workplace address that the respondent supplies. It applies to employed persons aged 15 and over and describes the main job, sitting beside INDP for the employer's industry and OCCP for the person's own occupation. The column appears in the 2011, 2016 and 2021 person tables.
value_definition: A single character: 1 national government, 2 state or territory government, 3 local government, 4 private sector, & not stated, @ not applicable, V overseas visitor.
limitation: Private sector is a default rather than a positive finding: ABS assigns anyone it cannot classify as public sector to code 4, so that category absorbs the doubtful cases and is overstated at the margin. Within the public sector, records that could not be split by level of government were imputed proportionally across national, state and local, so the three-way split is partly modelled and unreliable for small areas.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 page for GNGP gives the definition, the code list, the coding rule that unclassified records default to private, and the proportional imputation used to split the public sector by level.
evidence_quote: This variable classifies employed people according to whether they are employed in the government (public) or non-government (private) sector.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Public/Private Sector' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it hid both the four-way split and the fact that private sector is the fallback code.

value_domain: Census long-term health condition flag (arthritis)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has arthritis (HARTP)
variable_description: Whether the person ticked arthritis on the 2021 Census long-term health conditions question. ABS defines it as describing "whether a person reported that they have arthritis", one of ten conditions on a tick list asked for the first time in 2021. It feeds the household counts CPLTHD, CALTHD and CCLTHD and the comorbidity pair columns COARASP, COARDBP, COARHDP and COARMHP that sit on the same person row. It applies to all persons, including children.
value_definition: A three-character code: 011 has arthritis, 012 does not have arthritis, &&& not stated, VVV overseas visitor.
limitation: It does not separate osteoarthritis from rheumatoid arthritis, which are different diseases with different causes and treatments, and it carries no severity, treatment or date of onset. ABS states the Census long-term health condition data are not intended to produce prevalence estimates and directs users to the National Health Survey or the National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Surveys instead.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 page for HARTP gives the definition, the three-character code list, the derivation from the tick list, the arthritis-type caveat and the explicit prevalence warning.
evidence_quote: This variable describes whether a person reported that they have arthritis.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Whether has arthritis' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it showed neither the code shape nor the ABS warning against reading the column as prevalence.

value_domain: Census long-term health condition flag (asthma)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has asthma (HASTP)
variable_description: Whether the person ticked asthma on the 2021 Census long-term health conditions question. ABS defines the variable as "Whether a person has been told by a doctor or nurse that they have asthma", which makes the test a reported diagnosis rather than symptoms. Asthma is counted separately from the broader lung condition tick that feeds HLUNP, so the two columns do not overlap. It applies to all persons and feeds the comorbidity pairs COARASP, COASHDP and COASLCP on the same row.
value_definition: A three-character code: 021 has asthma, 022 does not have asthma, &&& not stated, VVV overseas visitor.
limitation: The condition is a diagnosis ever received, not asthma now: a person diagnosed in childhood whose symptoms have long resolved may still tick it, and undiagnosed asthma is coded 022 rather than left unknown. There is no severity, control or medication information, so the column cannot separate mild seasonal asthma from illness that requires hospital care.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 page for HASTP gives the definition with its doctor-or-nurse diagnosis wording, the code list, the derivation from the tick list and the prevalence caution.
evidence_quote: Whether a person has been told by a doctor or nurse that they have asthma.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Whether has asthma' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said the question turns on a past diagnosis rather than current illness.

value_domain: Census long-term health condition flag (cancer, including remission)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has cancer (including remission) (HCANP)
variable_description: Whether the person ticked cancer, including remission, on the 2021 Census long-term health conditions question. ABS defines the variable as describing "whether a person has been told by a doctor or nurse that they have cancer", and the tick explicitly covers people in remission as well as people under treatment. It applies to all persons and feeds the household counts and the comorbidity pair column COCNHDP on the same person row. This is the first Census to carry it.
value_definition: A three-character code: 031 has cancer (including remission), 032 does not have cancer, &&& not stated, VVV overseas visitor.
limitation: Because remission counts, a person successfully treated twenty years ago and a person in active treatment are both coded 031, so the column is a lifetime marker rather than a measure of current disease and cannot be used to size a treatment population. It carries no cancer type, site, stage or date, and ABS notes that respondents may have reported benign as well as malignant tumours.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 page for HCANP gives the definition, the code list, the derivation from the tick list, the benign-neoplasm caveat and the prevalence warning.
evidence_quote: This variable describes whether a person has been told by a doctor or nurse that they have cancer.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Whether has cancer (including remission)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never spelled out that remission and active disease share one code.

value_domain: Census family household composition at the dwelling level
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Family household composition (dwelling) (HCFMD)
variable_description: What kind of household this dwelling holds: how many families are in it and what type the main one is. ABS defines it as counting "the types of families within family households at the dwelling level" and says that "In multiple family households, only the family composition of the primary family is recorded". It is built during processing by combining family composition (FMCF) with household composition (HHCD), and it is the dwelling-row column to use when one value per household is wanted. It appears in the 2011, 2016 and 2021 dwelling tables.
value_definition: A two-digit code across 17 values in three groups: 11 to 14 one family households, 21 to 28 multiple family households, 31 to 34 other households, plus @@ not applicable.
limitation: In a household holding two families it describes only the primary one, so a dwelling containing a couple with children and a lone parent is summarised by the first and the second family is invisible; HCFMF at the family level keeps both. The "other not classifiable" group is mostly dwellings where no form was returned or too little information was available, so it is a response outcome rather than a household type.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 page for HCFMD gives the definition, the primary family rule, the code structure across three groups, the derivation from FMCF and HHCD, and what the not-classifiable category contains.
evidence_quote: This variable counts the types of families within family households at the dwelling level. In multiple family households, only the family composition of the primary family is recorded.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Family Household Composition (Dwelling)' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it did not say that the second and third families are dropped from the code.

value_domain: Census family household composition at the family level
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Family household composition (family) (HCFMF)
variable_description: This family's type, together with how many families share its household. ABS defines the variable as counting "the types of families within family households at the family level" and says that "In multiple family households all family types are counted", which is the whole difference from HCFMD on the dwelling row. It is built during processing from family composition (FMCF) and household composition (HHCD), so it carries both facts in one code. It appears in the 2011, 2016 and 2021 family tables.
value_definition: A two-digit code across 13 values, crossing one, two, and three-or-more family households with four family types: couple family with no children, couple family with children, one parent family and other family. @@ marks not applicable for non-family households, unoccupied dwellings, non-private dwellings and special geographic areas.
limitation: Counting this column counts families, not households or people, so a two-family household contributes two rows and any household tally built from it double counts; HCFMD is the one-row-per-dwelling column. Family definitions also differ between ABS collections, so these categories are not interchangeable with family types published by other agencies.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 page for HCFMF gives the definition, the explicit contrast with the dwelling-level variable, the 13-category structure, the derivation from FMCF and HHCD, and the caution about differing family definitions.
evidence_quote: This variable counts the types of families within family households at the family level. In multiple family households all family types are counted.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Family Household Composition (Family)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the unit of count, which is the only thing separating it from HCFMD, was never stated.

value_domain: Census long-term health condition flag (dementia, including Alzheimer's)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has dementia (including Alzheimer's) (HDEMP)
variable_description: Whether the person ticked dementia on the 2021 Census long-term health conditions question. ABS defines the variable as "Whether a person has been told by a doctor or nurse that they have dementia (including Alzheimer's)", so the test is a reported diagnosis. It applies to all persons and is one of ten conditions on the tick list that ABS asked for the first time in 2021; a person reporting several conditions is also counted in CLTHP and in whichever comorbidity pair columns match. It sits with HSTRP for stroke and HMHCP for mental health conditions on the same person row.
value_definition: A three-character code: 041 has dementia (including Alzheimer's), 042 does not have dementia, &&& not stated, VVV overseas visitor.
limitation: The person-level tick applies everywhere, but the household counts built on it (CPLTHD, CPLTHRD, CALTHD, CCLTHD) cover occupied private dwellings only, so people living in residential aged care are missing from those totals while still appearing here. The Census is also a household-completed form, so a dementia answer is often given by a relative or left blank, and it carries no stage, type or care setting.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary 2021 page for HDEMP gives the definition with its doctor-or-nurse diagnosis wording, the code list, the derivation from the tick list and the prevalence caution; the CPLTHD page supplies the occupied-private-dwellings scope of the household counts built from it.
evidence_quote: Whether a person has been told by a doctor or nurse that they have dementia (including Alzheimer's)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Whether has dementia (including alzheimer's)' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it did not flag that aged care residents drop out of every household-level health count built from this column.

value_domain: Census long-term health condition flag (diabetes)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has diabetes (excluding gestational diabetes) (HDIAP)
variable_description: Whether the person reported that a doctor or nurse had told them they have diabetes, other than gestational diabetes. The ABS Census Dictionary defines it as "Whether a person has been told by a doctor or nurse that they have diabetes (excluding gestational diabetes). This variable does not indicate whether a person has multiple long-term health conditions." It is one of ten separate condition flags added to the person record for the first time in 2021, all struck from the same tick-box question, so HLTHP beside it answers whether any condition was reported and HOLHP catches conditions outside the ten.
value_definition: Two substantive codes, 051 has diabetes and 052 does not, with &&& for not stated and VVV for an overseas visitor.
limitation: It records a reported diagnosis, not a clinical record, and the Census does not separate type 1 from type 2 diabetes, so the two cannot be counted apart. ABS also warns that Census condition data is not intended to give prevalence estimates, which belong to the National Health Survey.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary publishes a definition, an applicable-to statement and the full code list for this exact mnemonic in the 2021 Census, which is the only Census year the column appears in the PLIDA person table.
evidence_quote: Whether a person has been told by a doctor or nurse that they have diabetes (excluding gestational diabetes).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Whether has diabetes (excluding gestational diabetes)', with nothing to say the answer is self-reported diagnosis or that type 1 and type 2 are not distinguished.

value_domain: ASCED level of highest educational attainment
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Level of highest educational attainment (HEAP)
variable_description: One ranked measure of how far a person got in education, combining school and post-school study into a single ladder. ABS defines it as "a single measure of a person's overall highest level of educational attainment, whether it be a school or non-school qualification", built during processing by running the highest year of school completed (HSCP) and the level of the non-school qualification (QALLP) through a decision table. It sits on the person table for 2011, 2016 and 2021, and is the column to use when a single attainment ranking is wanted rather than the two inputs separately.
value_definition: Codes from the Australian Standard Classification of Education, released at one digit (12 categories), two digits (20) and three digits (31), running from postgraduate degree down to Year 9 and below, with supplementary codes for inadequately described, no attainment, not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor.
limitation: The ranking is not a clean ladder: Secondary Education Years 10 and above is placed above Certificate I and II, so a numeric ordering of the codes does not order people by years of study. It also says nothing about the field of study, which is QALFP, and nothing about when or where the qualification was obtained.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the derivation from HSCP and QALLP, the classification and the number of categories at each digit level, all for the same mnemonic PLIDA carries.
evidence_quote: This variable records a single measure of a person's overall highest level of educational attainment, whether it be a school or non-school qualification.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's title, 'Level of Highest Educational Attainment', and never said the column is derived from two other Census variables or that its ordering is not monotonic in years of study.

value_domain: Census household composition classification
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Household composition (HHCD)
variable_description: Whether the people counted in this dwelling formed one family, more than one family, or no family at all. ABS defines it as describing "the type of household within a dwelling. It indicates if a family is present on Census Night and if other unrelated household members are present." It sits on the dwelling record for 2011, 2016 and 2021, is built during processing from the relationship-in-household and temporarily-absent questions, and is the column that decides whether the family-level table has any rows for this dwelling at all.
value_definition: A three-level hierarchical code with ten final categories under four headings: one family household (110, 120), multiple family household (211, 212, 221, 222), non-family household (310, 320) and non-classifiable household (410, 420), plus @@@ not applicable for unoccupied private dwellings, non-private dwellings and migratory, off-shore and shipping SA1s.
limitation: It does not describe what kind of family is present. A couple with children and a lone parent both read as a one family household, and family type is FMCF. Census processing also codes at most three families to a household, so a larger shared dwelling is compressed rather than fully described.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the applicable population, the full hierarchical code list and the derivation from the relationship and temporarily-absent questions for the same mnemonic.
evidence_quote: This variable describes the type of household within a dwelling. It indicates if a family is present on Census Night and if other unrelated household members are present.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Household Composition' and never distinguished the household-type question from the family-type question a reader would otherwise assume it answered.

value_domain: Census long-term health condition flag (heart disease)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has heart disease (including heart attack or angina) (HHEDP)
variable_description: Whether the person reported being told by a doctor or nurse that they have heart disease, with heart attack and angina counted in. ABS defines it as describing "whether a person has been told by a doctor or nurse that they have heart disease (including heart attack or angina)". It is one of the ten condition flags new to the 2021 person record; because each condition has its own column, combinations have to be built by crossing them, and ABS publishes ready-made pair variables such as CODBHDP for diabetes and heart disease.
value_definition: Codes 061 has heart disease and 062 does not, with &&& not stated and VVV overseas visitor.
limitation: A tick covers everything from a past heart attack to managed angina, so it carries no severity, no date of onset and no current treatment status. ABS advises Census condition data is not for prevalence estimates.
rationale: The dictionary page publishes the definition, applicable population and code list for this exact mnemonic in the only Census year PLIDA carries it.
evidence_quote: This variable describes whether a person has been told by a doctor or nurse that they have heart disease (including heart attack or angina).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's title only, and gave no indication that the answer is a self-reported diagnosis with no severity or timing attached.

value_domain: Census household income derivation indicator
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Household income derivation indicator (HIDD)
variable_description: A quality flag saying why a household's income total may be incomplete or odd. ABS defines it as identifying "households where people were absent from the dwelling on Census Night, did not state their income, or stated a negative income". It is the column to filter on before using HIND, HINASD or HIED, because it separates a household whose members all reported income from one where a resident was away or left the income question blank.
value_definition: Nine categories crossing two conditions, whether any household member aged 15 and over was temporarily absent, and whether all incomes were stated and any were negative, running from code 1 (nobody absent, all incomes stated, none negative) to code 8, plus @ not applicable for non-private and unoccupied dwellings.
limitation: It flags the problem without fixing it, and it does not say how much income is missing. A household with one absent member and a household with three read the same way, so it cannot be used to bound the size of the understatement.
rationale: The dictionary page gives a verbatim definition, the applicable population and the structure of the nine categories, and names the derivation from household composition and personal income responses.
evidence_quote: This variable identifies households where people were absent from the dwelling on Census Night, did not state their income, or stated a negative income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Household Income Derivation Indicator' with no hint that it is the quality gate for the three household income columns beside it.

value_domain: Equivalised weekly household income range
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Equivalised total household income (weekly) (HIED)
variable_description: Weekly household income adjusted for how many people it has to support, so that households of different size can be compared. ABS defines it as "household income adjusted by the application of an equivalence scale to facilitate comparison of income levels between households of differing size and composition", using the modified OECD scale of 1 point for the first adult, 0.5 for each further person aged 15 and over and 0.3 for each child under 15. It sits on the dwelling record for 2011, 2016 and 2021 and is the household income column to use for living-standard comparisons, where HIND is the unadjusted total.
value_definition: Nineteen categories: sixteen income ranges from nil income up to $3,500 or more a week ($182,000 a year), plus code 17 partial income stated, && all incomes not stated and @@ not applicable. Personal income arrives in ranges, so median values from the Survey of Income and Housing are substituted before summing and dividing by the equivalence factor.
limitation: The published value is a range, not the household's actual equivalised dollars, and it rests on survey medians standing in for each member's reported income band, so it should not be treated as a measured amount for an individual household. Equivalising also assumes income is shared evenly inside the household, which the Census cannot check.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the equivalence scale point by point, the applicable population and the derivation using Survey of Income and Housing medians.
evidence_quote: Equivalised total household income is household income adjusted by the application of an equivalence scale to facilitate comparison of income levels between households of differing size and composition.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's title alone and never explained what equivalising does, which scale is used, or that the underlying dollars are imputed survey medians.

value_domain: Weekly household income range as stated
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total household income as stated (weekly) (HINASD)
variable_description: The household's weekly income built from whatever incomes its residents actually reported, keeping households where somebody left the question blank or was away. ABS defines it as the "total weekly income of a private household based on the reported personal incomes of all members that are aged 15 years or older". It is the permissive twin of HIND, which sends the same households to a partial-income code instead, and HIDD on the same row says which households the two columns treat differently.
value_definition: Twenty-two income brackets from negative income up to $8,000 or more a week ($416,000 a year), plus && all incomes not stated and @@ not applicable. Personal incomes are reported in ranges, so median values from the Survey of Income and Housing are assigned to each band before summing.
limitation: A stated total from an incomplete household understates that household's real income, and nothing in this column says by how much or how many members were missing. Reading it as the household total without checking HIDD biases income distributions downwards.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the applicable population, the bracket count and the explicit contrast with HIND, which is the fact that distinguishes the two columns sitting side by side in the PLIDA dwelling table.
evidence_quote: Total weekly income of a private household based on the reported personal incomes of all members that are aged 15 years or older.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Total Household Income as Stated (weekly)' and never said what 'as stated' excludes, leaving it indistinguishable from HIND on the same table.

value_domain: Weekly household income range
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total household income (weekly) (HIND)
variable_description: The household's weekly income, given only where every resident aged 15 and over who was present reported theirs. ABS defines it as "the sum of Total personal income (weekly) (INCP) of each resident aged 15 years or older who was present in the household on Census Night", and households with a member absent or an income left blank fall into a partial-income code rather than a dollar range. HINASD on the same row is the version that still adds up what was stated, so comparing the two shows how much of the income distribution rests on incomplete households.
value_definition: Twenty-five categories, from negative income and nil income through weekly ranges up to $8,000 or more ($416,000 a year), with separate codes for partial income stated, all incomes not stated and not applicable. Median incomes for each range, derived from the Survey of Income and Housing, stand in for each member's reported band before summing.
limitation: It is not income of the usual household. A resident temporarily absent on Census night contributes nothing, so a household counted on 10 August 2021 with a member away is not comparable with the same household counted in full. The value is also a bracket, not the household's actual dollars.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition naming INCP as the input, the applicable population, the category count and the treatment of partial and missing income, which is the fact that separates it from HINASD.
evidence_quote: The sum of Total personal income (weekly) (INCP) of each resident aged 15 years or older who was present in the household on Census Night.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's title with no statement of the presence-on-Census-night restriction or the partial-income code, the two things that make it differ from HINASD beside it.

value_domain: Census long-term health condition flag (kidney disease)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has kidney disease (HKIDP)
variable_description: Whether the person reported being told by a doctor or nurse that they have kidney disease. ABS defines it as "Whether a person has been told by a doctor or nurse that they have kidney disease. This variable does not indicate whether a person has multiple long-term health conditions." It is one of the ten condition flags added to the 2021 person record, and in PLIDA it can be checked against dialysis and transplant activity in the MBS and PBS products for the same person.
value_definition: Codes 071 has kidney disease and 072 does not, with &&& not stated and VVV overseas visitor.
limitation: It gives no stage, no function measure and no treatment status, so early chronic kidney disease and end-stage disease on dialysis are the same tick. ABS advises the Census condition data is not intended to produce prevalence estimates.
rationale: The dictionary page publishes the definition, applicable population and code list for this exact mnemonic in the only Census year PLIDA carries it.
evidence_quote: Whether a person has been told by a doctor or nurse that they have kidney disease.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's title only and said nothing about the tick being a reported diagnosis with no stage or treatment attached.

value_domain: Census long-term health condition flag (any condition)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has one or more long-term health condition(s) (HLTHP)
variable_description: A single summary tick across the whole 2021 health question: did the person report at least one long-term condition, or none. ABS defines it as identifying "the population who has at least one long-term health condition (including any other long-term health conditions) and the population who reported they did not have a long-term health condition". It is the natural population filter over the ten individual condition columns on the same person record, and CLTHP beside it counts how many of the named conditions were ticked.
value_definition: Codes 121 does not have a long-term health condition and 122 has one or more, with &&& not stated and VVV overseas visitor.
limitation: It cannot say which condition, or how many, and it does not carry its own non-response rate because it is built during processing; ABS points users to CLTHP for item non-response on the underlying health question. A person who ticked only 'any other' condition reads the same as one with three named conditions.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the two substantive codes, the derivation from the health question and the explicit note that non-response has to be read off CLTHP instead.
evidence_quote: This variable identifies the population who has at least one long-term health condition (including any other long-term health conditions) and the population who reported they did not have a long-term health condition.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's title and gave no route to the non-response rate, which for this derived column is not its own but CLTHP's.

value_domain: Census long-term health condition flag (lung condition)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has lung condition (including COPD and emphysema) (HLUNP)
variable_description: Whether the person reported being told by a doctor or nurse that they have a lung condition, with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and emphysema named on the form. ABS defines it as describing "whether a person has been told by a doctor or nurse that they have a lung condition (including Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disorder (COPD) or emphysema). This variable does not indicate whether a person has multiple long-term health conditions." Asthma is a separate tick box and a separate column, HASTP, so the two must be combined by hand to get any respiratory condition.
value_definition: Codes 081 has a lung condition and 082 does not, with &&& not stated and VVV overseas visitor.
limitation: The one tick covers a wide span of lung disease with no severity, no smoking history and no oxygen or treatment detail. ABS notes Census condition data is not intended for prevalence estimates, which should come from the National Health Survey.
rationale: The dictionary page publishes the definition, applicable population and code list for this exact mnemonic, and the health topic index confirms asthma is a separate variable.
evidence_quote: Long-term health conditions data from Census is not intended to provide prevalence estimates.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's title and did not point out that asthma is captured separately, the most likely mistake in counting respiratory conditions.

value_domain: Census long-term health condition flag (mental health condition)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has mental health condition (including depression or anxiety) (HMHCP)
variable_description: Whether the person reported being told by a doctor or nurse that they have a mental health condition, with depression and anxiety named on the form. ABS defines it as "Whether a person has been told by a doctor or nurse that they have a mental health condition (including depression or anxiety)", and notes the flag does not indicate whether the person has multiple long-term conditions. It is the Census-side counterpart to mental-health item use in the PBS and MBS products for the same person, and is the only mental health measure on the Census person record.
value_definition: Codes 091 has a mental health condition and 092 does not, with &&& not stated and VVV overseas visitor.
limitation: It cannot separate depression from anxiety from any other diagnosis, and it requires a person to have been told by a clinician, so undiagnosed and untreated conditions are absent by construction. ABS warns that Census condition data is not intended to give prevalence estimates.
rationale: The dictionary page publishes the definition, the applicable population and the code list for this exact mnemonic in the only Census year PLIDA carries it.
evidence_quote: Whether a person has been told by a doctor or nurse that they have a mental health condition (including depression or anxiety)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's title and gave no warning that the tick requires a clinician's diagnosis, which is what makes it undercount untreated conditions.

value_domain: Census long-term health condition flag (other conditions)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has other long-term health condition(s) (HOLHP)
variable_description: The residual tick on the 2021 health question: the person reported a long-term condition that is none of the ten named on the form. ABS defines it as whether a person has been told by a doctor or nurse that they have a long-term health condition, excluding arthritis, asthma, cancer, dementia, diabetes, heart disease, kidney disease, lung conditions, mental health conditions and stroke. It matters because HLTHP counts a person with only this tick as having a condition, so the ten named columns will not add up to HLTHP.
value_definition: Codes 111 has one or more other long-term health conditions and 112 does not, with &&& not stated and VVV overseas visitor.
limitation: It names nothing.
