The condition behind the tick is not recorded anywhere on the Census record, so this column cannot be used to identify any particular disease and cannot be compared with a diagnosis list from another dataset. ABS also directs users to CLTHP for item non-response, since this derived column has none of its own.
rationale: The dictionary page defines the residual by naming the ten conditions it excludes and publishes the code list for the exact mnemonic.
evidence_quote: Whether a person has been told by a doctor or nurse that they have a long-term health condition
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Whether has other long-term health condition(s)' without saying what 'other' is other than, or that this tick is what makes the ten named columns fall short of HLTHP.

value_domain: Canadian National Occupancy Standard bedroom surplus or shortfall
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Housing suitability (HOSD)
variable_description: How many bedrooms the dwelling has spare, or how many more it would need, given who was living in it. ABS defines it as "a measure of housing utilisation based on a comparison of the number of bedrooms in a dwelling with a series of household demographics", applying the Canadian National Occupancy Standard: no more than two people to a bedroom, children under 5 of different sexes may share, children under 18 of the same sex may share, and single adults and couples each need their own room. It sits on the dwelling record for 2016 and 2021 and is the ABS measure behind overcrowding counts, since needing one or more extra bedrooms is the usual overcrowding threshold.
value_definition: Nine ordered categories from 01 four or more extra bedrooms needed through 05 no bedrooms needed or spare to 09 four or more bedrooms spare, plus 10 unable to determine, && not stated and @@ not applicable, twelve categories in all.
limitation: It is a rule applied to bedroom counts and household demographics, not a judgement about the dwelling. It says nothing about floor area, dwelling condition, or whether the people sharing a room would choose to, and applying the standard to households whose sleeping arrangements are culturally different can register crowding that the residents would not.
rationale: The dictionary page publishes the definition, the applicable population, the ten-category code list and the Canadian National Occupancy Standard rules the derivation applies.
evidence_quote: This variable is a measure of housing utilisation based on a comparison of the number of bedrooms in a dwelling with a series of household demographics
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Housing Suitability' with 'not specified' as its domain, so nothing said the values are a signed bedroom surplus or that a specific occupancy standard defines them.

value_domain: Hours worked in the week before Census night (0 to 99)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Hours worked (HRSP)
variable_description: How many hours the person worked across all jobs in the single week before Census night. ABS defines it as "the number of hours worked by the employed person in all jobs during the week prior to Census night. This excludes any time off but includes overtime and extra time worked." It is the input to HRWRP, which bands the same answer, and to the full-time and part-time split in LFSP, which cuts at 35 hours. It sits on the person record for 2011, 2016 and 2021.
value_definition: A two-digit integer 00 to 99 giving hours singly, with && not stated, @@ not applicable and VV overseas visitor; 103 categories in all. The not-applicable code covers unemployed people, people not in the labour force, people whose labour force status was not stated and anyone under 15.
limitation: It is one week, not usual hours. A person on leave, on a rostered week off or stood down reports low hours without any change in their job, and in 2021 large parts of the country were in COVID-19 lockdown on Census night, so the week is not a normal one. It also gives no split between jobs for someone holding more than one.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the applicable population, the full value range including supplementary codes, the 1.7% non-response rate for 2021 and the lockdown caveat.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates the number of hours worked by the employed person in all jobs during the week prior to Census night. This excludes any time off but includes overtime and extra time worked.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Hours Worked' with no statement of the reference week, no note that it sums across jobs, and no warning about the 2021 lockdowns.

value_domain: Hours worked ranges
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Hours worked (ranges) (HRWRP)
variable_description: The banded form of the same weekly hours answer that HRSP holds singly. ABS defines it as "the number of hours worked in ranges by the employed person in all jobs during the week prior to Census night. This excludes any time off but includes overtime and extra time worked." Its bands break at 35 hours, the ABS full-time threshold, so it is the column to use for a full-time and part-time split; the 2021 bands were changed to line up with the labour force statistics standard, which makes comparison against the 2011 and 2016 versions on the same table a recoding job.
value_definition: Eleven bands: 00 zero hours, 01 one to nine, 02 ten to 19, 03 twenty to 29, 04 thirty to 34, 05 thirty-five to 39, 06 forty to 44, 07 forty-five to 49, 08 fifty to 59, 09 sixty to 69 and 10 seventy or more, plus && not stated, @@ not applicable and VV overseas visitor.
limitation: Banding removes the detail that separates people inside a band, so a 70 hour week and a 90 hour week are one category and no mean hours can be computed from this column alone. HRSP is the column that keeps single hours.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the applicable population, the complete band list and the note that the 2021 output categories were changed to align with the labour force standard.
evidence_quote: The number of hours worked in ranges by the employed person in all jobs during the week prior to Census night.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Hours Worked (ranges)' and did not disclose the band change between the 2016 and 2021 Census occurrences carried in the same PLIDA product.

value_domain: Highest year of school completed
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Highest year of school completed (HSCP)
variable_description: The furthest year of primary or secondary school the person finished, taken straight from a tick box on the form. ABS defines it as recording "the highest level of primary or secondary schooling completed", classified to the Australian Standard Classification of Education, 2001. It is one of the two inputs to HEAP on the same person record, the other being the non-school qualification level, and it is the only schooling measure available for people who never took a post-school qualification.
value_definition: Six ordered codes: 1 Year 12 or equivalent, 2 Year 11, 3 Year 10, 4 Year 9, 5 Year 8 or below and 6 did not go to school, with & not stated, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor.
limitation: Completed is not the same as passed a certificate. Year 12 or equivalent here does not mean the person was awarded a senior secondary certificate, and no result, subject or state credential is recorded. Where a person marked more than one box, only the first in form order was kept.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the applicable population, the full code list, the classification and the rule for handling multiple marked responses.
evidence_quote: This variable records the highest level of primary or secondary schooling completed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Highest Year of School Completed' with no note that it feeds HEAP, and no warning that completion is not certification.

value_domain: Census long-term health condition flag (stroke)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has had a stroke (HSTRP)
variable_description: Whether the person reported being told by a doctor or nurse that they have had a stroke. ABS defines it as describing "whether a person has been told by a doctor or nurse that they have had a stroke. This variable does not indicate whether a person has multiple long-term health conditions." Unlike the other nine flags on the 2021 person record it records a past event rather than a current condition, so it stays ticked whatever the person's present state.
value_definition: Codes 101 has had a stroke and 102 has not, with &&& not stated and VVV overseas visitor.
limitation: It carries no date, so it cannot say when the stroke happened or order it against anything else in a person's PLIDA record, and it carries no severity or disability outcome. ABS advises Census condition data is not intended for prevalence estimates.
rationale: The dictionary page publishes the definition, applicable population and code list for this exact mnemonic in the only Census year PLIDA carries it.
evidence_quote: This variable describes whether a person has been told by a doctor or nurse that they have had a stroke.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's title only and gave no indication that this flag is an ever-had event with no date attached.

value_domain: ASGS Indigenous Area code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Indigenous Areas
variable_description: The Indigenous Area the dwelling was in when it was enumerated on Census night 2021. ABS defines Indigenous Areas as "medium sized geographic areas built from whole Indigenous Locations. They are designed for the release and analysis of more detailed statistics for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people." It is the middle rung of the three Indigenous geographies on the dwelling record, above ILOCD and below IREGD, and the enumeration counterpart of IAREP, which places a person by usual residence.
value_definition: A six-digit hierarchical ASGS code: one digit for state or territory, two for the Indigenous Region and three for the Indigenous Area. There are 431 Indigenous Areas covering all of Australia without gaps or overlaps, including 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: The area is where the dwelling was counted, not where its residents live, so a holiday house or a hospital ward puts people in an Indigenous Area they have no connection with. The geography also carries no information about who lives there: an Indigenous Area is a statistical boundary, not a community, and INGDWTD is what says whether an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander person was in the household.
rationale: The ASGS Edition 3 page gives the definition, the code structure and the count for Indigenous Areas, which is the classification the value belongs to. The enumeration reading of the '(en)' suffix follows the ABS distinction between place of enumeration and place of usual residence set out at https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/detailed-methodology-information/information-papers/comparing-place-enumeration-place-usual-residence, and is inference rather than a quoted statement about this column.
evidence_quote: Indigenous Areas (IAREs) are medium sized geographic areas built from whole Indigenous Locations.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Indigenous area (en)' with 'not specified' as its domain, so nothing said the value is a six-digit ASGS code or what '(en)' means.

value_domain: ASGS Indigenous Area code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Indigenous Areas
variable_description: The Indigenous Area of the person's usual residence at the 2021 Census, not where they happened to be counted. ABS defines Indigenous Areas as "medium sized geographic areas built from whole Indigenous Locations. They are designed for the release and analysis of more detailed statistics for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people." It is the usual-residence counterpart of IARED on the dwelling record, and it sits between ILOCP and IREGP as the middle rung of the Indigenous geography hierarchy on the person table.
value_definition: A six-digit hierarchical ASGS code: one digit for state or territory, two for the Indigenous Region and three for the Indigenous Area. There are 431 Indigenous Areas covering all of Australia without gaps or overlaps, including 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: It locates the person, not their identification: everybody counted in an Indigenous Area carries the code, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander or not, so INGP is what says who identified. Usual residence is also imputed for some records, and IFPURP on the same row says at which geographic level.
rationale: The ASGS Edition 3 page gives the definition, the code structure and the count for Indigenous Areas. The usual-residence reading of the '(ur)' suffix follows the ABS place of enumeration against place of usual residence distinction at https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/detailed-methodology-information/information-papers/comparing-place-enumeration-place-usual-residence, and is inference rather than a quoted statement about this column.
evidence_quote: Indigenous Areas (IAREs) are medium sized geographic areas built from whole Indigenous Locations.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Indigenous area (ur)' with 'not specified' as its domain, and never said the code is an ASGS geography or that it says nothing about the person's own Indigenous status.

value_domain: Census imputation flag (age)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for age (IFAGEP)
variable_description: Whether the person's age on this Census record was reported or filled in by the ABS. The dictionary defines it as indicating "if a person's age was imputed. Imputation is a statistical process for predicting values where no response was provided to a question and a response could not be derived." It is on the person record for 2011, 2016 and 2021, and it is the column that turns AGEP beside it from a fact into a fact with a provenance; ABS reports 4.4% of ages were imputed in 2021, down from 5.6% in 2016.
value_definition: Two codes: 1 age not imputed and 2 age imputed.
limitation: It is a yes or no: it does not say how far the imputed age might be out, and it does not record why the value had to be imputed. Imputation is also uneven across the country, so ABS suggests using the flag to check how much of a given area's age data was imputed before treating an age distribution for that area as reported.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the two codes, the imputation rate and the statement that the flag can be used to identify how many respondents' age was imputed at different geographic levels; the method itself sits on the Age (AGEP) page.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates if a person's age was imputed. Imputation is a statistical process for predicting values where no response was provided to a question and a response could not be derived.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Imputation Flag for Age' with no rate, no explanation of what triggers imputation, and no warning about remote areas where the imputed share is high enough to distort the age profile.

value_domain: Census imputation flag (registered marital status)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for registered marital status (IFMSTP)
variable_description: Whether the registered marital status on this record was reported or filled in by the ABS. The dictionary defines it as indicating "if a person's Registered marital status (MSTP) was imputed", and where it was, the value was hot-decked from a similar person matched on sex, relationship in household, age, dwelling type and non-private dwelling type, within the same capital city or balance of state. It is on the person record for 2011, 2016 and 2021, and ABS reports 5.5% of registered marital status values were imputed in 2021, down from 6.9% in 2016.
value_definition: Three codes: 1 marital status not imputed, 2 marital status imputed and @ not applicable, the last covering responding and imputed people under 15.
limitation: It applies only to registered marital status, not to MDCP, the social marital status on the same record, which is derived from relationships in the household and is not covered by this flag. Nor does it identify who the donor record was, so imputed statuses cannot be checked or re-derived.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the applicable populations, the three codes, the hot-deck matching variables and the 2021 and 2016 rates.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates if a person's Registered marital status (MSTP) was imputed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's title and never distinguished registered marital status from the social marital status column beside it, which this flag does not cover.

value_domain: Census imputation flag (persons imputed into dwelling)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for number of males and females in dwelling (IFNMFD)
variable_description: Whether the people counted in this occupied private dwelling came from a returned form or were created by the ABS because no form came back. The dictionary defines it as indicating "whether the number of males and females were counted for an occupied private dwelling or were imputed". It is the strongest data-quality flag on the dwelling record for 2011, 2016 and 2021, because where it says imputed, only sex, age, registered marital status and place of usual residence carry imputed values and every other person variable in the dwelling reads not stated or not applicable.
value_definition: Three codes: 1 persons not imputed into dwelling, 2 persons imputed into dwelling and @ not applicable, the last covering unoccupied dwellings, non-private dwellings and migratory, off-shore and shipping SA1s.
limitation: An imputed dwelling is not a partly missing dwelling, it is a wholly constructed one, so counting its residents in any analysis of income, employment, education or health silently adds people whose only real attributes are sex, age, marital status and residence. The flag also gives no rate of its own, since it reflects processing method rather than item non-response.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the applicable population, the three codes and the statement of exactly which person variables are imputed and which are set to not stated for an imputed dwelling.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates whether the number of males and females were counted for an occupied private dwelling or were imputed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Imputation Flag for Number of Males and Females in Dwelling' and never said that where the flag is set, almost every other person variable in the dwelling is empty by construction.

value_domain: Census imputation flag (place of work, by geographic level)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for place of work (IFPOWP)
variable_description: Whether the workplace address on this record was coded from what the person wrote or imputed, and how coarse the stated part was. The dictionary defines it as indicating "if a person's place of work in the week before Census Night was imputed, and to what geographic level". On the PLIDA person record for 2016 and 2021 it is the quality flag for the workplace geography columns beside it, IMPSA2WKADP and IMPSTEWKADP in 2016, so a code of 4 means only the state was stated and everything finer was filled in.
value_definition: Five substantive codes, 1 workplace address not imputed, 2 imputed with SA2 stated, 3 imputed with capital city stated, 4 imputed with state or territory stated and 5 imputed with nothing stated, plus @ not applicable and V overseas visitor.
limitation: It is not a measure of accuracy for the workplace address itself. In 2021 the bigger problem was people entering their home address while working from home during lockdown, and an address like that is not imputed, so this flag reads 1 for it. ABS puts the place of work non-response rate at 11.1% in 2021, up from 10.0% in 2016.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the applicable population, the full code list distinguishing the geographic levels, and the non-response and lockdown notes.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates if a person's place of work in the week before Census Night was imputed, and to what geographic level.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Imputation Flag for Place of Work' as though it were a yes or no, when the codes actually grade how much of the address was stated.

value_domain: Census imputation flag (place of usual residence, by geographic level)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for place of usual residence (IFPURP)
variable_description: Whether the person's usual address was coded from what they wrote or imputed, and at which level of the geographic hierarchy the imputation started. The dictionary defines it as indicating "if a person's place of usual residence was imputed in the Census, and to what geographic level". It is on the person record for 2011, 2016 and 2021 and it is the quality flag for every usual-residence geography column on the same row, so an SA1 of usual residence with a flag of 3 or 4 was chosen for the person rather than reported by them.
value_definition: Four codes: 01 not imputed with state or territory, SA2 and SA1 all stated; 02 SA1 imputed; 03 SA2 and SA1 imputed with state or territory or capital city given; and 04 state or territory, SA2 and SA1 all imputed.
limitation: An unimputed flag does not mean the address is right, only that a codeable one was supplied; a stale or mistaken address passes as code 01. The flag also grades only the residence geography, so a person moved into the wrong SA1 by imputation still carries correct answers everywhere else on the record. ABS puts the SA2-level non-response at 4.3% in 2021, down from 5.4% in 2016.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the applicable population, the four graded codes and the SA1 and SA2 non-response rates for 2016 and 2021.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates if a person's place of usual residence was imputed in the Census, and to what geographic level.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Imputation Flag for Place of Usual Residence' as if binary, when the codes actually record which level of the ASGS hierarchy was the first to be imputed.

value_domain: Census imputation flag (sex)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for sex (IFSEXP)
variable_description: Whether the person's sex on this record was reported or filled in by the ABS. The dictionary defines it as indicating "if a person's binary sex was imputed. Imputation is a statistical process for predicting values where no response was provided to a question and a response could not be derived." It is on the person record for 2016 and 2021 and is created during processing of SEXP beside it; ABS reports 4.7% of sex values were imputed in 2021, down from 5.8% in 2016.
value_definition: Two codes: 01 sex not imputed and 02 sex imputed.
limitation: The flag is about binary sex only. It has nothing to say about the separate 2021 non-binary sex response, and a record flagged as not imputed can still be a form filled in by another household member rather than the person concerned.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition naming binary sex, the two codes, the derivation during SEXP processing and the 2021 and 2016 imputation rates.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates if a person's binary sex was imputed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Imputation Flag for Sex' with no rate and no note that the flag concerns binary sex specifically.

value_domain: ASGS Indigenous Location code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Indigenous Locations
variable_description: The Indigenous Location the dwelling was in when it was enumerated on Census night 2021, the finest of the three Indigenous geographies on the dwelling record. ABS builds them from whole SA1s to represent "small Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities (urban and rural) that are near each other or that share language, traditional borders or Native Title", with a minimum population of about 90 people. ILOCD nests inside IARED and IREGD on the same row, so the three columns are one address at three scales.
value_definition: An eight-digit hierarchical ASGS code: one digit for state or territory, two for the Indigenous Region, three for the Indigenous Area and two for the Indigenous Location, for example 40101303 Raukkan. There are 1,139 Indigenous Locations covering all of Australia, including 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: The small population that makes the geography useful also makes it disclosive, so a cross-tabulation at this level will often be perturbed or suppressed in cleared output. And because it records where the dwelling was counted, not where its residents live, a dwelling occupied by visitors on Census night carries a location that describes none of them.
rationale: The ASGS Edition 3 page gives the definition, the minimum population, the eight-digit code structure and the count. The enumeration reading of the '(en)' suffix follows the ABS place of enumeration against place of usual residence distinction at https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/detailed-methodology-information/information-papers/comparing-place-enumeration-place-usual-residence and is inference.
evidence_quote: small Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities (urban and rural) that are near each other or that share language, traditional borders or Native Title
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Indigenous location (en)' with 'not specified' as its domain, so nothing said the code is an eight-digit ASGS geography or that its small populations force disclosure control.

value_domain: ASGS Indigenous Location code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Indigenous Locations
variable_description: The Indigenous Location of the person's usual residence at the 2021 Census, the finest Indigenous geography on the person record. ABS builds them from whole SA1s to represent "small Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities (urban and rural) that are near each other or that share language, traditional borders or Native Title", with a minimum population of about 90 people. It nests inside IAREP and IREGP on the same row, and IFPURP says whether the usual residence behind all three was imputed.
value_definition: An eight-digit hierarchical ASGS code: one digit for state or territory, two for the Indigenous Region, three for the Indigenous Area and two for the Indigenous Location. There are 1,139 Indigenous Locations covering all of Australia, including 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: Living in an Indigenous Location does not make a person Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander, and most Indigenous Locations are ordinary urban areas rather than discrete communities, so INGP is the only column that carries identification. The small populations behind these codes also mean cell counts at this level rarely survive disclosure control.
rationale: The ASGS Edition 3 page gives the definition, the minimum population and the eight-digit code structure. The usual-residence reading of the '(ur)' suffix follows the ABS place of enumeration against place of usual residence distinction at https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/detailed-methodology-information/information-papers/comparing-place-enumeration-place-usual-residence and is inference.
evidence_quote: small Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities (urban and rural) that are near each other or that share language, traditional borders or Native Title
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Indigenous location (ur)' with 'not specified' as its domain, and left open the reading that living in an Indigenous Location implies Indigenous status.

value_domain: ASGS Statistical Area Level 2 code (workplace)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of work (POWP)
variable_description: The SA2 the person's workplace address fell in during the week before Census night 2016, after ABS imputation filled any gaps. ABS describes place of work as recording "the geographic area in which a person worked in the week before Census Night", with the workplace address coded to a Destination Zone and then aggregated to SA2, SA3, SA4, greater capital city and state. In PLIDA's 2016 person table this SA2 is the finest workplace geography supplied, since the Destination Zone itself is not carried, and IFPOWP beside it says whether the value was reported or imputed.
value_definition: A nine-digit ASGS Statistical Area Level 2 code, the standard workplace geography output of place of work coding.
limitation: It is the workplace, not the employer, and not the person's home. Comparing it with the usual-residence SA2 on the same row gives a commuting pair, but neither an employer identity nor a distance travelled, and where IFPOWP shows imputation the SA2 was assigned rather than reported.
rationale: The mnemonic is a PLIDA name rather than a Census Dictionary variable, so the description is assembled from the ABS place of work page, which gives the geographic levels the workplace address is coded to, and from the neighbouring IFPOWP column, whose codes grade imputation of exactly this geography.
evidence_quote: This variable records the geographic area in which a person worked in the week before Census Night. The address of the person's workplace is coded to a Destination zone (DZN).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Imputed SA2 of workplace address' with 'not specified' as its domain, so nothing said the value is an ASGS SA2 code or that IFPOWP is what qualifies it.

value_domain: ASGS State and Territory code (workplace)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of work (POWP)
variable_description: The state or territory the person's workplace address fell in during the week before Census night 2016, after ABS imputation filled any gaps. It is the coarsest rung of the same place of work coding that produced IMPSA2WKADP on the row, since ABS codes the workplace address to a Destination Zone and then up through SA2, SA3, SA4, greater capital city and state. Its value is that it survives when the finer workplace geography does not: IFPOWP code 4 means the state was stated and everything below it was imputed.
value_definition: A one-digit ASGS state and territory code, 1 New South Wales through 8 Australian Capital Territory, with codes 9 and above for other territories and special purpose areas.
limitation: A state of workplace cannot show interstate commuting patterns at any useful resolution, and it hides the very large share of Australian employment concentrated in a handful of capital city SA2s. Where the finer geography was imputed rather than stated, IMPSA2WKADP is not an independent check on this column, because both come from the same address.
rationale: The mnemonic is a PLIDA name rather than a Census Dictionary variable, so the description is assembled from the ABS place of work page listing state and territory as one of the levels the workplace address is coded to, and from the IFPOWP code list, which explicitly grades a case where only the state was stated.
evidence_quote: This variable records the geographic area in which a person worked in the week before Census Night. The address of the person's workplace is coded to a Destination zone (DZN).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Imputed state/territory of workplace address' with 'not specified' as its domain, and never linked it to the place of work coding hierarchy or to IFPOWP.

value_domain: Weekly total personal income range
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total personal income (weekly) (INCP)
variable_description: The band the person put themselves in when asked what they usually receive each week, from all sources before tax. ABS defines it as indicating "the total income (in ranges) that a person usually receives each week". It is on the person record for 2011, 2016 and 2021, and it is the input the ABS sums to build HIND, HINASD and HIED on the dwelling record, using Survey of Income and Housing medians in place of each band. In PLIDA it is the self-reported income to set against the ATO's assessed income in the PIT products for the same person.
value_definition: Sixteen bands from negative income and nil income through $1 to $149 a week up to $3,500 or more a week ($182,000 a year), with && not stated, @@ not applicable for people under 15 and VV overseas visitor.
limitation: It is usual income as the respondent understands it, not a measured amount for any period, so it does not reconcile with taxable income on a tax return and cannot be used to test tax compliance. The top band is open, so no mean income can be computed from it, and non-response was 7.2% in 2021.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the applicable population, the full band list with weekly and annual equivalents and the 2021 and 2016 non-response rates.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates the total income (in ranges) that a person usually receives each week.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Total Personal Income (weekly)' with no note that the value is a band, that the top band is open, or that it is a self-report rather than an assessed amount.

value_domain: ANZSIC industry of employment code
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Industry of employment (INDP)
variable_description: The industry of the person's main job in the week before Census night, coded to ANZSIC. ABS defines it as describing "the industry of the main job held by the employed person in the week prior to Census night", built by matching the business name and address written on the form against ABS lists of businesses whose main industry activity is already known, and coding the industry and goods or services descriptions by hand where no match is found. It is on the person record for 2011, 2016 and 2021, and it is the Census-side industry to compare with the ANZSIC on the employer's BLADE record for the same period.
value_definition: Codes from the Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification 2006 (Revision 2.0): 20 categories at one digit, 106 at two, 293 at three and 721 at four, with &&&& not stated, @@@@ not applicable and VVVV overseas visitor.
limitation: It is the main job only, so a second job in another industry is invisible, and it is the industry of the employing business rather than the work the person does, which is OCCP. A cleaner in a hospital and a surgeon both code to Health Care and Social Assistance.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the applicable population, the classification and edition, the category count at each digit level, the coding process and the 1.3% non-response rate for 2021.
evidence_quote: This variable describes the industry of the main job held by the employed person in the week prior to Census night.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Industry of Employment' without naming ANZSIC or its edition, and without separating industry from occupation, which is the confusion that matters most in the same table.

value_domain: Indigenous household indicator
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Indigenous household indicator (INGDWTD)
variable_description: Whether at least one person counted at home in this dwelling identified as Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander. ABS defines it as indicating "households which have at least one person who identified as being Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander", derived from the usual address indicator, Indigenous status and household composition. It is on the dwelling record for 2011, 2016 and 2021, and it is what makes a household-level Indigenous analysis possible, since INGP is a person attribute and INGF does the same job for a family.
value_definition: Three codes: 1 household with Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander person(s), 2 other households and @ not applicable for non-private and unoccupied dwellings.
limitation: People who were temporarily absent on Census night are excluded from the derivation, so a household whose only Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander member was away reads as an other household. The 2021 Post Enumeration Survey also put the net undercount of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people at 170,752, a rate of 17.4%, so the flag understates such households more than a general undercount would.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the applicable population, the three codes, the three variables the derivation uses, the exclusion of temporarily absent people and the Post Enumeration Survey undercount figure.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates households which have at least one person who identified as being Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Indigenous Household Indicator' and never said that temporarily absent members are excluded, which is exactly how a household can be miscounted.

value_domain: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander family indicator
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander family indicator (INGF)
variable_description: Whether at least one member of this family identified as Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander and was at home on Census night 2021. ABS defines the flagged group as "Families with at least one person who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander origin, who is a usual resident in the dwelling, and was at home on Census Night." It sits on the family record, where INGDWTD does the same job for the dwelling and INGP for the person, and it is derived from the usual address indicator, Indigenous status and family composition.
value_definition: Four codes: 1 family with Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander person(s), 2 other families, & not stated and @ not applicable for non-family and non-classifiable households, unoccupied and non-private dwellings and migratory, off-shore and shipping SA1s.
limitation: The test requires usual residence and presence on the night at once, so a family whose Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander member was visiting elsewhere is coded as an other family. A dwelling can also hold several families, and the flag is set family by family, so INGDWTD on the dwelling can read yes while a particular family in it reads no.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the applicable population, the four codes and the derivation from usual address indicator, Indigenous status and family composition, including the exclusion of temporarily absent people.
evidence_quote: Families with at least one person who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander origin, who is a usual resident in the dwelling, and was at home on Census Night.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's title and never explained the double test of usual residence and presence, nor how the family flag can disagree with the dwelling flag beside it.

value_domain: Census Indigenous status classification
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Indigenous status (INGP)
variable_description: Whether the person identified as being of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander origin on the Census form. ABS defines it as recording "the response of persons who identified themselves as being of Australian Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander origin in the Census". It is on the person record for 2011, 2016 and 2021, and it is the input to INGDWTD on the dwelling record and INGF on the family record; in PLIDA it is also the Census answer to compare with the Indigenous status recorded administratively in DOMINO, MBS and the health datasets.
value_definition: Four substantive codes: 1 non-Indigenous, 2 Aboriginal, 3 Torres Strait Islander and 4 both Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander, with & not stated and V overseas visitor.
limitation: It is self-identification at one moment, and it is never imputed: where the answer is unclear the record is coded not stated rather than filled in, so 4.9% of 2021 records carry no status at all. Change in the counts between censuses reflects people choosing to identify differently as much as any change in the population, and the 2021 Post Enumeration Survey put the net undercount at 170,752 people, a rate of 17.4%.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the scope, the code list, the explicit statement that Indigenous status is not imputed, the 2021 and 2016 non-response rates and the Post Enumeration Survey undercount.
evidence_quote: This variable records the response of persons who identified themselves as being of Australian Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander origin in the Census.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Indigenous Status' with no note that the variable is never imputed, which is the reason its not-stated share is larger than for neighbouring demographic columns.

value_domain: ASGS Indigenous Region code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Indigenous Regions
variable_description: The Indigenous Region the dwelling was in when it was enumerated on Census night 2021, the broadest of the three Indigenous geographies on the dwelling record. ABS defines them as "large geographic areas built from whole Indigenous Areas and are based on historical boundaries." With only 59 regions covering Australia, it is the level at which Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander analysis usually survives disclosure control, where ILOCD and IARED on the same row often will not.
value_definition: A three-digit hierarchical ASGS code, one digit for state or territory and two for the region, for example 304 Mount Isa. There are 59 Indigenous Regions covering all of Australia, plus 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: The regions follow historical administrative boundaries rather than nations, language groups or Native Title determinations, so a region is not a cultural unit and should not be read as one. Being a dwelling enumeration geography, it also places visitors, not just residents.
rationale: The ASGS Edition 3 page gives the definition, the code structure, the count and the aggregation from Indigenous Areas. The enumeration reading of the '(en)' suffix follows the ABS place of enumeration against place of usual residence distinction at https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/detailed-methodology-information/information-papers/comparing-place-enumeration-place-usual-residence and is inference.
evidence_quote: Indigenous Regions (IREGs) are large geographic areas built from whole Indigenous Areas and are based on historical boundaries.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Indigenous region (en)' with 'not specified' as its domain, and gave no code structure and no warning against reading a region as a cultural boundary.

value_domain: ASGS Indigenous Region code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Indigenous Regions
variable_description: The Indigenous Region of the person's usual residence at the 2021 Census, the broadest Indigenous geography on the person record. ABS defines them as "large geographic areas built from whole Indigenous Areas and are based on historical boundaries." It is the level most Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander outputs are published at, because the 59 regions carry enough population for detailed cross-tabulation where IAREP and ILOCP on the same row do not.
value_definition: A three-digit hierarchical ASGS code, one digit for state or territory and two for the region. There are 59 Indigenous Regions covering all of Australia, plus 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: Everybody usually resident in the region carries the code, so it counts population in a place rather than membership of a community, and INGP is the column that says who identified. The boundaries are also historical administrative lines, not nations or language groups.
rationale: The ASGS Edition 3 page gives the definition, the code structure, the count and the aggregation from Indigenous Areas. The usual-residence reading of the '(ur)' suffix follows the ABS place of enumeration against place of usual residence distinction at https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/detailed-methodology-information/information-papers/comparing-place-enumeration-place-usual-residence and is inference.
evidence_quote: Indigenous Regions (IREGs) are large geographic areas built from whole Indigenous Areas and are based on historical boundaries.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Indigenous region (ur)' with 'not specified' as its domain, so a reader had no code structure and no way to tell it from the dwelling-level IREGD.

value_domain: ASCL language used at home code
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Language used at home (LANP)
variable_description: The main language other than English the person uses at home, or English where no other language is used. The variable identifies whether a person uses a language other than English at home and records that language, classified to the Australian Standard Classification of Languages, 2016. It is on the person record for 2011, 2016 and 2021, and ENGLP beside it carries how well the person speaks English, which this column does not. In 2021 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander respondents were offered an extra tick box letting them name a traditional language.
value_definition: Codes from the Australian Standard Classification of Languages 2016: 505 four-digit languages within 63 three-digit groups and 63 two-digit divisions under nine broad groups, plus supplementary codes for inadequately described and non-verbal responses and for non-response.
limitation: Only one language is kept. A person who uses three languages at home is recorded with the first response on the form, so this column cannot measure multilingualism, and a value of English means the person uses only English at home, not that they speak it. Non-response was 5.7% in 2021.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the applicable population, the classification and edition, the category counts at each level, the single-response rule, the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander tick box and the non-response rate. The description assembles these rather than quoting one sentence, since the page's definition is expressed across several.
evidence_quote: This question only allows for one answer and therefore the number of responses shown in the category '1201 English' is not all persons who use English, but specifically persons who use only English at home.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Language Spoken at Home' for 2011 and 2016 and 'Language used at home' for 2021 with no classification named, and no warning that only the first language given is kept.

value_domain: Labour force participation flag
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Labour force participation flag (LFFP)
variable_description: A two-way collapse of labour force status into in the labour force or not, built for national reporting. ABS defines it as flagging "whether or not a person is participating in the labour force for people who had a stated Labour force status (LFSP)", folding employed full-time, part-time and away from work together with both unemployed categories into one participating group. It appears on the 2021 person record only and exists to support Closing the Gap Target 8, so its category boundaries follow that reporting rule rather than a general analytical need.
value_definition: Two substantive codes, 1 participates in the labour force and 2 not in the labour force, with @ not applicable and V overseas visitor.
limitation: It is not a participation rate and it hides the employment margin: an unemployed jobseeker and a full-time worker are both code 1, so LFSP is needed for anything about employment. People with an unstated labour force status fall into the not-applicable code rather than being counted either way, which was 5.8% of the 2021 population aged 15 and over.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the applicable population, the code list, the recoding from LFSP and the national reporting purpose the categories were designed for.
evidence_quote: This variable flags whether or not a person is participating in the labour force for people who had a stated Labour force status (LFSP).
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Labour force participation flag' with no statement that it is a recode of LFSP built for Closing the Gap reporting, or that unstated status is excluded rather than counted as not participating.

value_domain: Labour force status with hours not stated
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Labour force status and hours worked not stated (LFHRP)
variable_description: Labour force status with employed people whose hours were not stated pulled out into their own category. ABS defines it as combining "Labour force status (LFSP) with the 'Not stated' category from the Hours worked (HRSP) variable to provide more detailed information on employed persons." It is on the person record for 2011, 2016 and 2021, unchanged across all three, and it is the column to use when full-time and part-time shares need a denominator that does not silently include people whose hours are missing.
value_definition: Seven substantive codes: 1 employed worked full-time, 2 employed worked part-time, 3 employed away from work, 4 employed hours of work not stated, 5 unemployed looking for full-time work, 6 unemployed looking for part-time work and 7 not in the labour force, with & labour force status not stated, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor.
limitation: The codes do not line up with LFSP beside it. LFSP puts not in the labour force at 6 and unemployment at 4 and 5, while this column shifts them to 7 and 5 and 6, so recoding one to the other by number rather than by label produces a silently wrong result.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the applicable population, the full code list and the note that the variable was unchanged between 2011 and 2021, which matters because PLIDA carries all three Census years.
evidence_quote: This variable combines Labour force status (LFSP) with the 'Not stated' category from the Hours worked (HRSP) variable to provide more detailed information on employed persons.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Labour Force Status and Hours Worked Not Stated' and never warned that the code numbers differ from LFSP on the same row.

value_domain: Labour force status of parents and partners in families
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Labour force status of parents/partners in families (LFSF)
variable_description: The joint work situation of the adults heading this family, in one code. ABS defines it as recording "the labour force status of parents/partners in couple and lone parent families", so a couple family gets a combination such as both employed full-time or one employed and one not in the labour force, and a lone parent family gets that parent's status alone. It is on the family record for 2011, 2016 and 2021 and it is the family-level column behind jobless family counts.
value_definition: Twenty-nine categories: codes 01 to 21 for couple families covering every combination of the two adults' statuses, 22 to 27 for one parent families, 28 for other family, and @@ not applicable for non-family and non-classifiable households, unoccupied and non-private dwellings and migratory areas. Full-time is 35 hours or more in the week before Census night and part-time is less.
limitation: It covers only parents and partners, so an employed non-dependent child or other adult relative in the family does not change the code, and a family reading as jobless may still contain an earner. Away from work also absorbs people who worked zero hours or did not state hours, so it is not a clean count of people on leave.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the applicable population, the structure of the 29 categories, the full-time and part-time cut and the treatment of away from work and not stated.
evidence_quote: This variable records the labour force status of parents/partners in couple and lone parent families.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Labour Force Status of Parents/Partners in Families' and never said the code ignores other working adults in the family, which is what makes a jobless-family count from it an overstatement.

value_domain: Census labour force status classification
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Labour force status (LFSP)
variable_description: Whether the person was employed, unemployed or out of the labour force in the week before Census night. ABS defines it as recording "a person's labour force status for the week prior to Census Night", derived from five questions on work, hours, job search and availability to start. It is on the person record for 2011, 2016 and 2021, and it is the Census statement of employment to compare with employer-reported earnings in the STP and PIT products for the same person, which measure a different thing.
value_definition: Six substantive codes: 1 employed worked full-time, 2 employed worked part-time, 3 employed away from work, 4 unemployed looking for full-time work, 5 unemployed looking for part-time work and 6 not in the labour force, with & not stated, @ not applicable for people under 15 and V overseas visitor. Full-time is 35 hours or more in the reference week.
limitation: It is a single week and it applies the labour force test strictly, so a person who did any paid work at all is employed and someone who wanted work but did not actively look is not unemployed. Community Development Program participants are not counted as employed despite their activity, non-response was 5.8% in 2021, and the 2021 reference week fell during widespread COVID-19 lockdowns.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the applicable population, the full code list, the five source questions, the full-time threshold, the Community Development Program treatment and the non-response rate.
evidence_quote: This variable records a person's labour force status for the week prior to Census Night.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Labour Force Status' with no reference week, no full-time threshold and no mention of the 2021 lockdowns or the Community Development Program rule.

value_domain: ASGS Local Government Area code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Local Government Areas
variable_description: The council area the dwelling was enumerated in at the 2021 Census, expressed on the 2022 boundaries rather than the 2021 ones. ABS defines Local Government Areas as "an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory", reviewed and reissued each year. It sits on the 2021 dwelling record beside LGAD, which carries the same address on the 2021 edition, so the pair exists to let a user match either the Census-year boundaries or the later ones a council reports against today.
value_definition: A five-digit code: one digit for the state or territory and four for the LGA, all ending in zero, for example 54830 Kwinana. There were 567 Local Government Areas under ASGS Edition 3 covering all of Australia, including unincorporated areas and 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: The gain over LGAD is small and specific. ABS records only one boundary change between the 2021 and 2022 editions, an expansion of Palmerston in the Northern Territory into part of the adjacent Unincorporated NT area, with no code change and every other boundary and code held constant. The boundaries are also a Mesh Block approximation of the gazetted lines, not the lines themselves, so neither column reproduces a council's legal boundary.
rationale: The ASGS page gives the definition, the code structure, the count and the annual review cycle that produces the 2022 edition this column uses. The 2022 boundary year is taken from the custodian's own description of the column.
evidence_quote: Local Government Areas are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Local government areas (2022 boundaries) (en)' with 'not specified' as its domain, so nothing said what the code looks like or why the same table carries a second LGA column on 2021 boundaries.

value_domain: ASGS Local Government Area code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Local Government Areas
variable_description: The council area the dwelling was enumerated in at the 2021 Census, on the boundaries current in 2021. ABS defines Local Government Areas as "an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory." It is the boundary set the 2021 Census was published on, so this is the column to use when matching Census counts to ABS Census products; LGA22D beside it carries the same dwelling on the 2022 edition.
value_definition: A five-digit code: one digit for the state or territory and four for the LGA, all ending in zero. There were 567 Local Government Areas covering all of Australia, including unincorporated areas and 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: An LGA is an enumeration geography here, so it locates the dwelling and not the usual residence of the people in it; LGAP on the person record is the usual-residence version. Councils are also unequal in size, from a few hundred people to over a million, so an LGA average is not comparable across the classification.
rationale: The ASGS page gives the definition, the code structure, the count and the annual review cycle. The 2021 boundary year and the enumeration basis are taken from the custodian's own description of the column, read against the ABS place of enumeration and place of usual residence distinction.
evidence_quote: Local Government Areas are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Local government areas (2021 boundaries) (en)' with 'not specified' as its domain, and gave no code structure and no distinction from the person-level LGAP.

value_domain: ASGS Local Government Area code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Local Government Areas
variable_description: The council area of the person's usual residence at the 2021 Census, on the 2021 boundaries. ABS defines Local Government Areas as "an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory." It is the usual-residence counterpart of LGAD on the dwelling record, and it is the geography most council and state service catchments are defined on, which is what makes it the practical join for local-area analysis in PLIDA.
value_definition: A five-digit code: one digit for the state or territory and four for the LGA, all ending in zero. There were 567 Local Government Areas covering all of Australia, including unincorporated areas and 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: It is built up from Mesh Blocks, so it approximates the gazetted council boundary rather than reproducing it, and a dwelling near the edge can fall on the wrong side. Where usual residence was imputed, IFPURP on the same row shows at which level, and an LGA derived from an imputed SA1 is an assignment rather than a reported address.
rationale: The ASGS page gives the definition, the code structure, the count and the annual review cycle. The usual-residence reading of the '(ur)' suffix follows the ABS place of enumeration against place of usual residence distinction at https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/detailed-methodology-information/information-papers/comparing-place-enumeration-place-usual-residence and is inference.
evidence_quote: Local Government Areas are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Local government areas (2021 boundaries) (ur)' with 'not specified' as its domain, so a reader had neither the code shape nor the fact that it can rest on an imputed residence.

value_domain: ASGS local government area code (2022 boundaries)
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Non ABS Structures: Local Government Areas
variable_description: The council area a person usually lived in at the 2021 Census, on the 2022 vintage of ABS local government boundaries. These areas are built from mesh blocks rather than read off the statute book: the ABS calls them "an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory", so the value follows the mesh block held in MBUCP. LGAP on the same row is the same address on 2021 boundaries, and LGAU1P and LGAU5P are the person's earlier addresses, also on 2021 boundaries.
value_definition: A five-digit code made of a one-digit state or territory identifier and a four-digit area identifier that is unique within that state and always ends in zero, as in 54830 for Kwinana. Non-spatial codes sit alongside the real areas, with 9799 for migratory, offshore and shipping and 9499 for no usual address.
limitation: A code that differs between this column and LGAP, LGAU1P or LGAU5P is a boundary vintage difference, not a move. The gap between the two vintages is narrow: the ABS records one 2021 to 2022 boundary change, an expansion of Palmerston in the Northern Territory, and no code changes at all. Being a mesh block approximation, the column also cannot settle whether a given address falls inside a council's legal jurisdiction.
rationale: The ASGS Edition 3 page for local government areas defines the structure, states that it is a mesh block approximation of gazetted boundaries, gives the coding structure and lists the special purpose codes, which is exactly what the values in this column are.
evidence_quote: Local Government Areas are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording, 'Local government areas (2022 boundaries) (ur)', with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said the boundaries are ABS approximations or that the 2022 vintage differs from the 2021 vintage used by the columns beside it.

value_domain: ASGS local government area code (2021 boundaries), place of usual residence one year earlier
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence one year ago (PUR1P)
variable_description: The council area the person usually lived in one year before the 2021 Census, on 2021 local government boundaries. It is the address behind PUR1P coded to a local government area instead of the Statistical Area Level 2 the ABS uses as the base output; the dictionary defines the underlying variable as "the geographic area in which a person usually lived one year before the Census". Paired with LGAP or LGAP22 it answers whether the person changed council area over the year, and MBU1P holds the same earlier address at mesh block level.
value_definition: A five-digit local government area code on 2021 boundaries, one digit for state or territory and four for the area. Addresses that cannot be placed carry the ABS non-spatial codes instead: overseas, no usual address, migratory or offshore or shipping, an incomplete address coded only to a state, and not stated.
limitation: It records where the person said they lived, not the fact of a move, and it misses moves within a council area entirely, so a household that shifted three suburbs shows no change. The ABS reports a 6.0 per cent non-response rate for place of usual residence one year ago in 2021, and children under one year old are out of scope rather than stable.
rationale: The dictionary page for PUR1P defines the concept, the scope, the special purpose codes and the non-response rate, and the ASGS local government area page fixes the shape of the codes this column carries.
evidence_quote: This variable records the geographic area in which a person usually lived one year before the Census.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's title and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, giving no scope, no treatment of overseas or unplaceable addresses, and no warning that it is on a different boundary vintage from LGAP22.

value_domain: ASGS local government area code (2021 boundaries), place of usual residence five years earlier
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence five years ago (PUR5P)
variable_description: The council area the person usually lived in five years before the 2021 Census, that is on 10 August 2016, on 2021 local government boundaries. The ABS defines the parent variable as recording "the geographic area in which a person usually lived five years before the Census", and this column carries that address coded to a local government area rather than to the Statistical Area Level 2 used for standard output. Its one-year twin is LGAU1P, so the pair separates a recent move from a move earlier in the five-year window.
value_definition: A five-digit local government area code on 2021 boundaries, one digit for state or territory and four for the area. Addresses that cannot be placed carry the ABS non-spatial codes for overseas, no usual residence, migratory or offshore or shipping, state only, and not stated.
limitation: It is a snapshot of two dates, so it cannot count moves: a person who moved four times and returned looks identical to one who never moved. Scope excludes children under five, and the ABS reports a 6.9 per cent non-response rate for place of usual residence five years ago in 2021, against 6.0 per cent for the one-year version.
rationale: The dictionary page for PUR5P gives the definition, the five-year reference date, the scope and the non-response rate, and the ASGS page gives the code structure this column uses.
evidence_quote: This variable records the geographic area in which a person usually lived five years before the Census.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's title and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not say which two dates are compared or that under-fives are out of scope.

value_domain: Census landlord type code
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Landlord type (LLDD)
variable_description: Who the household rents the dwelling from, for dwellings that are rented. The ABS says the variable "records the landlord type of rented dwellings" and that "it applies to all occupied private dwellings that are being rented, including being occupied rent free", so it is TEND, the tenure type on the same row, that decides whether this column has a value at all. It is the column that separates public housing from community housing and from the private rental market, and TENLLD carries tenure and landlord as a single combined code.
value_definition: A two-digit code. The 2021 categories are 10 real estate agent, 20 state or territory housing authority, 21 community housing provider, 31 person not in the same household who is a parent or other relative, 32 other person not in the same household, 40 owner or manager of a residential park, 51 government employer including Defence Housing Australia and 52 other employer, with && not stated and @@ not applicable.
limitation: The category list is not stable across the three Census years in this dataset, so a code cannot be carried from the 2011 or 2016 table to the 2021 table without a concordance. Non-response is small, 0.9 per cent in 2021, but the not applicable group is large, because every owner-occupied, life-tenure, unoccupied and non-private dwelling falls into it.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the scope tied to tenure type, the full 2021 code list, the composition of the not applicable category and the non-response rate.
evidence_quote: This variable records the landlord type of rented dwellings. It applies to all occupied private dwellings that are being rented, including being occupied rent free.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Landlord Type' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that the column depends on TEND, that the codes change between Census years, or which dwellings are not applicable.

value_domain: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander language use indicator
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether reported using an Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander language at home (LNGP)
variable_description: A yes or no flag for whether the person reported using an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander language at home, which the ABS defines as indicating "whether a person reports using an Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander language at home". It is not asked directly: it is derived from LANP, the full language used at home classification on the same row, by collapsing every Australian Indigenous language to one category. It answers how many people use such a language, not which language, which stays in LANP.
value_definition: A single character: 1 for an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander language used at home, 2 for not used at home, & for not stated and V for overseas visitor. Four categories, all persons in scope.
limitation: It is not a measure of Indigenous status and must not be used as one. A non-Indigenous person living in a community can be coded 1, and most people coded as Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander in INGP are coded 2 because they speak English at home. The ABS also warns that the parent question takes only one answer, so the count in category 1 "is not all persons who speak an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander language"; non-response on that question was 5.7 per cent in 2021.
rationale: The dictionary page states the definition, the four categories, and that the variable is derived from Language used at home (LANP) with that question's non-response rate.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates whether a person reports using an Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander language at home.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long title as its description and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the column is derived from LANP or warned against reading it as an Indigenous status flag.

value_domain: Mortgage affordability indicator category
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Mortgage affordability indicator (MAID)
variable_description: Whether the household's mortgage repayments take more than 30 per cent of its income. The ABS builds it during processing by dividing MRED by a household income imputed from the personal income of each resident aged 15 and over, and it "allocates an in scope household to one of two categories: mortgage repayments less than or equal to 30% of household income" and "mortgage repayments more than 30% of household income". Only dwellings owned with a mortgage or bought under a shared equity scheme are in scope, so renters fall to not applicable and are covered by RAID instead.
value_definition: A single digit: 1 for repayments at or below 30 per cent of household income, 2 for above 30 per cent, 3 for unable to be determined and @ for not applicable. Four categories in all.
limitation: This is not the housing stress measure most analysts mean. The commonly used 30/40 rule counts only households in the lowest 40 per cent of the income distribution, whereas this column applies the 30 per cent test to every mortgaged household, so a high-income household with a large loan is counted the same way as a low-income one. Category 3 also hides the cases where income or repayments were not stated, and the ABS publishes no non-response rate because the variable is derived.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the two-way rule the indicator applies, its scope in tenure terms, the code list and the note that a derived variable has no non-response rate of its own.
evidence_quote: This variable allocates an in scope household to one of two categories: mortgage repayments less than or equal to 30% of household income
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Mortgage affordability indicator' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not give the 30 per cent threshold, the income denominator, or the difference from the 30/40 housing stress measure.

value_domain: ASGS mesh block code, place of usual residence one year earlier
value_source: ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Main Structure and Greater Capital City Statistical Areas: Mesh Blocks
variable_description: The mesh block containing the address the person usually lived at one year before the 2021 Census. This is finer than anything the ABS publishes for that concept: standard output for place of usual residence one year ago stops at Statistical Area Level 2, while mesh blocks are "the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS" and are designed to hold between 30 and 60 dwellings. Compared with MBUCP, the mesh block of usual residence at the Census, it is the sharpest available test of whether a person moved during the year.
value_definition: An 11-digit code, one digit for the state or territory and ten for the mesh block, as in 60106840000. ASGS Edition 3 holds 368,286 mesh blocks including 114 non-spatial codes for migratory, offshore, shipping and no usual address populations.
limitation: A shared mesh block is not a shared address and certainly not a shared household, since 30 to 60 dwellings sit inside a typical one. The mesh block also cannot be compared like for like against a 2016 Census mesh block, because Edition 3 retired and reissued codes wherever a 2016 mesh block was split or redesigned.
rationale: The ASGS mesh block page defines the unit, its dwelling target, its 11-digit coding structure and the recoding between editions, which fixes what the values are; the mesh block level of output for a one-year-ago address is specific to the integrated asset rather than to published Census products.
evidence_quote: The 11-digit Mesh Block code comprises: State and Territory identifier (1 digit), and a Mesh Block identifier (10 digits).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Meshblock (place of usual residence 1 year ago)' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it gave no code shape, no sense of how small a mesh block is, and no warning about comparing codes across ASGS editions.

value_domain: ASGS mesh block code, place of usual residence five years earlier
value_source: ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Main Structure and Greater Capital City Statistical Areas: Mesh Blocks
variable_description: The mesh block containing the address the person usually lived at five years before the 2021 Census, that is on 10 August 2016. Mesh blocks are "the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS" and most hold 30 to 60 dwellings, so this column places a five-year-old address far more precisely than PUR5P, which the ABS outputs at Statistical Area Level 2. Set against MBUCP it gives a five-year migration origin and destination at the finest ASGS level, and MBU1P narrows the same question to the last year.
value_definition: An 11-digit code, one digit for the state or territory and ten for the mesh block. ASGS Edition 3 holds 368,286 mesh blocks including 114 non-spatial codes covering migratory, offshore, shipping and no usual address.
limitation: The code stands for the address the person reported for 2016, not for a residence history, so anyone who moved and returned inside the five years is indistinguishable from someone who stayed put. Children under five are out of scope, which removes exactly the group whose families move most often.
rationale: The ASGS mesh block page defines the unit, its size and its coding structure; the five-year reference date and the under-five exclusion come from the dictionary page for the parent variable PUR5P.
evidence_quote: Mesh Blocks are the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS and form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS).
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's title and the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, leaving no code shape, no reference date and no scope.

value_domain: ASGS mesh block code, place of enumeration
value_source: ABS, Census geography glossary, 2021 Census
variable_description: The mesh block where the dwelling stood and where the people in it were counted on Census night. The ABS calls this basis place of enumeration, "where a person was on Census night", as distinct from place of usual residence; on the person table it therefore differs from MBUCP for anyone who was away from home. Because it appears on the dwelling, family and person tables it is the common small-area key that joins a household record to the people counted in it.
value_definition: An 11-digit code, one digit for the state or territory and ten for the mesh block. Mesh blocks are the smallest ASGS unit, most containing 30 to 60 dwellings, with non-spatial codes for migratory, offshore, shipping and no usual address.
limitation: Counts built on it are Census-night counts, so a coastal town in August or a hospital ward carries visitors and patients who live elsewhere; use MBUCP when the question is about residents. It is also not a dwelling identifier, since many dwellings share a mesh block, and DWELLING_ID is the column that separates them.
rationale: The Census geography glossary defines mesh blocks and states the difference between place of enumeration, place of usual residence and place of work, which is what the (en) suffix on this column means.
evidence_quote: Place of enumeration – where a person was on Census night
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Meshblock (en)' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader had no way to know that (en) means Census night location rather than usual residence.

value_domain: ASGS mesh block code, place of usual residence
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence (PURP)
variable_description: The mesh block a person usually lived in at the 2021 Census. The ABS treats the mesh block as the base unit for that concept: place of usual residence "records the geographic area in which a person usually lives", "may or may not be the place where the person was counted on Census Night", and its base area "is a mesh block (MB)". SA1UCP, SA2UCP, SA3UCP, SA4UCP, LGAP and STEUCP on the same row are this mesh block rolled up, and MBUCD is the mesh block the person was actually counted in.
value_definition: An 11-digit code, one digit for the state or territory and ten for the mesh block, drawn from the 368,286 mesh blocks in ASGS Edition 3, plus non-spatial codes for migratory, offshore, shipping and no usual address.
limitation: Where the address written on the form was incomplete, the ABS imputes usual residence at whatever geographic level the response supports, so a mesh block can be an imputed allocation rather than a reported one; IFPURP on the same row is the flag that says which. The ABS reports a 4.3 per cent non-response rate at Statistical Area Level 2 in 2021, and the rate at mesh block level is necessarily higher.
