rationale: The dictionary page for PURP names the mesh block as the base area for place of usual residence, separates it from place of enumeration, and documents the imputation and its flag.
evidence_quote: This variable records the geographic area in which a person usually lives. It may or may not be the place where the person was counted on Census Night. The base area for Place of usual residence (PURP) is a mesh block (MB).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Meshblock (ur)' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not distinguish usual residence from enumeration or mention that incomplete addresses are imputed.

value_domain: Social marital status category
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Social marital status (MDCP)
variable_description: Whether the person is living with a partner, and whether that partnership is a registered marriage or a de facto one. The ABS defines it as recording "a person's relationship status based on their current living arrangements" and identifying "whether they form a couple relationship with another person living in the same usual residence". It is derived from the household relationship grid rather than asked, which is what separates it from MSTP, the legal marital status on the same row.
value_definition: A single digit: 1 married in a registered marriage, 2 married in a de facto marriage, 3 not married, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor. Five categories, for persons aged 15 and over who were usually resident and present in the household on Census night.
limitation: A couple who live apart cannot be seen, because the partner has to be in the same dwelling for the relationship to be coded, so partners separated by work, illness or aged care are all coded 'not married'. Everyone in a non-private dwelling, every visitor and every person in a non-classifiable household is not applicable, which removes prisons, hospitals and aged care from any analysis built on this column.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the three substantive categories with their own definitions, the scope restricted to usual residents present on the night, and the full composition of the not applicable category.
evidence_quote: This variable records a person's relationship status based on their current living arrangements. It identifies whether they form a couple relationship with another person living in the same usual residence, and the nature of that relationship.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Social Marital Status' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which left the reader unable to tell it apart from MSTP or to know that couples living apart are invisible.

value_domain: Monthly mortgage repayment in whole dollars
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Mortgage repayments (monthly) dollar values (MRED)
variable_description: The dollar amount the household reported paying each month on the mortgage for the dwelling it was counted in. The ABS defines it as "the monthly mortgage repayments being paid by a household for the dwelling in which they were counted on Census Night", collected "in single dollar values", which makes it the continuous version of MRERD, the banded column beside it. It is also the numerator behind MAID, the affordability indicator, whose denominator is a household income the ABS imputes from personal income responses rather than HIND.
value_definition: A four-character field holding a whole dollar amount from 0000 to 9999, with &&&& for not stated and @@@@ for not applicable, giving 10,002 categories in 2021.
limitation: It measures the payment, not the debt, so it says nothing about the loan balance, the interest rate or how much equity the household holds, and a household paying extra to get ahead looks identical to one on a larger loan. The range stops at $9,999 a month, so the top of the distribution is not resolved, and the not stated rate rose to 6.0 per cent in 2021 from 4.2 per cent in 2016.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the single dollar collection, the code range, the category count and the change in non-response between 2016 and 2021.
evidence_quote: This variable records the monthly mortgage repayments being paid by a household for the dwelling in which they were counted on Census Night.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Mortgage Repayments (monthly) Dollar Values' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that the field is capped at $9,999, that it is a monthly figure, or that it feeds MAID.

value_domain: Monthly mortgage repayment range code
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Mortgage repayments (monthly) ranges (MRERD)
variable_description: The household's monthly mortgage repayment placed in a dollar band. The ABS defines it as recording "the mortgage repayments being paid by a household in ranges" and derives it from MRED, the single-dollar column on the same row, because the bands are what standard Census products such as QuickStats and Community Profiles publish. Scope is dwellings owned with a mortgage or purchased under a shared equity scheme, so owner-occupiers without a loan and renters are not applicable.
value_definition: A two-digit code from 01 to 21, running 01 nil repayments, 02 $1 to $149, then bands that widen with the amount: $150 wide to $599, $200 wide to $2,999, $500 wide to $3,999, 20 for $4,000 to $4,999 and 21 for $5,000 and over, with && not stated and @@ not applicable. Twenty-three categories in 2021.
limitation: The bands are nominal dollars fixed for each Census, so the same code buys progressively less housing over time and a shift up the scale between 2011 and 2021 is partly price inflation rather than a real change in burden. Because the column is derived from MRED, using both in one model double counts the same response.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, states that the ranges are a recode of MRED for standard products, and lists all 21 bands with the supplementary codes.
evidence_quote: This variable records the mortgage repayments being paid by a household in ranges.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Mortgage Repayments (monthly) Ranges' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not give the bands, the open top band, or the fact that it is a recode of MRED.

value_domain: Registered marital status category
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Registered marital status (MSTP)
variable_description: The person's legal marital status, as registered, regardless of who they live with. The ABS defines it as recording "a person's formal registered marital status" and adds that "if registered marital status is not stated, it is imputed", which is why the column has no not stated category. It is the legal counterpart to MDCP, the living-arrangements measure on the same row, and IFMSTP flags which records were imputed.
value_definition: A single digit: 1 never married, 2 widowed, 3 divorced, 4 separated and 5 married, with @ for persons aged under 15. Six categories, all persons aged 15 and over in scope.
limitation: It cannot identify couples. A person living with a de facto partner is coded by their registered status, so most de facto partners appear as 'never married' and only MDCP will find them. Because non-response is imputed from other form information and a population distribution, the column also looks complete when 5.5 per cent of 2021 records were in fact filled in by the ABS.
rationale: The dictionary page defines the variable, states that non-response is imputed, names the imputation flag IFMSTP, gives the imputation rate for 2021 and 2016, and lists the five categories.
evidence_quote: This variable records a person's formal registered marital status. If registered marital status is not stated, it is imputed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Registered Marital Status' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never warned that the values are imputed where the question was skipped, nor that de facto partners are invisible here.

value_domain: Method of travel to work, six-mode grouping
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Method of travel to work (6 travel modes) (MTW06P)
variable_description: How the person got to work on Census day, collapsed to six broad modes. The ABS says it "records the method of travel to work in six modes on Census day 10 August 2021" and that the "data is derived from the Method of travel to work (MTWP) variable", which holds up to three modes per person. It exists so that the hundreds of MTWP combinations can be tabulated, and MTW15P sits between the two at fifteen modes.
value_definition: A single digit: 1 public transport, 2 vehicle, 3 active transport, 4 other mode, 5 worked at home or did not go to work, 6 not stated, with @ for not applicable and V for overseas visitor. Eight categories.
limitation: It cannot measure working from home, because category 5 merges people who worked at home with people who did not go to work at all. That is a serious trap for 2021, when much of New South Wales, Victoria and the ACT was in lockdown on Census day; MTW15P separates the two as codes 13 and 14.
rationale: The dictionary page states the six-mode derivation from MTWP, gives the code list including the merged 'worked at home or did not go to work' category, and defines the scope and supplementary codes.
evidence_quote: This variable records the method of travel to work in six modes on Census day 10 August 2021. Data is derived from the Method of travel to work ( MTWP ) variable.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's title and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, hiding the one thing a 2021 user most needs to know, that working at home is not separable in this column.

value_domain: Method of travel to work, fifteen-mode grouping
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Method of travel to work (15 travel modes) (MTW15P)
variable_description: How the person got to work on Census day, reduced to a single mode from a list of fifteen. The ABS describes it as recording "the method of travel to work in 15 travel modes on Census day 10 August 2021", derived from MTWP, and it is the column to use when working at home matters, because code 13 is worked at home and code 14 is did not go to work. It keeps train, bus, ferry and tram apart where MTW06P lumps them into public transport.
value_definition: A two-digit code from 01 to 15: 01 train, 02 bus, 03 ferry, 04 tram or light rail, 05 taxi or ride-share, 06 car as driver, 07 car as passenger, 08 truck, 09 motorbike or scooter, 10 bicycle, 11 other mode, 12 walked only, 13 worked at home, 14 did not go to work, 15 not stated, plus @@ not applicable and VV overseas visitor.
limitation: One person gets one mode, so a journey made by train and then bus is reduced to a single code and the connecting legs disappear; MTWP is the column that keeps up to three modes together. It also describes one day only, so a person who normally drives but walked on 10 August 2021 is a walker in this data.
rationale: The dictionary page defines the variable, states that it derives from MTWP, and lists all fifteen modes with the supplementary codes and the not applicable population.
evidence_quote: These variables record the method of travel to work in 15 travel modes on Census day 10 August 2021. Data is derived from the Method of travel to work MTWP variable.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's title and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not list the modes or explain how the column relates to MTWP and MTW06P.

value_domain: Method of travel to work, up to three modes combined
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Method of travel to work (MTWP)
variable_description: The full combination of ways the person travelled to work on Census day, holding up to three modes in a single code. The ABS defines it as recording "up to three methods, or means, of travel to work on the day of the Census, for each person aged 15 years and over who was employed during the week before the Census", and notes that multiple responses are allowed for every category except walked only, worked at home and did not go to work. MTW15P and MTW06P are the flattened versions of this column.
value_definition: A three-digit code standing for a whole combination, not a single mode: 001 is train alone, 012 is train and bus, 067 is train, bus and ferry, and so on across several hundred combinations grouped under headings such as public transport and vehicle.
limitation: The code is a set, not a route. It does not say which leg was longest, which came first, or how far the person travelled, so any notion of a main mode has to be imposed by the analyst rather than read off. Only 0.5 per cent of 2021 records are not stated, but that figure is calculated on employed persons alone, since everyone else is not applicable.
rationale: The dictionary page defines the three-mode structure, explains which categories cannot be combined, publishes the combination code list and gives the non-response rate against the employed population.
evidence_quote: This variable records up to three methods, or means, of travel to work on the day of the Census, for each person aged 15 years and over who was employed during the week before the Census.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Method of Travel to Work' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader would assume the code was a single mode rather than a combination of up to three.

value_domain: Household one-year mobility category
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Household one year mobility indicator (MV1D)
variable_description: Whether all, some or none of the household's residents were living somewhere else a year earlier. The ABS defines it as indicating "if all, some, or none of the usual residents of a household on 10 August 2021 have a different usual address compared to one year earlier", built up from each resident's PUR1P response. It is the household-level summary of what MBU1P and LGAU1P record person by person, and MV5D asks the same question over five years.
value_definition: A single character: 1 all residents aged one year and over had a different address a year ago, 2 some did, 3 none did, & at least one resident did not state an address a year ago, and @ not applicable. Five categories.
limitation: It says nothing about where anyone came from or how far they moved, so a household that moved next door and one that moved interstate both read as code 1. Persons temporarily absent and visitors are excluded from the calculation, so a household of two where one member was away on Census night is classified on the remaining person alone.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition with both reference dates, states which persons are excluded, lists the five categories and reports the 1.9 per cent non-response rate for 2021.
evidence_quote: This derived variable indicates if all, some, or none of the usual residents of a household on 10 August 2021 have a different usual address compared to one year earlier (i.e. 10 August 2020).
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Household One Year Mobility Indicator' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the two dates compared, that visitors and absent residents are excluded, or what 'some' means.

value_domain: Household five-year mobility category
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Household five year mobility indicator (MV5D)
variable_description: Whether all, some or none of the household's residents were living somewhere else five years earlier. The ABS defines it as indicating "if all, some, or none of the usual residents of a household on 10 August 2021 have a different usual address compared to five years earlier (i.e. 10 August 2016)", and it is derived from each resident's PUR5P answer. Read with MV1D it separates a household that has just arrived from one that settled some years ago.
value_definition: A single character: 1 all residents aged five years and over had a different address five years ago, 2 some did, 3 none did, & at least one resident did not state an address five years ago, and @ not applicable. Five categories.
limitation: Only residents aged five and over count towards it, so children born since the last Census neither create nor prevent a 'some' classification, and a family that moved together but has a new baby still reads as code 1. Non-response is higher than for the one-year version, 2.5 per cent in 2021, because a single resident who could not recall a 2016 address sends the whole household to the & category.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition with both dates, the exclusions, the code list and the non-response rate, and explains that a household counts as non-responding if any one resident did not state an address.
evidence_quote: This derived variable indicates if all, some, or none of the usual residents of a household on 10 August 2021 have a different usual address compared to five years earlier (i.e. 10 August 2016).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's title with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not explain the age floor, the exclusions, or how one resident's missing answer classifies the household.

value_domain: Dwelling internet access indicator
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), NEDD Dwelling Internet Connection
variable_description: Whether anyone in the household got online from the dwelling. The 2016 dictionary defines the variable as recording "whether any member of the household accesses the internet from the dwelling", counting access "through a desktop/laptop computer, mobile or smart phone, tablet, music or video player, gaming console, smart TV or any other devices" and "through any type of connection for example ADSL, fibre, cable, wireless, satellite and mobile broadband (3G/4G)". It is a household-level column on occupied private dwellings and it stops after 2016, because the question was dropped from the 2021 Census.
value_definition: A single character: 1 internet accessed from dwelling, 2 internet not accessed from dwelling, & not stated, @ not applicable. Four categories, applicable to occupied private dwellings only.
limitation: It cannot tell you anything about the quality of the connection. A household sharing one phone on mobile broadband and a household on fibre are both code 1, so the column will not support any statement about broadband speed, NBN rollout or data allowance. It is also absent from the 2021 dwelling table, so a series built on it ends at 2016.
rationale: The archived 2016 Census Dictionary page for NEDD gives the definition, the devices and connection types in scope, the applicable population and the full category list.
evidence_quote: Records whether any member of the household accesses the internet from the dwelling.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Dwelling Internet Connection' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which invited the reading that the column records connection type when it records only whether the internet was accessed at all.

value_domain: Type of non-private dwelling code
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Type of non-private dwelling (NPDD)
variable_description: What kind of communal establishment the people on this record were counted in. The ABS defines the variable as classifying "the Type of non-private dwelling in which people were counted on Census Night" and describes non-private dwellings as "establishments which provide a communal and often short-term type of accommodation". Unusually for a Census variable it is not a form response at all: the ABS sources it from the Address Register, which is the same register behind ARID in the Core module, so it carries no non-response rate.
value_definition: A two-digit code from 01 to 20 covering hotels and motels, nurses' and staff quarters, boarding houses, boarding schools, residential colleges, public, private and psychiatric hospitals, hostels for people with disability, nursing homes, aged accommodation, homelessness hostels and refuges, child care and corrective institutions for children, other welfare institutions, prisons, immigration detention, convents, and other and non-classifiable, with && not stated and @@ not applicable.
limitation: It describes the establishment, not the person's circumstances or their usual home, so a tourist in a hotel, a prisoner and a permanent aged care resident are only distinguished by the establishment type, and a stay of one night looks the same as a stay of ten years. Everyone counted in a non-private dwelling is also not applicable on most household variables, including LLDD, MAID and MDCP, so those columns are empty rather than zero for this population.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition of the variable and of non-private dwellings, the full 20-category list, and the statement that the variable comes from the ABS Address Register rather than from a Census question.
evidence_quote: This variable classifies the Type of non-private dwelling in which people were counted on Census Night. Non-private dwellings (NPDs) are establishments which provide a communal and often short-term type of accommodation.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Type of Non-Private Dwelling' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it neither listed the establishment types nor recorded that the column is sourced from the Address Register.

value_domain: Count of usual residents in dwelling
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of persons usually resident in dwelling (NPRD)
variable_description: How many people usually live in this occupied private dwelling. The ABS defines it as counting "the number of people who usually reside in an occupied private dwelling" and adds that "it includes up to three residents who were temporarily absent from the household on Census Night", so it is a usual-residence count rather than a count of who was present. It is the denominator behind household measures such as HOSD housing suitability and HIED equivalised household income, and CPAD records how many residents were absent.
value_definition: A single digit from 1 to 8, where 8 means eight or more persons, with @ for not applicable. Nine categories, applicable to occupied private dwellings.
limitation: Large households cannot be sized, because eight is a ceiling rather than a count, which matters most in remote and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities where the largest households are. The rule that only three absent residents can be added also means a household with four or more members away on Census night is recorded as smaller than it is.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the three-absentee rule, the top-coded category list and the note that the variable is derived and so carries no non-response rate.
evidence_quote: This variable counts the number of people who usually reside in an occupied private dwelling. It includes up to three residents who were temporarily absent from the household on Census Night.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Number of Persons Usually Resident in Dwelling' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not disclose the top code at eight or the limit of three temporarily absent residents.

value_domain: Natural resource management region code, place of enumeration
value_source: ABS, Census geography glossary, 2021 Census
variable_description: The environmental management region containing the dwelling where the household was counted on Census night. The ABS explains that these regions "are based on catchments or bioregions", that "the Australian government, in association with state and territory governments, has identified 56 regions covering all of Australia", and that they exist "to administer and report on aspects of environmental policy including sustainable farming and biodiversity". The (en) suffix marks it as place of enumeration, so NRMRP is the matching column for a person's usual residence.
value_definition: A code identifying one of the 56 natural resource management regions covering Australia, approximated by the ABS from mesh blocks so that Census counts can be reported on catchment and bioregion boundaries.
limitation: These are not statistical regions and were dropped from the standard geography: the ABS states that "Natural Resource Management Regions are no longer included in Non ABS Structures as they were found to be rarely used", so no maintained correspondence exists between them and the SA and LGA structures. They also cut across councils and statistical areas, which makes any join to administrative data approximate.
rationale: The Census geography glossary defines the regions and their purpose for 2021 Census output, and the ASGS Edition 3 Non ABS Structures page records that they were removed from the standard, which together fix both what the codes mean and how far they can be relied on.
evidence_quote: Natural Resource Management Regions (NRMRs) are based on catchments or bioregions. The Australian government, in association with state and territory governments, has identified 56 regions covering all of Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Natural resource management regions (en)' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it gave neither the purpose of the regions, the number of them, nor the fact that ABS has stopped publishing them as a standard structure.

value_domain: Natural resource management region code, place of usual residence
value_source: ABS, Census geography glossary, 2021 Census
variable_description: The environmental management region containing the address where the person usually lives. The ABS says these regions "are based on catchments or bioregions" and that 56 of them cover all of Australia, used "to administer and report on aspects of environmental policy including sustainable farming and biodiversity". Because it is coded on usual residence rather than Census-night location, it is the column to use when the question is about the resident population of a catchment, and NRMRD gives the enumeration-based equivalent on the dwelling table.
value_definition: A code identifying one of the 56 natural resource management regions covering Australia, allocated from the person's usual residence mesh block in MBUCP.
limitation: The region tells you nothing about the person's relationship to the land or water it manages, so a city dweller inside a catchment carries the same code as a farmer on an irrigated property. The ABS has also retired these regions from the standard geography, so their boundaries are not maintained alongside the ASGS structures a user would otherwise join to.
rationale: The Census geography glossary defines these regions for 2021 Census output and separately defines place of usual residence as the coding basis marked by the (ur) suffix.
evidence_quote: They are used to administer and report on aspects of environmental policy including sustainable farming and biodiversity.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Natural resource management regions (ur)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not explain what the regions are for or that (ur) means the person's usual residence rather than where they were counted.

value_domain: ANZSCO 2021 Australian Update occupation code
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Occupation experimental update version 1 (OCCEV1P)
variable_description: The person's main job coded to the experimental 2021 Australian update of ANZSCO rather than to the standard classification. The ABS describes the update as "a targeted update limited to occupations relating to agriculture, cyber security, naval ship building and emerging occupations" that "relates to the Australian labour market only". OCCP on the same row holds the same job coded to ANZSCO 2013 Version 1.3, and OCSKEV1P holds the skill level implied by this column.
value_definition: A six-digit hierarchical code from ANZSCO 2021 Australian Update, nesting one-digit major groups inside two-digit sub-major, three-digit minor and four-digit unit groups, with 'nfd' codes where a response supports only a broader level, plus supplementary codes for inadequately described, not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor.
limitation: It is not comparable with OCCP beside it or with occupation in the 2011 and 2016 tables, because only part of the classification was rebuilt, so differences between the two columns are classification artefacts in the updated areas and nothing at all elsewhere. Being flagged experimental, it is also not a series the ABS supports for time comparison.
rationale: The dictionary page states which parts of ANZSCO the experimental update covers, names the classification version, publishes the code list and reports the 0.8 per cent non-response rate for 2021.
evidence_quote: This was a targeted update limited to occupations relating to agriculture, cyber security, naval ship building and emerging occupations and relates to the Australian labour market only.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Occupation experimental update version 1' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say which classification is behind it, what the update covered, or that it cannot be compared with OCCP.

value_domain: ANZSCO 2013 Version 1.3 occupation code
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Occupation (OCCP)
variable_description: The job the person held in the week before Census night, coded to ANZSCO. The ABS defines it as describing "the primary job or occupation held by employed people in the week prior to Census Night", coded using the Australian and New Zealand Standard Classification of Occupations 2013 Version 1.3 and available to the six-digit level. It is derived from the written occupation title and duties on the form, and INDP holds the industry of the same job while OCSKP holds its skill level.
value_definition: A six-digit hierarchical ANZSCO code, with 8 major groups at one digit, 51 sub-major at two, 134 minor at three, 478 unit groups at four and 1,357 occupations at six. Supplementary codes are 099888 inadequately described, &&&&&& not stated, @@@@@@ not applicable and VVVVVV overseas visitor.
limitation: Only the main job is coded, so a person with two jobs contributes one occupation and multiple job holding cannot be measured here. The not applicable group is also not a residual of interest: it holds everyone unemployed, out of the labour force, under 15 or with labour force status not stated, so an empty value means 'not employed' rather than 'occupation unknown'.
rationale: The dictionary page names the classification and version, gives the counts of categories at each digit level, lists the supplementary codes, defines the not applicable population and reports the 0.8 per cent non-response rate.
evidence_quote: This variable describes the primary job or occupation held by employed people in the week prior to Census Night.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the single word 'Occupation' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it named neither ANZSCO nor its version, and did not say that only the main job is captured.

value_domain: ANZSCO skill level, 2021 Australian Update basis
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Occupation skill level experimental update version 1 (OCSKEV1P)
variable_description: The ANZSCO skill level attached to the person's job, taken from the experimental 2021 Australian update of the classification. The ABS is explicit that "the skill level is set by the person's occupation (OCCP), rather than the skill level of the person themselves", and that this version "has been created based on the ANZSCO - Australian and New Zealand Standard Classification of Occupations, 2021 Australian Update". It is the companion of OCCEV1P in the way OCSKP is the companion of OCCP.
value_definition: A single digit from 1 to 5, where 1 is the highest skill level and 5 the lowest, with 9 for skill level not determined, & not stated, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor. Nine categories.
limitation: It measures the job, not the worker, so a person with a degree working in a skill level five job is coded 5 and this column cannot stand in for education; QALLP and HEAP hold the person's own qualifications. It also cannot be compared with OCSKP on the same row, because the two are built from different versions of ANZSCO.
rationale: The dictionary page states that the skill level comes from the occupation rather than the person, names the classification update it rests on, and lists the nine categories with the not applicable population.
evidence_quote: The skill level is set by the person's occupation ( OCCP ), rather than the skill level of the person themselves.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Occupation skill level experimental update version 1' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which left open the common misreading that the column measures the worker's skill.

value_domain: ANZSCO skill level, 2013 Version 1.3 basis
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Occupation skill level (OCSKP)
variable_description: The ANZSCO skill level of the job recorded in OCCP, on a five-point scale where one is highest. The ABS states that "the skill level is determined from the characteristics of the person's occupation (OCCP), rather than the skill level of the person themselves", so it is a property of the job title, assigned by the classification, not an assessment of the individual. It is a direct recode of OCCP and carries that variable's 0.8 per cent non-response.
value_definition: A single digit from 1 to 5, with 1 the highest and 5 the lowest skill level, plus 9 skill level not determined, & not stated, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor. Nine categories, employed persons aged 15 and over.
limitation: Because every person in a given ANZSCO unit group gets the same value, the column carries no within-occupation variation at all: two nurses on very different duties and pay are both skill level one. Reading a fall in skill level as deskilling of workers is therefore wrong; it reflects a change in the mix of jobs held.
rationale: The dictionary page defines the scale, states plainly that the skill level comes from the occupation rather than the person, lists the categories and gives the non-response rate inherited from OCCP.
evidence_quote: The skill level is determined from the characteristics of the person's occupation (OCCP) , rather than the skill level of the person themselves.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Occupation skill level' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying which direction of the scale is high or that the value is a property of the occupation.

value_domain: Primary health network region code, place of enumeration
value_source: ABS, Census geography glossary, 2021 Census
variable_description: The primary health network region containing the dwelling where the household was counted on Census night. The ABS defines these as "administrative health regions established to deliver primary care services for patients, as well as coordinate with local hospitals to improve the overall operational efficiency of the network". The (en) suffix marks the coding basis as place of enumeration, and PHNP is the equivalent coded on usual residence. It is the natural join key for linking Census characteristics to MBS, PBS and hospital data reported by network.
value_definition: A code identifying one primary health network, approximated from mesh blocks. The ABS notes two vintages in Census output: "The 2017 PHNs are based on Mesh Block (MB) 2016 boundaries" and the 2023 networks added in August 2024 are based on 2021 mesh blocks.
limitation: A network is a planning region, not a catchment of care, so it does not tell you where the household actually saw a doctor; patients cross network boundaries routinely, particularly near capital city edges. The column also does not state which boundary vintage it carries, so the 2017 and 2023 definitions have to be told apart from the extract documentation rather than from the data.
rationale: The Census geography glossary defines primary health networks for 2021 Census output, names both boundary vintages with the mesh block edition each rests on, and defines the place of enumeration basis marked by the (en) suffix.
evidence_quote: Primary Health Networks (PHNs) are administrative health regions established to deliver primary care services for patients, as well as coordinate with local hospitals to improve the overall operational efficiency of the network.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Primary health networks (en)' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say what a network is, that two boundary vintages exist, or that (en) means Census-night location.

value_domain: Primary health network region code, place of usual residence
value_source: ABS, Census geography glossary, 2021 Census
variable_description: The primary health network region covering the address where the person usually lives. The ABS defines these regions as "administrative health regions established to deliver primary care services for patients, as well as coordinate with local hospitals", and the (ur) suffix means the code is allocated from usual residence rather than from where the person spent Census night. That makes it the right column for building a resident population denominator for network-level health statistics, with PHND the enumeration-based version on the dwelling table.
value_definition: A code identifying one primary health network, approximated from mesh blocks. The 2017 networks in Census output are built on 2016 mesh blocks and the 2023 networks, added to Census TableBuilder in August 2024, are built on 2021 mesh blocks.
limitation: It records where the person lives, not which network funded their care, so it cannot be used to attribute a service to a network without the service's own location. Because the regions are approximated from mesh blocks, they also do not follow the exact administrative boundaries the health portfolio publishes.
rationale: The Census geography glossary defines primary health networks, records both boundary vintages available for 2021 Census data, and defines place of usual residence as the coding basis for a (ur) column.
evidence_quote: The 2017 PHNs are based on Mesh Block (MB) 2016 boundaries.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Primary health networks (ur)' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it explained neither the purpose of the regions nor the difference between the (ur) and (en) versions.

value_domain: ASGS postal area code, place of enumeration
value_source: ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Non ABS Structures: Postal Areas
variable_description: The postal area containing the dwelling where the household was counted on Census night. A postal area is not a postcode: the ABS builds it as "an ABS Mesh Block approximation of a general definition of postcodes" so that Census data can be lined up with records collected by postcode. It appears on the dwelling and family tables, with POAP giving the same approximation on a person's usual residence.
value_definition: A four-digit code that matches a postcode number where one exists. ASGS Edition 3 defines 2,644 postal areas covering Australia without gaps or overlaps, including three non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: Joining an external postcode-coded file to it will lose and misplace records. The ABS excludes post office box, mail-back and other non-street-delivery postcodes entirely, allocates each mesh block to a single postal area on population share where a mesh block spans two postcodes, and a handful of areas cross state borders, among them 0872, 2540, 2611, 2620, 2618, 2406 and 3707.
rationale: The ASGS Edition 3 postal areas page gives the definition, the count of areas, the allocation rule, the excluded postcode types and the list of cross-border postal areas.
evidence_quote: Postal Areas are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of a general definition of postcodes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Postal areas (en)' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader would treat the value as a postcode and would not know which postcodes have no postal area at all.

value_domain: ASGS postal area code, place of usual residence
value_source: ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Non ABS Structures: Postal Areas
variable_description: The postal area covering the address where the person usually lives. It is an approximation rather than the postcode itself: the ABS builds it as "an ABS Mesh Block approximation of a general definition of postcodes" and warns that "ABS approximations of administrative boundaries do not match official legal boundaries and should only be used for statistical purposes". It is derived from MBUCP, the usual-residence mesh block, and is the practical bridge from Census characteristics to any administrative file that only records a postcode.
value_definition: A four-digit code matching a postcode number where one exists, drawn from the 2,644 postal areas in ASGS Edition 3, which include three non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: Postal area boundaries are frozen for the life of an ASGS edition, so a postcode that Australia Post changes between 2021 and 2026 will not be reflected here and a join to recent administrative data will drift. Postal areas are also far larger than a mesh block, so two people sharing a code can live 50 kilometres apart in rural Australia.
rationale: The ASGS Edition 3 postal areas page defines the structure, warns that ABS approximations do not match official legal boundaries, and records that postcode changes will not be reflected until ASGS Edition 4 in 2026.
evidence_quote: ABS approximations of administrative boundaries do not match official legal boundaries and should only be used for statistical purposes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Postal areas (ur)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not warn that the value approximates a postcode or that the boundaries are frozen between ASGS editions.

value_domain: ASGS Australia code, place of work
value_source: ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Main Structure: Australia and State/Territory
variable_description: The top of the place-of-work geography hierarchy: whether the person's reported workplace fell inside Australia. The ABS gives geographic Australia the alpha code AUS in ASGS Edition 3, noting that this "replaces the three-digit numeric code of 036 (also ISO 3166 standard) as used in ASGS 2016", and workplaces that cannot be placed in Australia take the Outside Australia special purpose code. Everything from POWSTE down to POWDZN is a finer cut of this same workplace address.
value_definition: A short alpha code for Australia, AUS in ASGS Edition 3, sitting alongside the Outside Australia special purpose code, which the ABS says "does not have a geographic region and has a code of 'ZZZZ' so that it can be easily distinguished from all other geographies".
limitation: An empty or not applicable value almost always means the person was not employed, not that they worked overseas: everyone unemployed, out of the labour force, aged under 15 or with labour force status not stated is out of scope for place of work. The ABS also warns that during the 2021 lockdowns "people may have put their home address as the workplace address despite instructions", so home-based work can appear as a workplace location.
rationale: The ASGS Australia and State/Territory page gives the code for geographic Australia and the special purpose codes page gives the Outside Australia code, while the dictionary page for POWP gives the scope and the lockdown warning that make the column readable.
evidence_quote: the ASGS Edition 3 code for Geographic Australia is identified by the unique three-character alpha code of AUS
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the bare custodian wording 'Australia (pow)' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the column is a place-of-work flag whose blank values mean 'not employed'.

value_domain: ASGS destination zone code, place of work
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of work (POWP)
variable_description: The destination zone the person's workplace address was coded to, which is the level the ABS actually codes place of work at. The dictionary says "the address of the person's workplace is coded to a Destination zone (DZN)" and that destination zones "are co-designed with state and territory transport authorities for the analysis of Place of work (POWP) data, commuting patterns and the development of transport policy". POWSA2, POWSA3, POWSA4, POWLGA, POWGCCSA and POWSTE on the same row are aggregations of this code.
value_definition: A nine-digit code made of a one-digit state or territory identifier, a four-digit SA2 identifier and a four-digit destination zone identifier, as in 111728922. ASGS Edition 3 has 9,329 destination zones, including 22 non-spatial codes, with 9499 for no fixed place of work and 9799 for migratory, offshore and shipping.
limitation: Destination zones were redesigned for 2021 from the 2016 set, with new zones created in growth areas, so a 2016 and a 2021 zone code with the same value are not guaranteed to be the same ground. Place of work was also imputed for 11.1 per cent of employed people in 2021, up from 10.0 per cent in 2016, and IFPOWP is the column that says which.
rationale: The dictionary page for POWP names the destination zone as the coding unit and gives the imputation rate, while the ASGS destination zones page gives the code structure, the count of zones and the 2021 redesign.
evidence_quote: The address of the person's workplace is coded to a Destination zone (DZN) . Destination zones are co-designed with state and territory transport authorities for the analysis of Place of work (POWP) data, commuting patterns and the development of transport policy.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Destination zone (pow)' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that this is the base level for place of work or how much of it is imputed.

value_domain: ASGS greater capital city statistical area code, place of work
value_source: ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Main Structure: Greater Capital City Statistical Areas
variable_description: Which capital city region, or which rest-of-state region, the person's workplace was in. The ABS says these areas "are designed to represent the functional area of each of the eight State and Territory capital cities" and that their boundaries "represent labour markets", which makes this the coarsest useful cut of commuting on the person record. Paired with GCCSAP, the usual residence version, it identifies people who work in a capital city but live outside it.
value_definition: A five-character alphanumeric code: one digit for the state or territory then a four-character area identifier, as in 1GSYD for Greater Sydney. Sixteen areas cover Australia, plus 19 non-spatial special purpose codes for populations such as migratory and no usual address.
limitation: It understates commuting badly, because almost all journeys to work happen inside one greater capital city area and therefore show no movement at all; POWSA4 or POWDZN are needed to see commuting within a city. The rest-of-state areas are also so large that a single code covers everything from a regional city to a remote station.
rationale: The ASGS page defines the areas, states that they represent labour markets and capital city functional areas, gives the count of areas and special purpose codes, and gives the coding structure.
evidence_quote: GCCSAs are designed to represent the functional area of each of the eight State and Territory capital cities which includes populations who regularly socialise, shop or work within the city, but may live either in the city or in the small towns and rural areas surrounding the city.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Greater capital city statistical area (pow)' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it gave no code shape and no sense of how coarse the geography is for commuting work.

value_domain: ASGS local government area code (2021 boundaries), place of work
value_source: ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Non ABS Structures: Local Government Areas
variable_description: The council area the person's workplace was in, on 2021 local government boundaries. It is one of the geographies the Census dictionary lists for place of work data, built by aggregating the destination zone in POWDZN, and the ABS describes local government areas as "an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries". Set against LGAP, the council area of usual residence, it gives council-to-council commuting flows for 2021.
value_definition: A five-digit code, one digit for the state or territory and four for the area identifier, unique within the state and always ending in zero. Non-spatial codes include 9799 for migratory, offshore and shipping and 9499 for no usual address.
limitation: The workplace is the address the person or their employer nominated, so people with no fixed workplace are coded to a depot and people directed to enter 'None' are coded to a non-spatial code rather than to a council, which biases commuting flows away from mobile trades and transport work. Comparing it with POWLGAP22 also mixes boundary vintages rather than showing movement.
rationale: The ASGS local government area page defines the structure and code shape, and the dictionary page for POWP lists local government areas among the geographies place of work data is available for and explains the depot and 'None' response rules.
evidence_quote: Local Government Areas are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Local government areas (2021 boundaries) (pow)' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying how a workplace address becomes a council code or what happens to people with no fixed workplace.

value_domain: ASGS local government area code (2022 boundaries), place of work
value_source: ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Non ABS Structures: Local Government Areas
variable_description: The council area of the person's workplace, on the 2022 vintage of local government boundaries rather than the 2021 vintage used by POWLGA. The ABS reviews these areas annually and applies changes "by including or excluding whole Mesh Blocks", so the two columns describe the same workplace under two boundary sets. Use whichever vintage matches the council data being joined, and LGAP22 for the person's own council on the same vintage.
value_definition: A five-digit code, one digit for the state or territory and four for the area identifier, ending in zero. When an area is abolished its identifier is retired, and a new area takes the next available identifier in alphabetical order, so codes are not reused across vintages.
limitation: It is not a second, independent measurement: POWLGA and this column come from the same workplace address, so differences between them are boundary changes and never commuting behaviour. Because retired identifiers are not reused, a code present in one vintage and missing in the other signals an amalgamation rather than an empty council.
rationale: The ASGS local government area page documents the annual review, the whole-mesh-block change rule, the retirement and assignment of identifiers and the code structure, which is what separates the two vintages carried in this dataset.
evidence_quote: The ABS reviews Local Government Areas annually, and any changes will be made by including or excluding whole Mesh Blocks.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Local government areas (2022 boundaries) (pow)' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, giving no reason for two local government columns to exist on the same record.

value_domain: ASGS mesh block code, place of work
value_source: ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Main Structure and Greater Capital City Statistical Areas: Mesh Blocks
variable_description: The mesh block containing the workplace address the person reported for their main job. Mesh blocks are "the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS" and are designed to hold between 30 and 60 dwellings. This is finer than anything the published Census reaches: the dictionary states that destination zones "are aggregates of whole Mesh blocks (though data is not coded to the Mesh block level)", so a mesh block on this column comes from the address geocoding inside the integrated asset rather than from the published place-of-work coding chain. Compared against MBUCP it gives commuting origin and destination at the finest ASGS unit.
value_definition: An 11-digit code, one digit for the state or territory and ten for the mesh block, drawn from the 368,286 mesh blocks in ASGS Edition 3. Non-spatial codes cover migratory, offshore, shipping and no usual address populations.
limitation: A workplace mesh block is a single point standing for a whole job, so a truck driver, a plumber and a home care worker are each pinned to one depot or office and their actual working locations are invisible. Because published place-of-work output stops at the destination zone, counts built from this column will also not reproduce ABS destination zone commuting tables exactly.
rationale: The ASGS mesh block page fixes the code structure and the size of the unit, and the dictionary page for POWP states explicitly that place of work is coded to destination zones and not to mesh blocks in published output, which is the caveat this column needs.
evidence_quote: Responses are coded to units of geography known as DZN. DZNs are aggregates of whole Mesh blocks (though data is not coded to the Mesh block level), and aggregate to Statistical area level 2.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Meshblock (pow)' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not flag that this level is finer than the published place-of-work coding and could not be reconciled with ABS destination zone output.

value_domain: ASGS Statistical Area Level 2 code, place of work
value_source: ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Main Structure: Statistical Area Level 2
variable_description: The SA2 the person's workplace fell in, obtained by aggregating the destination zone in POWDZN, which the ABS designs to align to SA2 exactly. SA2s are "medium-sized general purpose areas" whose "purpose is to represent a community that interacts together socially and economically", generally holding 3,000 to 25,000 people. Paired with SA2UCP, the SA2 of usual residence, it is the standard unit for journey-to-work flows because ABS non-Census statistics are also released at this level.
value_definition: A nine-digit fully hierarchical code: one digit for the state or territory, two for the SA4, two for the SA3 and four for the SA2, as in 503021295 for East Perth. Edition 3 holds 2,473 SA2s including 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: The ABS retired the old five-digit SA2 short code in Edition 3, so a nine-digit code here will not join to an older file keyed on the short code without conversion. An SA2 also spans a whole suburb, so a workplace shared with a colleague at this level says nothing about proximity within the suburb.
rationale: The ASGS SA2 page defines the areas, their population range, the nine-digit coding structure and the withdrawal of the short code, and the destination zones page confirms that whole zones aggregate to SA2s.
evidence_quote: An SA2 is identifiable by a 9-digit fully hierarchical code comprising the 1-digit State or Territory identifier, and Statistical Areas Level 2-4 identifiers.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Sa2 (pow)' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it gave neither the code length nor the warning about five-digit short codes from earlier editions.

value_domain: ASGS Statistical Area Level 3 code, place of work
value_source: ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Main Structure: Statistical Area Level 3
variable_description: The SA3 containing the person's workplace, one level up from POWSA2. The ABS builds SA3s "from whole Statistical Areas Level 2" and designs them "for the output of regional data", clustering SA2s with similar regional characteristics into areas of roughly 30,000 to 130,000 people. It is the level at which regional labour market patterns can be read without the small-cell problems of SA2, and SA3UCP holds the residential counterpart.
value_definition: A five-digit hierarchical code: one digit for the state or territory, two for the SA4 and two for the SA3, as in 11401 for Shoalhaven. Edition 3 holds 359 SA3s including 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: Because SA3s are drawn to match administrative regions such as State Regional Development Areas, their boundaries do not follow labour market catchments, so an SA3-level commuting flow can straddle two unrelated employment centres. Zero SA3s also exist for large unpopulated areas, and they can hold workplaces even though no one lives there.
rationale: The ASGS SA3 page gives the definition, the population range, the design intent, the count of areas and the five-digit coding structure that the values in this column follow.
evidence_quote: Statistical Areas Level 3 (SA3s) are geographic areas built from whole Statistical Areas Level 2 (SA2s). They are designed for the output of regional data, including 2021 Census of Population and Housing data.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Sa3 (pow)' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it gave no code shape and no indication of the regional scale the areas represent.

value_domain: ASGS Statistical Area Level 4 code, place of work
value_source: ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Main Structure: Statistical Area Level 4
variable_description: The SA4 containing the person's workplace, which is the largest sub-state region in the ASGS main structure. The ABS states that "SA4 boundaries represent labour markets" and that they are "designed with an emphasis on stability over time to support the time series of statistical releases such as the Quarterly Labour Force publication". That makes this the column to use when Census place of work has to be compared with Labour Force Survey estimates, and SA4UCP is the matching residential region.
value_definition: A three-digit hierarchical code: one digit for the state or territory and two for the SA4, as in 102 for Central Coast. Edition 3 holds 108 SA4s including 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: SA4s are drawn to hold enough people for survey estimates rather than to bound a commute, with metropolitan areas of 300,000 to 500,000 people, so most journeys to work start and end inside one code and the column will show far less mobility than actually occurs. Its stability over time is also a design goal, not a guarantee, since Edition 3 changed some boundaries from 2016.
rationale: The ASGS SA4 page defines the areas, their labour market purpose, their population targets, the count of areas and the three-digit code structure the values follow.
evidence_quote: SA4 boundaries represent labour markets and the functional area of Australian capital cities respectively. They are designed with an emphasis on stability over time to support the time series of statistical releases such as the Quarterly Labour Force publication.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Sa4 (pow)' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that SA4s are labour market regions or how coarse they are for commuting analysis.

value_domain: ASGS state and territory code, place of work
value_source: ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Main Structure: Australia and State/Territory
variable_description: The state or territory the person's workplace was in. The ABS notes that these boundaries are "a cartographic representation of legally designated boundaries and therefore should not be used for legal purposes", and that Jervis Bay, Christmas Island, the Cocos (Keeling) Islands and Norfolk Island are grouped together as Other Territories. Against STEUCP, the state of usual residence, it identifies cross-border workers, which matters most around Albury-Wodonga, Tweed Heads-Coolangatta and the ACT boundary.
value_definition: A single digit: 1 New South Wales, 2 Victoria, 3 Queensland, 4 South Australia, 5 Western Australia, 6 Tasmania, 7 Northern Territory, 8 Australian Capital Territory and 9 Other Territories.
limitation: Cross-border commuting is the only movement it can show, so it is close to useless as a mobility measure for the great majority of workers whose job is in their own state. It also cannot separate the four Other Territories from one another, since they share the single code 9.
rationale: The ASGS Australia and State/Territory page lists the nine codes with their names and states the cartographic caveat, which fixes both the domain and its correct use.
evidence_quote: The ASGS State and Territory boundaries are a cartographic representation of legally designated boundaries and therefore should not be used for legal purposes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'State (pow)' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not give the nine codes or note that Other Territories are collapsed into one.

value_domain: Place of usual residence one year ago, ASGS area code
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence one year ago (PUR1P)
variable_description: Where the person usually lived one year before the Census, as an ASGS area code. The ABS defines it as recording "the geographic area in which a person usually lived one year before the Census" and states that "the base area that is output is Statistical area level 2". In this dataset it sits with MBU1P, LGAU1P and STEU1P, which carry the same one-year-ago address at mesh block, council and state level, so this column is the standard-output version of that address.
value_definition: An ASGS area code, output at Statistical Area Level 2 and aggregable upwards, with four-digit special purpose codes for cases that cannot be placed: 9099 capital city not further defined, 9299 overseas, 9499 no usual address, 9799 migratory, offshore and shipping, 9899 state or territory not further defined, &&&& not stated and @@@@ not applicable.
limitation: The overseas category is a single code with no country attached, so a return migrant cannot be traced to an origin, and 'capital city not further defined' and 'state not further defined' mark answers too vague to place rather than real locations. Children under one year old are not applicable, which is a different thing from not having moved.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, names Statistical Area Level 2 as the base output, lists all the special purpose codes with their meanings and reports the 6.0 per cent non-response rate for 2021.
evidence_quote: This variable records the geographic area in which a person usually lived one year before the Census. The base area that is output is Statistical area level 2.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Place of Usual Residence One Year Ago' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say what geography the codes are, or that overseas and vague answers have their own codes.

value_domain: Place of usual residence five years ago, ASGS area code
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence five years ago (PUR5P)
variable_description: Where the person usually lived five years before the Census, as an ASGS area code. The ABS defines it as recording "the geographic area in which a person usually lived five years before the Census" and gives Statistical Area Level 2 as "the base area that is output", which can be aggregated to SA3, SA4, significant urban area, greater capital city statistical area and state. MBU5P and LGAU5P hold the same five-year-old address at finer and administrative levels, and PUR1P narrows the window to one year.
value_definition: An ASGS area code, output at Statistical Area Level 2 and aggregable upwards, with four-digit special purpose codes 9099 capital city not further defined, 9299 overseas, 9499 no usual residence, 9799 migratory, offshore and shipping, 9899 state or territory not further defined, &&&& not stated and @@@@ not applicable.
limitation: More of the column is missing than for the one-year version: non-response was 6.9 per cent in 2021 against 6.0 per cent, both down on their 2016 levels. Children under five are not applicable, so any migration rate calculated on the whole population will be diluted unless that group is removed.
rationale: The dictionary page gives the definition, the base geography and the aggregations available, the full special purpose code list with definitions, the under-five exclusion and the non-response rate.
evidence_quote: This variable records the geographic area in which a person usually lived five years before the Census. The base area that is output for Place of usual residence five years ago (PUR5P) is Statistical area level 2 (SA2).
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Place of Usual Residence Five Years Ago' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it gave no geography, no special purpose codes and no sense of how much of the column is missing.

value_domain: ASCED 2001 field of study code
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Non-school qualification: field of study (QALFP)
variable_description: What subject the person's highest completed post-school qualification was in. The ABS defines the variable as describing "the field of study of a person's highest completed non-school qualification", coded using the Australian Standard Classification of Education (ASCED), 2001. QALLP on the same row holds the level of that same qualification, so field and level have to be read together: a certificate III in engineering and a doctorate in engineering share this code.
value_definition: A six-digit ASCED code nesting inside a four-digit narrow field and a two-digit broad field, giving 16 broad fields, 87 narrow fields and 435 detailed fields, with 'nfd' codes where the answer supports only a broader level and @@@@@@ for not applicable.
limitation: It cannot be used to count qualification holders. The ABS warns that people who said they held a qualification but did not name a field are coded to not stated here, so the population that actually holds a qualification is not identifiable from this column alone. The 12.3 per cent non-response rate in 2021 falls to 2.3 per cent once the qualification indicator question is used as a filter.
rationale: The dictionary page names the classification, gives the category counts at each digit level, states the scope, and sets out the data use warning and both non-response rates.
evidence_quote: This variable describes the field of study of a person's highest completed non-school qualification.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Non-School Qualification: Field of Study' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, naming neither ASCED nor the trap that the column cannot be used to count people with a qualification.

value_domain: ASCED level of education (non-school qualification)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Non-school qualification: level of education (QALLP)
variable_description: The level of the highest non-school qualification a person has completed, recorded as a level rather than a subject. ABS defines it as a variable that "describes the level of a person's highest completed non-school qualification", coded to the Australian Standard Classification of Education (ASCED) 2001 Level of Education classification. QALFP on the same person record holds the field of study of that same qualification, and HEAP combines school and non-school attainment into one ranking. A person with several qualifications is counted once, at the highest level only.
value_definition: A hierarchical ASCED level code running from postgraduate degree through graduate diploma and certificate, bachelor degree, advanced diploma and diploma, down to certificate levels I to IV, published at broad and detailed levels. Supplementary codes cover level inadequately described (0), not stated (&), not applicable (@) and overseas visitor (V).
limitation: It does not say where or when the qualification was gained, so it cannot date a person's study or separate Australian from overseas credentials. The not applicable code pools four different situations — no non-school qualification, a qualification out of scope of ASCED, still studying, and aged under 15 — so it is not evidence that a person holds no qualification. Because only the highest level is kept, a tradesperson who later took a degree shows as a graduate with no trade.
rationale: The ABS Census Dictionary gives a definition for this exact mnemonic, names the classification behind the codes and lists the supplementary codes and what the not applicable category comprises.
evidence_quote: This variable describes the level of a person's highest completed non-school qualification.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording 'Non-School Qualification: Level of Education', with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both value definition and limitation, so it never named ASCED or said that only the highest qualification is kept.

value_domain: ASGS Remoteness Area code (state-based)
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Remoteness Areas
variable_description: The remoteness class of the place where the dwelling was counted, on the 2021 dwelling record. Remoteness Areas group whole SA1s by their average ARIA+ score, a measure of road distance to service centres, and ABS states that they are "identifiable by a 2 digit hierarchical code, comprising the 1-digit State and Territory, and a Remoteness Area identifier". RAD is that state-based form; RAND on the same row is the national form of the same classification. Every person counted in the dwelling shares this value, and the person record's RANP is the usual-residence counterpart.
value_definition: A two-digit ASGS Edition 3 code: one digit for state or territory, one for the remoteness class. The five classes are Major Cities of Australia, Inner Regional, Outer Regional, Remote and Very Remote Australia, with supplementary codes for migratory-offshore-shipping and no usual address.
limitation: Remoteness measures access to services, not population density or disadvantage, so an Inner Regional code says nothing about a household's income or the size of its town. The class is assigned to the dwelling's whole SA1, so a well-serviced pocket inside a remote area carries the remote code. It is also where the dwelling is, not where its occupants usually live.
rationale: ASGS Edition 3 publishes the classification, its five classes, the ARIA+ basis and the two-digit state-prefixed code structure. That the PLIDA column is the state-based rather than the national form is read from its pairing with RAND on the same dwelling record, which is why confidence is medium rather than high.
evidence_quote: Remoteness Areas are identifiable by a 2 digit hierarchical code, comprising the 1-digit State and Territory, and a Remoteness Area identifier.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Remoteness areas (en)' with the generic no-value-list sentence repeated as definition and limitation, so it did not say what remoteness measures, that the code carries the state, or how it differs from RAND beside it.

value_domain: Rent affordability category (30 per cent of household income)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Rent affordability indicator (RAID)
variable_description: Whether the household counted in this dwelling paid more than 30 per cent of its income in rent. ABS allocates "an in scope household to one of two categories: rent payments less than or equal to 30% of household income" or more than 30 per cent, dividing weekly rent from RNTD by an imputed household income. Because the Census collects personal income in ranges rather than dollars, the denominator is built by assigning each member aged 15 and over a median dollar value for their INCP bracket, taken from the Survey of Income and Housing, and summing them. Only rented occupied private dwellings are in scope.
value_definition: Four categories: rent payments 30 per cent or less of household income, rent payments more than 30 per cent, unable to be determined, and not applicable. The last covers unoccupied dwellings, owner-occupied dwellings and non-private dwellings.
limitation: It is not a measure of housing stress. The 30 per cent line is applied to every renting household regardless of income, so a well-off household paying a large rent by choice scores the same as a low-income household with no alternative; the usual stress measure restricts the rule to the bottom 40 per cent of incomes. The denominator is imputed from income brackets, so a household near a bracket edge can fall on the wrong side of the line.
rationale: The Census Dictionary page for this mnemonic gives the two-category definition, names the input variables RNTD and INCP, and describes the Survey of Income and Housing median-value imputation used to build the denominator.
evidence_quote: This variable allocates an in scope household to one of two categories: rent payments less than or equal to 30% of household income
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Rent affordability indicator' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it never said what the threshold was, that the income denominator is imputed, or that this is not the 30/40 housing stress measure.

value_domain: ASGS Remoteness Area class (national)
value_source: ABS Census geography glossary, Remoteness Areas (RA)
variable_description: The remoteness class of the dwelling's location on a single national scale, without the state prefix that RAD carries. ABS defines the classification as one that "divides the States and Territories into 5 classes of remoteness based on relative access to services", and in its state-based form a remoteness identifier is only unique once a state digit precedes it, so the national form is what you need to treat Outer Regional Australia as one group across the country. RAD and RAND sit on the same 2021 dwelling record and describe the same place; they differ only in whether the state is part of the code. RANP is the person-level, usual-residence equivalent.
value_definition: The five national remoteness classes — Major Cities of Australia, Inner Regional, Outer Regional, Remote and Very Remote Australia — under ASGS Edition 3, plus supplementary categories for migratory-offshore-shipping and no usual address.
limitation: It cannot be broken down by state without joining to another geography column, which is what RAD is for. A national class also pools very different places: Very Remote Australia covers a mining town of several thousand and an outstation of twenty, and the class boundary depends on an averaged ARIA+ score rather than on anything a resident would recognise.
rationale: The Census geography glossary defines Remoteness Areas for Census use, and the ASGS Edition 3 page establishes that the ordinary remoteness code is state-prefixed, which is what makes a separate national column meaningful. The national reading of this column comes from its name and its pairing with RAD, so confidence is medium.
evidence_quote: Remoteness Areas (RA) divides the States and Territories into 5 classes of remoteness based on relative access to services.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Remoteness areas (national) (en)' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell why the dwelling record carries two remoteness columns or which one to use.

value_domain: ASGS Remoteness Area class (national)
value_source: ABS Census geography glossary, Remoteness Areas (RA)
variable_description: The national remoteness class of the area where the person usually lived, on the 2021 person record. ABS defines the classification as dividing "the States and Territories into 5 classes of remoteness based on relative access to services", built by grouping SA1s on their average ARIA+ score. Because this is coded to usual residence rather than to where the person was counted, it can differ from RAND on the dwelling record for anyone away from home on Census night. It is the column to use when comparing remoteness across the whole country on one scale.
value_definition: The five national classes — Major Cities of Australia, Inner Regional, Outer Regional, Remote and Very Remote Australia — under ASGS Edition 3, with supplementary categories for migratory-offshore-shipping and no usual address.
limitation: Remoteness is about distance to services, so it is not a measure of disadvantage and should not be used as one: some of the most disadvantaged areas in Australia sit inside Major Cities. It also cannot say how far the person actually travels for anything, because the class is an average over the SA1 rather than a property of the person's address.
rationale: The Census geography glossary gives the Census-specific definition of Remoteness Areas, and the '(ur)' in the custodian's own description matches the ABS usual-residence coding that the glossary distinguishes from place of enumeration. The national rather than state-based reading rests on the variable name, so confidence is medium.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Remoteness areas (national) (ur)' and nothing else, with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not explain the usual-residence basis or the ARIA+ service-access idea underneath the classes.
evidence_quote: Remoteness Areas (RA) divides the States and Territories into 5 classes of remoteness based on relative access to services.

value_domain: ASGS Remoteness Area code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Remoteness Areas
variable_description: The remoteness class of the area the person usually lived in, carried on the 2016 and 2021 person records. Remoteness Areas are made up of SA1s grouped on their average ARIA+ score, and ABS states they are "identifiable by a 2 digit hierarchical code, comprising the 1-digit State and Territory, and a Remoteness Area identifier". The 2016 value uses the ASGS boundaries of that Census and the 2021 value uses ASGS Edition 3, so the two are not a clean before-and-after pair for the same person. In 2021 the person record also carries RANP, the same classification without the state prefix.
value_definition: A two-digit ASGS code combining state or territory with the remoteness class, over five classes from Major Cities of Australia to Very Remote Australia, plus supplementary codes for migratory-offshore-shipping and no usual address.
limitation: A change in this code between the 2016 and 2021 person records is not proof that the person moved: ARIA+ scores and SA1 boundaries are both rebuilt between editions, so an unmoved household can change class. The code also cannot be read as rurality of the dwelling itself, since a whole SA1 takes one class.
