rationale: The registry shows STEUCD sitting inside the dwelling table's enumeration geography block, and the ABS Census glossary and the enumeration-versus-usual-residence information paper give the definition and the size of the gap between the two bases.
evidence_quote: The place at which the person is counted on Census Night, which may not be where they usually live.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'State of Dwelling on Census Night' with the generic no-finite-list sentence twice over, which left a reader unable to tell whether the column was an enumeration geography or a usual-residence one, and gave no way to reconcile counts built from it with usual-residence counts.

value_domain: ASGS state and territory of usual residence
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence (PURP)
variable_description: The state or territory a person usually lives in, which is the state-level roll-up of the mesh block their usual address was coded to. The Census Dictionary defines the underlying variable as recording "the geographic area in which a person usually lives. It may or may not be the place where the person was counted on Census Night", so this column follows the person home rather than staying with the dwelling they were enumerated in. UAICP on the same row says whether the person was at home that night, IFPURP says whether the address was imputed, and SA1UCP through SA4UCP hold the finer cuts of the same address.
value_definition: A single ASGS state and territory code derived from the mesh block the usual address was coded to, plus an overseas visitor category and the migratory, off-shore and shipping category. People with no fixed address write 'None' and are placed in a designated SA1 and SA2 for their state or territory.
limitation: A value here can be imputed rather than reported. Where the address was incomplete the ABS imputes place of usual residence, sometimes at a level coarser than mesh block, and IFPURP is the only column that records that this happened; non-response was 4.3% at SA2 level in 2021. The column also has nothing to say about how long the person has lived there, which is what UAI1P and UAI5P are for.
rationale: STEUCP is the state and territory output of the Census place-of-usual-residence concept, and the 2021 PURP page gives the definition, the mesh block base, the ASGS aggregation, the no-fixed-address handling and the imputation flag.
evidence_quote: This variable records the geographic area in which a person usually lives. It may or may not be the place where the person was counted on Census Night.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'State/territory of usual address' with the generic sentence printed as both value definition and limitation, so it did not distinguish usual residence from enumeration and gave no warning that the value may be imputed.

value_domain: ASGS state and territory of place of work
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of work (POWP)
variable_description: The state or territory a person worked in during the week before Census Night, held only on the 2011 person table. The ABS defines the underlying place-of-work variable as recording "the geographic area in which a person worked in the week before Census Night", with "the address of the person's workplace ... coded to a Destination zone (DZN)", and this column is that coding aggregated to state. Compared with STEUCP, the state of usual residence, it is what identifies cross-border commuters; the 2021 table replaces it with an explicit POWSTE alongside POWMB, POWSA2 and POWDZN.
value_definition: A single ASGS state and territory code, taken from the destination zone the reported workplace address was coded to, with separate categories for workplaces that could not be coded to a zone and for people the variable does not apply to.
limitation: A missing value is usually not a missing workplace: the variable applies only to employed people aged 15 and over, so the unemployed, people not in the labour force and people with unstated labour force status are all not applicable. It also describes one job in one week, so a second job in another state and any travel the job involves are invisible, and an employee working from home is coded to the employer's address, because the form asks for the employer's workplace address rather than where the work was done.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page for place of work gives the concept, the reference week, the destination zone coding and the employed-persons scope; STEWKADP is the 2011 state-level output of the same concept, so the definition transfers even though the 2011 page itself is archived.
evidence_quote: This variable records the geographic area in which a person worked in the week before Census Night. The address of the person's workplace is coded to a Destination zone (DZN).
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave only 'State/territory of workplace' and the generic no-finite-list sentence twice, so it did not say that the value comes from a coded workplace address, that it covers one week, or that non-employed people are out of scope rather than missing.

value_domain: Census dwelling structure classification
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Dwelling structure (STRD)
variable_description: What kind of building the dwelling is: a separate house, a semi-detached or terrace house by storeys, a flat or apartment banded by the height of the block it sits in, a caravan, a cabin or houseboat, or an improvised home. The ABS says the variable "records the structure of private dwellings" and that it "is not collected from a question on the Census form" — it comes from the ABS Address Register supplemented by Building Approvals, with field officers updating it during collection. It applies to private dwellings only, so every hotel, hospital, prison and nursing home is not applicable and NPDD and DWTD are the columns that describe those instead.
value_definition: Twelve substantive categories covering separate house, two semi-detached bands, four flat and apartment bands set by the number of storeys in the block, a flat or apartment attached to a house, caravan, cabin or houseboat, improvised home or tent, and house or flat attached to a shop or office, plus not stated and not applicable, for fourteen codes in all.
limitation: It says nothing about the size of the dwelling or who lives in it, and the flat categories count storeys in the block rather than the dwelling's own floor, so a ground-floor unit and a top-floor unit in the same nine-storey tower share a code. Because the value is drawn from an administrative register rather than a form answer, a new dwelling can have its structure assigned by a field officer or imputed from neighbouring properties, so it is not always a reported fact about that building.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page for STRD gives the definition, the full category list, the administrative derivation from the Address Register and Building Approvals, and the private-dwellings-only scope.
evidence_quote: This variable records the structure of private dwellings.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Dwelling Structure' and the generic no-finite-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, even though the ABS publishes a closed category list and the unusual fact that this variable is not asked on the form.

value_domain: Census full-time or part-time student status
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Full-time/part-time student status (STUP)
variable_description: Whether a person was attending an educational institution at Census time and, if so, whether full time or part time. The ABS says the variable "describes the full-time or part-time status of students" and is "collected from a mark box response" on the form, so it is a reported status rather than a derived one. The not-attending code sits in the same column as the two student codes, which makes this single field both the student filter and the study-load grading; TYPP names the type of institution and TYSTAP combines the two with age. It applies to all persons, so a preschooler and a doctoral candidate are both in scope.
value_definition: Single-character codes: 1 not attending, 2 full-time student, 3 part-time student, 4 institution stated but full-time or part-time status not stated, & both institution and status not stated, and V overseas visitor.
limitation: Full time and part time are the institution's own enrolment labels as the respondent understood them, not a measured study load, and the Census sets no hours threshold, so the split is not comparable with a workload definition. Code 4 also means the person named an institution but not a load, which is a different problem from the blanket not-stated code and should not be pooled with it.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page for STUP gives the definition, the full code list including the two distinct not-stated codes, the mark-box collection method and the all-persons scope.
evidence_quote: This variable describes the full-time or part-time status of students.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Full-Time/Part-Time Student Status' and the generic sentence twice, so it did not disclose the closed code list, the two different kinds of non-response, or that non-students are coded in the same column rather than left blank.

value_domain: ASGS Significant Urban Area of the dwelling
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Significant Urban Areas
variable_description: Which named urban area of 10,000 people or more the dwelling stands in, on the 2021 dwelling table. The ABS defines the classification as areas that "represent Urban Centres, or groups of Urban Centres, that contain population of 10,000 persons or more", built from SA2s, so this column places a dwelling in a town or city by name rather than inside an administrative boundary. It is one of the '(en)' enumeration geography columns beside UCLD, TRD, SOSD, GCCSAD and LGAD, all coded from the dwelling's address. A dwelling outside every significant urban area takes a state-specific 'not in a Significant Urban Area' code rather than a blank.
value_definition: A unique four-digit non-hierarchical code, the first digit identifying the state or territory and the remaining three assigned alphabetically within it from 001. Perth is 5009 and Gold Coast – Tweed Heads 3007; codes ending in 000 mean not in a significant urban area.
limitation: A significant urban area has no administrative existence, so it cannot attribute a dwelling to a council, a state electorate or a health region — LGAD, SED22D and PHND do that. Because it is assembled from whole SA2s, its boundary only approximates the urban centre underneath it and includes surrounding non-urban land, and a cross-border area is coded to the state holding its largest urban centre, so Gold Coast – Tweed Heads dwellings in New South Wales carry a Queensland first digit.
rationale: The ASGS Edition 3 Significant Urban Areas page publishes the definition, the population threshold, the SA2 construction, the four-digit coding structure and the cross-border naming rule, which is exactly the classification behind the 2021 dwelling column.
evidence_quote: Significant Urban Areas (SUAs) represent Urban Centres, or groups of Urban Centres, that contain population of 10,000 persons or more.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the metadata phrase 'Significant urban areas (en)' with the generic no-finite-list sentence printed twice, which explained neither what a significant urban area is, what '(en)' means, nor that the codes are a published ASGS classification.

value_domain: ASGS Significant Urban Area of usual residence
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Significant Urban Areas
variable_description: The named urban area of 10,000 people or more that a person usually lives in, on the 2021 person table. The ABS defines the classification as areas that "represent Urban Centres, or groups of Urban Centres, that contain population of 10,000 persons or more". The '(ur)' tag on this column, against '(en)' on SUAD, is the whole difference between them: SUAP follows the person to their usual address while SUAD stays with the dwelling they were counted in, so a person away from home on Census Night has different values in the two tables. It gives a way to compare like-sized towns and cities that LGAP and POAP cannot, because those follow administrative lines instead.
value_definition: A unique four-digit non-hierarchical code, the first digit identifying the state or territory and the last three assigned alphabetically within it from 001, with codes ending in 000 meaning not in a significant urban area.
limitation: It describes where the person sleeps, not where they work: there is no significant urban area coding of the workplace, and POWSA2, POWSA4 and POWSTE are the columns that hold that. The value also inherits any imputation of place of usual residence — 4.3% of 2021 records were non-response at SA2 level — so an urban area here can rest on an imputed address rather than a reported one.
rationale: The ASGS Edition 3 page gives the classification, the threshold and the code structure, and the registry shows SUAP sitting in the 2021 person table's usual-residence geography block with SA1UCP to SA4UCP, UCLP and TRP.
evidence_quote: Significant Urban Areas (SUAs) represent Urban Centres, or groups of Urban Centres, that contain population of 10,000 persons or more.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Significant urban areas (ur)' and the generic sentence twice, so a reader could not tell that '(ur)' means usual residence, that SUAD is the same classification on a different basis, or that a published ASGS code list stands behind the values.

value_domain: Census national reporting scope flag
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Level of workforce participation survey comparison flag (SVFP)
variable_description: Marks the people the ABS keeps when it reports Census workforce participation on a basis comparable with household surveys. The ABS says the variable "approximates a population that is comparable with in-scope survey populations as used in the Closing the Gap Target 8 – strong economic participation and development of people and their communities". It is not asked on the form: it is assembled from age, dwelling type, household composition, industry of employment, relationship in household and place of usual residence, and it has only two values, so its job is to define a denominator rather than to describe a person.
value_definition: Two categories: 1 for a person in scope of the workforce participation survey comparison population, and @ for not applicable. Not applicable covers people in non-private dwellings, non-classifiable households, Defence and foreign government roles, people aged under 15, and visitors.
limitation: It says nothing about whether the person worked — LFSP, UEFP and HRSP carry participation, employment and hours. Using it as a filter silently removes everyone in a non-private dwelling, so any estimate that needs residents of nursing homes, prisons, hostels or student accommodation is biased by the filter itself rather than by the data.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page for SVFP gives the purpose, the six source variables, the two-value code list and the exact composition of the not-applicable group.
evidence_quote: This variable approximates a population that is comparable with in-scope survey populations as used in the Closing the Gap Target 8 – strong economic participation and development of people and their communities.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Level of workplace participation survey comparison flag' with the generic no-finite-list sentence twice, which was wrong on two counts: the domain is finite at two values, and the flag is a scope marker rather than a participation measure.

value_domain: Census imputation flag for sex
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for sex (IFSEXP)
variable_description: Says whether the SEXP value on the same row was reported on the Census form or filled in by the ABS. The 2021 equivalent, IFSEXP, is defined as indicating "if a person's binary sex was imputed", where "imputation is a statistical process for predicting values where no response was provided to a question and a response could not be derived". On the 2011 person table it sits with IFAGEP, IFMSTP and IFPURP, the matching flags for age, registered marital status and place of usual residence, so the imputed content of a record can be counted before any analysis leans on it.
value_definition: Two codes, one meaning sex was not imputed and one meaning it was; the 2021 equivalent uses 01 and 02. The flag is produced during processing of the sex variable, not collected.
limitation: It does not say what the imputation drew on or how reliable it was, and it covers sex alone, so an imputed age on the same record shows in a different column. Non-response to sex was 5.8% in 2016 and 4.7% in 2021, which means dropping every flagged record removes a sizeable and non-random group rather than trimming a rounding error.
rationale: The 2011 registry shows SXFP sitting with the other IF-prefixed imputation flags and describes it as the imputation flag for SEXP, and the 2021 Census Dictionary publishes the same flag under the name IFSEXP with its definition, its two codes and the sex non-response rates for both Censuses.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates if a person's binary sex was imputed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Imputation flag for SEXP' with the generic no-finite-list sentence twice, which is doubly wrong: the domain is two values, and nothing on the page told a reader what imputation means or how much of the sex variable it affects.

value_domain: Synthetic person identifier within a Census file
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The person key inside a single Census file: one value per counted person, used to join that person's record across the person, family and dwelling tables of the same Census. It appears on all three 2016 tables and on the 2021 person table, which is what lets a person be tied to the family and dwelling they were counted in; DWELLING_ID and FAMILY_ID are the keys for those units themselves. It is not the PLIDA spine identifier, so it does not by itself reach a person's tax, health or payment records — ABS says the "Person Linkage Spine allows us to link datasets through a spine of key information, separate from the main body of data", and that link is what crosses datasets. The 2011 tables use C11_PERSON_ID for the same job.
value_definition: An opaque identifier with no internal structure, unique within one Census year's files. The domain is open and there is no list to publish.
limitation: Do not assume it is a longitudinal key. Nothing the ABS publishes says the value persists from one Census to the next, so change over time is safer assembled through the PLIDA spine than by joining this column across years. Nor is it a household key: where it appears on a dwelling or family row it marks a person's link into that unit, not the unit's own identity.
rationale: No ABS page documents this column by name; the description is assembled from the PLIDA linkage architecture, which the ABS publishes, and from the registry's own table layout, which shows the identifier repeated across the person, family and dwelling tables of a Census year alongside separate DWELLING_ID and FAMILY_ID keys, and replaced by C11_PERSON_ID in 2011.
evidence_quote: The Person Linkage Spine allows us to link datasets through a spine of key information, separate from the main body of data.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Synthetic id of individual person on dataset' with a domain inferred from the variable name, so it did not say which tables the key joins, that it does not persist across Census years, or that it is separate from the spine identifier that links Census to the rest of PLIDA.

value_domain: Census tenure type classification
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Tenure type (TEND)
variable_description: How the household holds the dwelling — owned outright, owned with a mortgage, bought under a shared equity scheme, rented, occupied rent free, held under a life tenure scheme, or other. The ABS defines it as describing "whether a dwelling is owned, being purchased or rented", asked as a single question with one answer allowed. It applies to occupied private dwellings only, so unoccupied dwellings, non-private dwellings and migratory, off-shore and shipping areas are not applicable. Since 2006 the question has separated owners with a mortgage from owners without one, which is why an 'owned' total has to be built from two codes.
value_definition: Seven substantive categories — owned outright, owned with a mortgage, purchased under a shared equity scheme, rented, occupied rent free, occupied under a life tenure scheme, and other — plus not stated (&) and not applicable (@).
limitation: It records the household's tenure, not who owns the dwelling, so an owner-occupier and their adult children counted at the same address all sit under one value and the column cannot identify a title holder. It also does not say who the landlord is, which is the difference between a public housing tenancy and a private one; LLDD and TENLLD carry that. Non-response was 5.4% in 2021, down from 7.7% in 2016.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page for TEND gives the definition, the closed category list, the derivation from a single form question, the occupied-private-dwelling scope and the non-response rates for both Censuses.
evidence_quote: This variable describes whether a dwelling is owned, being purchased or rented.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Tenure Type' and the generic no-finite-list sentence twice, despite the ABS publishing a nine-category closed list, and it did not warn that owner-occupation has to be summed across two codes.

value_domain: Census tenure and landlord type classification
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Tenure and landlord type (TENLLD)
variable_description: Tenure with the landlord named for rented dwellings, which makes it the column that separates a public housing tenancy from a community housing one and from a private rental. The ABS says it "combines Tenure type (TEND) and Landlord type (LLDD) to provide more detailed information for rented dwellings", so it is built during processing rather than asked. It has no non-response rate of its own, because it inherits whatever TEND and LLDD carried. Like TEND it applies to occupied private dwellings only.
value_definition: Eleven categories: owned outright; owned with a mortgage; rented from a real estate agent, a state or territory housing authority, a community housing provider, a person not in the same household, or another landlord type; rented with landlord type not stated; other tenure type; and tenure type not stated or not applicable.
limitation: It is not a strict refinement of TEND. Rent-free occupancy and life tenure schemes, which TEND keeps as separate codes, are folded into 'other tenure type' here, and shared equity purchases are folded into 'owned with a mortgage', so reading the two columns as nested loses those groups and will overstate mortgaged ownership.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page for TENLLD gives the definition, the eleven-category list, the derivation from TEND and LLDD, the recoding of rent-free, life tenure and shared equity, and the absence of a separate non-response rate.
evidence_quote: This variable combines Tenure type (TEND) and Landlord type (LLDD) to provide more detailed information for rented dwellings.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Tenure and Landlord Type' with the generic sentence twice, giving no category list and no notice of the collapsing that makes TENLLD and TEND disagree on rent-free and shared-equity households.

value_domain: Count of children ever born
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of children ever born (TISP)
variable_description: How many children a woman aged 15 and over has ever given birth to, as a count rather than a band. The ABS defines it as recording "the number of children ever born to each female aged 15 years and over", and the question excludes adopted, foster and step children. It is the Census's lifetime fertility measure, so it counts children who have died or left home as well as those in the dwelling on Census Night. TISRP holds the banded version of the same answer.
value_definition: Two-digit counts from 00 to 30, where 30 means thirty or more, with && not stated, @@ not applicable and VV overseas visitor. All numeric responses are accepted as reported.
limitation: It will not match the number of children present in the household, because it counts births over a lifetime and excludes adopted, foster and step children — HKIDP and the family variables describe who is actually there. Males and non-binary respondents were not asked, so their records are not applicable rather than zero, and treating not-applicable as zero halves any population-wide average. Non-response was 6.7% in 2021, and because responses are accepted as written the top of the distribution contains implausible values.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page for TISP gives the definition, the female-15-and-over scope, the 00-to-30 code range with supplementary codes, the exclusion of adopted, foster and step children, the acceptance of all numeric responses and the non-response rate.
evidence_quote: This variable records the number of children ever born to each female aged 15 years and over.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Number of Children Ever Born' with the generic no-finite-list sentence printed twice, so it neither gave the closed 00-to-30 domain nor warned that men and non-binary respondents are not applicable rather than zero.

value_domain: Banded count of children ever born
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of children ever born (ranges) (TISRP)
variable_description: The banded version of the children-ever-born count, running from no children to eight or more. The ABS defines it as recording "the number of children ever born to each female aged 15 years and over in ranges" and says it "is derived from Number of children ever born (TISP)", so it holds no information TISP does not. Use it where a banded output is wanted or where small counts at the top of the distribution would otherwise be identifying.
value_definition: Twelve categories: single values from 0 (no children) through 7, then 8 for eight or more children, plus & not stated, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor.
limitation: The top band closes at eight, so a mean computed from this column is biased downward against the same mean from TISP, and no upper tail can be recovered from it. Because it is derived, it repeats TISP's exclusions and its 6.7% non-response rather than reducing either.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page for TISRP gives the definition, the band list, and the statement that it is derived from TISP.
evidence_quote: This variable records the number of children ever born to each female aged 15 years and over in ranges.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Number of Children Ever Born (ranges)' with the generic sentence twice, which hid both the published band list and the closed top band that makes averages from this column differ from TISP.

value_domain: ASGS Tourism Region of the dwelling
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Tourism Regions
variable_description: Which of the 76 tourism regions the dwelling was enumerated in, on the 2021 dwelling table. The ABS says "Tourism Regions are an ABS approximation of tourism regions provided by Tourism Research Australia (TRA)" and that they "have been created using Statistical Areas Level 2 (SA2s)", so the boundaries are statistical stand-ins for someone else's administrative regions rather than ABS-defined areas. It sits with SUAD, UCLD and the other '(en)' geography columns coded from the dwelling's address. TRP on the person table is the same classification applied to usual residence instead.
value_definition: A five-character code combining a state or territory digit, the letter R and a three-digit region number: 1R100 is Hunter in New South Wales and 2R100 is High Country in Victoria. Codes stay put while boundaries do and change when a boundary changes materially, so they are not stable across ASGS editions.
limitation: It says where a dwelling is, not that anything touristic happens there: a resident household and a holiday let inside the same region carry the same code and nothing distinguishes them. The 76 regions also do not cover all of Australia, and the ABS has removed Tourism Regions from the Non-ABS Structures in ASGS Edition 4 from July 2026, so a code here has no direct successor and must be carried forward through correspondences.
rationale: The ASGS Edition 3 Tourism Regions page gives the definition, the SA2 construction, the count of 76 regions, the coding structure with worked examples, and the coverage gap; the Edition 4 release notes record the removal.
evidence_quote: Tourism Regions are an ABS approximation of tourism regions provided by Tourism Research Australia (TRA).
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Tourism regions (en)' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say who defines the regions, that the ABS only approximates them from SA2s, or that the classification is being retired.

value_domain: ASGS Tourism Region of usual residence
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Tourism Regions
variable_description: The tourism region a person usually lives in, on the 2021 person table. The ABS says "Tourism Regions are an ABS approximation of tourism regions provided by Tourism Research Australia (TRA)", approximated from SA2s. Because this is the '(ur)' version it counts residents of a tourism region, which is what makes it useful for describing the workforce and population that a tourism economy rests on; TRD on the dwelling table is the enumeration counterpart.
value_definition: A five-character code combining a state or territory digit, the letter R and a three-digit region number, with 76 regions defined in ASGS Edition 3.
limitation: It cannot measure tourism. The value comes from where the person lives, so a visitor counted in a region on Census Night still carries the region they usually live in, and Tourism Research Australia's own visitor surveys are what estimate flows. Coverage is also incomplete: Christmas Island, the Cocos (Keeling) Islands, Norfolk Island and Jervis Bay fall outside the structure, so an absent value there is a gap in the classification rather than a missing response.
rationale: The ASGS Edition 3 Tourism Regions page gives the definition, the SA2 construction, the code structure and the excluded territories, and the registry shows TRP in the 2021 person table's usual-residence geography block beside SUAP and UCLP.
evidence_quote: Tourism Regions are an ABS approximation of tourism regions provided by Tourism Research Australia (TRA).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Tourism regions (ur)' and the generic sentence twice, leaving it unclear that '(ur)' means usual residence and that the column counts residents rather than visitors.

value_domain: Census type of educational institution attending
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Type of educational institution attending (TYPP)
variable_description: Which kind of institution a student was attending: preschool, primary or secondary split three ways by government, Catholic and other non-government, or tertiary split into vocational education including TAFE and university or other higher education. The ABS defines it as recording "the type of education institution being attended by people who are full-time or part-time students", collected from a mark box. Each of primary, secondary and tertiary also carries a not-further-defined code, used when a person named the broad type but not the sector. STUP on the same row says whether the attendance was full time or part time, and a person coded not attending there is not applicable here. Non-response was 0.8% in 2021, low because the question only reaches people who said they were students.
value_definition: Sixteen categories: preschool; three primary sectors plus primary not further defined; three secondary sectors plus secondary not further defined; tertiary split into vocational education including TAFE, university or other higher education, and tertiary not further defined; other; and not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor.
limitation: It names the institution, not the course or the level being studied, so a TAFE student doing a certificate II and one doing an advanced diploma share a code; QALLP holds the level of a completed non-school qualification and QALFP the field. Nor does the school sector split describe funding or religious affiliation — an independent religious school and a secular one both fall under 'other non-government'.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page for TYPP gives the definition, the sixteen-category list, the mark-box collection, the students-only scope and the non-response rate.
evidence_quote: This variable records the type of education institution being attended by people who are full-time or part-time students.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Type of Educational Institution Attending' with the generic sentence twice, which neither gave the closed category list nor explained that non-students are not applicable, so a missing value could be misread as unknown attendance.

value_domain: Census educational institution attendee status
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Educational institution: attendee status (TYSTAP)
variable_description: One column that says what kind of institution a student attends, at what study load, and for tertiary students in which age band. The ABS says it "combines responses from Type of educational institution attending (TYPP), Full-time/part-time student status (STUP) and Age (AGEP) to indicate a person's attendee status at an education institution". It exists so that a common output cut — full-time university students aged 15 to 24, say — can be read from a single field instead of a three-way cross-tabulation. Its not-applicable code means the person was not attending an institution.
value_definition: About thirty two-digit codes: 10 preschool, 21 to 29 primary by sector, 31 to 39 secondary by sector, 41 to 45, 51 to 55 and 61 to 65 for vocational, university and tertiary-not-further-defined broken by age and study mode, 71 to 73 other, plus && not stated, @@ not applicable and VV overseas visitor, thirty codes in all.
limitation: It cannot be decomposed cleanly, because the tertiary codes bundle an age band and a study mode into one value: recovering full-time status alone means mapping codes back rather than reading a field, and STUP is the direct column for that. The age bands inside it are fixed for output and cannot be recut, so AGEP is still needed for any other age analysis.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page for TYSTAP names the three input variables, gives the code ranges and their structure, and states the composition of the not-applicable group.
evidence_quote: This variable combines responses from Type of educational institution attending (TYPP), Full-time/part-time student status (STUP) and Age (AGEP) to indicate a person's attendee status at an education institution.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Educational Institution: Attendee Status' with the generic sentence twice, which did not reveal that the variable is a derived cross-classification of three columns, nor that its tertiary codes carry an age band.

value_domain: Census usual address one year ago indicator
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Usual address one year ago indicator (UAI1P)
variable_description: Whether a person's usual address a year before the Census was the same one they usually live at now, another Australian address, or an address overseas. The ABS defines it as indicating whether a person "lived in the same address one year ago as their current usual residence, lived elsewhere in Australia one year ago, [or] usually lived in another country one year ago", from the question 'Where did the person usually live one year ago (at 10 August 2020)?'. STEU1P holds the state that goes with it and UAI5P asks the same question over five years. It applies to people aged one year and over, so infants are not applicable.
value_definition: Six codes: 1 same address as at this Census, 2 elsewhere in Australia, 3 overseas one year earlier, & not stated, @ not applicable for people aged under one, and V overseas visitor.
limitation: 'Same address' means the same usual residence at two points, not that the person never moved: someone who moved out and back within the year reads identically to someone who stayed put. Where a child under 16 gave no answer the value can be copied from a parent's response, so an apparent child move is really the parent's, and the two records are not independent.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page for UAI1P gives the definition, the exact question and reference date, the full code list, the derivation from a reported address where the mark box was blank, and the copying rule for children under 16.
evidence_quote: This variable contains the response category answer to the question 'Where did the person usually live one year ago (at 10 August 2020)?'.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Usual Address One Year Ago Indicator' with the generic no-finite-list sentence twice, despite the domain being six published codes, and it did not disclose that children's values may be inherited from a parent.

value_domain: Census usual address five years ago indicator
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Usual address five years ago indicator (UAI5P)
variable_description: Whether a person's usual address five years before the Census was the same one they live at now, another Australian address, or an overseas one. The ABS defines it as indicating whether a person "lived in the same address five years ago as their current usual residence, lived elsewhere in Australia five years ago, [or] usually lived in another country five years ago", asked as 'Where did the person usually live five years ago (at 10 August 2016)?'. It pairs with STEU5P, which holds the state, and with UAI1P for the shorter window. It applies to people aged five and over.
value_definition: Six codes: 1 same address as at this Census, 2 elsewhere in Australia, 3 overseas five years earlier, & not stated, @ not applicable for people aged under five, and V overseas visitor.
limitation: Five years is a single gap, not a history: a person who moved three times and one who moved once both read 'elsewhere in Australia', and nothing in the column dates any move. Where a person under 20 gave no answer but a parent did, the child takes the parent's value, so youth mobility measured from this column is largely household mobility. Non-response was 6.0% in 2021.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page for UAI5P gives the definition, the question and reference date, the six codes, the copying rule for people aged under 20, and the 6.0% non-response rate for 2021.
evidence_quote: This variable is derived from the response category answer to the question on the 2021 Census forms which asks, 'Where did the person usually live five years ago (at 10 August 2016)?'.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Usual Address Five Years Ago Indicator' and the generic sentence twice, so it neither published the six-code domain nor warned that a young person's value can be inherited from a parent.

value_domain: Census usual address indicator on Census Night
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Usual address indicator Census night (UAICP)
variable_description: Whether the person was counted at their own usual address on Census Night or somewhere else. The ABS defines it as indicating "whether a person was at home or elsewhere on Census Night". This is the column that tells a reader when the enumeration geography and the usual-residence geography part company: where it reads 'elsewhere in Australia', the dwelling the person appears in is not the dwelling they live in, and the household composition around them is not their own. Non-response was 4.3% in 2021, and where usual residence was not stated both this variable and PURP are imputed.
value_definition: Three published categories: 1 at home, 2 elsewhere in Australia, and V overseas visitor. Where the mark box was blank but a usual address was reported, the indicator is derived from that address.
limitation: It does not say where 'elsewhere' was, or why. A fly-in-fly-out worker in a mining camp, a patient in hospital and a family on holiday all take code 2, and PURP has to be compared with the enumeration geography to see how far apart the two places were. It also cannot be used to identify visitors reliably at the household level, because a dwelling holds no marker of how many of its occupants were away.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page for UAICP gives the definition, the three categories, the derivation from a reported address and the joint imputation with place of usual residence, plus the 2021 and 2016 non-response rates.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates whether a person was at home or elsewhere on Census Night.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Usual Address Indicator Census Night' with the generic sentence twice, which said nothing about the de facto versus usual-residence distinction that this column exists to mark.

value_domain: ASGS Urban Centre or Locality of the dwelling
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Urban Centres and Localities
variable_description: The named town or urban area the dwelling was enumerated in, on the 2021 dwelling table. The ABS says "Urban Centres and Localities (UCLs) represent areas of concentrated urban development" and are "defined using Statistical Areas Level 1 (SA1s) that meet density and/or urban infrastructure criteria", with urban centres needing 1,000 people or more and localities 200 to 999. It is the finest of the dwelling table's settlement geographies, sitting under SUAD and beside SOSD and SOSRD, which band the same classification into urban-rural groupings.
value_definition: A six-digit hierarchical code built from the state or territory, the section of state, the section of state range and a UCL identifier, so Jervis Bay (L) is 9-2-2-002. Special codes cover migratory, off-shore and shipping (997), no usual address (994) and outside Australia.
limitation: The boundaries are rebuilt from each Census's own population and dwelling density, so a dwelling can change code between 2016 and 2021 without moving and the two vintages are not directly comparable. Rural areas fall outside every urban centre and locality and are labelled remainder of state or territory, so this is not a complete address geography and cannot substitute for a suburb or postcode.
rationale: The ASGS Edition 3 Urban Centres and Localities page gives the definition, the SA1 density criteria, the population thresholds for centres and localities, the six-digit code structure and the rural remainder handling.
evidence_quote: Urban Centres and Localities (UCLs) represent areas of concentrated urban development.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the metadata phrase 'Urban centres and localities (en)' with the generic sentence twice, which did not say that a published ASGS classification stands behind the codes or that the boundaries are re-derived each Census.

value_domain: ASGS Urban Centre or Locality of usual residence
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Urban Centres and Localities
variable_description: The named town or urban area a person usually lives in, on the 2021 person table. The ABS says "Urban Centres and Localities (UCLs) represent areas of concentrated urban development", built from SA1s meeting density or urban infrastructure criteria, with urban centres at 1,000 people or more and localities between 200 and 999. SOSP and SOSRP on the same row are the coarse urban-rural cuts of this same classification, and SUAP is the 10,000-plus aggregation above it, so the three together let a person be placed on a settlement-size gradient rather than in an administrative area.
value_definition: A six-digit hierarchical code composed of state or territory, section of state, section of state range and a UCL identifier, with special codes for migratory, off-shore and shipping, no usual address, and outside Australia.
limitation: Settlement size sits in the middle of the code rather than in the UCL identifier: the second and third digits are Section of State and Section of State Range, so a size comparison has to read those, or the SOSP and SOSRP columns, not the UCL name. The ABS also states that urban centres and localities "are not an official definition of towns and cities", so a UCL boundary will not agree with a council's or a resident's idea of where a town ends.
rationale: The ASGS Edition 3 page gives the definition, the construction from SA1s, the population thresholds, the code structure and the explicit warning that these are not official town definitions; the registry shows UCLP in the person table's usual-residence geography block with SOSP, SOSRP and SUAP.
evidence_quote: Urban Centres and Localities (UCLs) represent areas of concentrated urban development.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Urban centres and localities (ur)' with the generic sentence twice, so a reader learnt neither what the classification is, that '(ur)' means usual residence, nor that the ABS warns against reading the areas as official towns.

value_domain: Census unemployed or employed flag
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Unemployment flag (UEFP)
variable_description: A two-way employed-or-unemployed split for people in the labour force, built so Census unemployment can be reported consistently for national indicators. The ABS says it "flags whether a person is unemployed or employed for people who reported they are in the labour force" and that it "is used for national reporting purposes", specifically Closing the Gap Target 8. It is a collapse of LFSP, so it adds no information but fixes the denominator: everyone not in the labour force, aged under 15, or with unstated labour force status is not applicable rather than counted as employed.
value_definition: Four categories: 1 unemployed, 2 employed, @ not applicable, and V overseas visitor. Not applicable covers people aged under 15, people not in the labour force and people whose labour force status was not stated.
limitation: It is not a rate and cannot supply a population denominator, because the not-applicable category mixes children, people outside the labour force and non-respondents into one value. It also cannot grade employment: a person working one hour in the reference week and a person working full time both take code 2, and HRSP holds hours worked.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page for UEFP gives the definition, the four codes, the derivation from LFSP, the composition of the not-applicable group and the Closing the Gap target it supports.
evidence_quote: This variable flags whether a person is unemployed or employed for people who reported they are in the labour force.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Unemployment flag' with the generic no-finite-list sentence twice, even though the domain is four published codes, and it gave no hint that the flag is a reporting device with a deliberately narrow scope.

value_domain: Census unpaid assistance to a person with disability indicator
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Unpaid assistance to a person with disability, health condition or due to old age (UNCAREP)
variable_description: Whether a person aged 15 and over gave unpaid care, help or assistance in the two weeks before Census Night because of a disability, a long-term health condition or a problem related to old age. The ABS defines it as recording people who "spent time providing unpaid care, help or assistance to family members or others" for those reasons, and notes that it "includes people who are in receipt of a Carer Allowance or Carer Payment". It is the Census's carer identifier, and ASSNP on the same row is the other side of the relationship: whether the person themselves needs assistance with a core activity. CHCAREP and DOMP cover unpaid child care and unpaid domestic work, which this question excludes.
value_definition: Five categories: no unpaid assistance provided, provided unpaid assistance, not stated, not applicable for persons aged under 15, and overseas visitor.
limitation: It is a yes-or-no over a two-week window and carries no hours, so a person who gave an hour of help and a full-time carer share one code. The care recipient can live anywhere, so the column cannot say who was cared for and will not, on its own, identify a co-resident carer and cared-for pair; joining ASSNP within a dwelling is an inference, not a stated relationship.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page for UNCAREP gives the definition, the three qualifying reasons, the explicit inclusion of Carer Allowance and Carer Payment recipients, the reference period and the five categories with the under-15 exclusion.
evidence_quote: This variable records the number of people who in the two weeks prior to Census Night spent time providing unpaid care, help or assistance to family members or others because of: a disability a long-term health condition problems related to old age
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Unpaid Assistance to a Person with a Disability' with the generic sentence twice, which omitted the two-week reference period, the five-code domain and the fact that the recipient need not live with the carer.

value_domain: Count of motor vehicles at the dwelling
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of motor vehicles (VEHD)
variable_description: How many registered motor vehicles the household had garaged or parked at or near the dwelling on Census Night. The ABS defines it as recording "the number of registered motor vehicles owned or used by household members that were garaged or parked at or near private dwellings on Census Night", written as a number on the form or answered with a 'None' mark box. It applies to occupied private dwellings only, and it is a count at a place on a night rather than a register of what the household owns. VEHRD holds the banded version.
value_definition: Thirty-three categories: single values for 0 to 29 vehicles, one category for 30 or more, plus not stated and not applicable.
limitation: A car away with a household member on Census Night is out of scope even though the household owns it, and a company car kept at the dwelling and used by a resident is in scope even though nobody there owns it, so this is not a measure of household vehicle ownership. Motorbikes, scooters, heavy vehicles over 4.5 tonnes, tractors, boats and caravans are all excluded. Non-response was 5.4% in 2021.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page for VEHD gives the definition, the code range to 29 with a 30-or-more group, the capture method, the exclusions and the non-response rate.
evidence_quote: This variable records the number of registered motor vehicles owned or used by household members that were garaged or parked at or near private dwellings on Census Night.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Number of Motor Vehicles' with the generic no-finite-list sentence twice, despite a closed 33-category domain, and it did not warn that the count is location-based on one night rather than ownership-based.

value_domain: Banded count of motor vehicles at the dwelling
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of motor vehicles (ranges) (VEHRD)
variable_description: The banded vehicle count for the dwelling, from none to four or more. The ABS defines it as recording "the number in ranges of registered motor vehicles owned or used by household members that were garaged or parked at or near private dwellings on Census Night", grouping "1 to 3 motor vehicles available singly, then responses of 4 or more motor vehicles coded into the grouped category". It is the output form most Census tables use, and it inherits VEHD's exclusions of motorbikes, scooters and heavy vehicles.
value_definition: Seven categories: 0 no motor vehicles, 1 one, 2 two, 3 three, 4 four or more motor vehicles, plus & not stated and @ not applicable.
limitation: The top band closes at four, so a four-car household and a fifteen-car one are indistinguishable and any mean vehicles-per-dwelling built from this column understates the true figure; VEHD keeps single values to 29 and is the column for that. Because it is a regrouping of VEHD it repeats the same non-response rather than resolving any of it.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page for VEHRD gives the definition, the five substantive bands with not stated and not applicable, and the explicit statement of how the bands differ from VEHD's coding.
evidence_quote: This variable groups responses to this question, with 1 to 3 motor vehicles available singly, then responses of 4 or more motor vehicles coded into the grouped category of 'Four or more motor vehicles'.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Number of Motor Vehicles (ranges)' with the generic sentence twice, which hid a five-category closed domain and the top-coding that makes averages from this column differ from VEHD.

value_domain: Census voluntary work indicator
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Voluntary work for an organisation or group (VOLWP)
variable_description: Whether a person aged 15 and over did unpaid voluntary work for an organisation or group in the twelve months before Census Night. The ABS defines it as recording "people who spent time doing unpaid voluntary work for an organisation or group in the twelve months prior to Census Night". The words 'for an organisation or group' are the working part of the definition: help given informally to a neighbour or relative does not count here, and UNCAREP, CHCAREP and DOMP hold the unpaid work done outside organisations. Where a respondent marked both yes and no, the yes is accepted.
value_definition: Five categories: 1 not a volunteer, 2 volunteer, & not stated, @ not applicable for persons aged under 15, and V overseas visitor.
limitation: It carries no hours and no frequency, so a single afternoon at a school fete across the year reads the same as a weekly shift, and it cannot support any estimate of volunteering effort. The twelve-month window also means it is a recall question rather than a Census-night observation, so it is more exposed to memory error than the other unpaid work variables.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page for VOLWP gives the definition, the twelve-month reference period, the five categories, the 15-and-over scope and the rule for conflicting mark box responses.
evidence_quote: This variable records people who spent time doing unpaid voluntary work for an organisation or group in the twelve months prior to Census Night.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Voluntary Work for an Organisation or Group' and the generic no-finite-list sentence twice, so it published neither the five-code domain nor the exclusion of informal help that decides what the variable counts.

value_domain: Census non-school qualification attainment or study indicator
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, People with or working towards a non-school qualification (WTNSQP)
variable_description: Splits people aged 15 and over four ways: holding a non-school qualification, working towards one, both, or neither. The ABS says the variable "indicates whether a person has a non-school qualification, is working towards a non-school qualification or both" and that it "is used for national reporting purposes" — it feeds Report on Government Services indicators BA.7 and BA.8 on 20 to 64 year olds. It is derived by combining QALLP, the level of a completed non-school qualification, with TYPP, the type of institution being attended, so it holds no new answer of its own. People aged under 15 and primary school attendees are not applicable.
value_definition: Seven categories: with a non-school qualification only, working towards one only, with and working towards one, neither, status not determined or not stated, not applicable, and overseas visitor.
limitation: It does not carry the level of the qualification — a certificate I and a doctorate both read 'with a non-school qualification', and QALLP is the column that ranks them. 'Working towards' is read from attendance at a non-school institution at Census time, so it is a snapshot of that week rather than evidence that a qualification is on track or will be finished.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page for WTNSQP gives the definition, the two input variables, the seven categories, the 15-and-over scope with the primary school exclusion, and the RoGS indicators it supports.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates whether a person has a non-school qualification, is working towards a non-school qualification or both.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'People with or working towards a non-school qualification' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say the column is derived from QALLP and TYPP, nor that it deliberately discards qualification level.

value_domain: Year of first arrival in Australia
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (YARP)
variable_description: The calendar year an overseas-born person first came to Australia intending to stay a year or more. The ABS says the variable "is applicable to persons born overseas and records the year they first arrived in Australia to live for one year or more", with scope set by BPLP, country of birth, so Australian-born records are not applicable rather than missing. Subtracting it from the Census year gives years of residence, which is the standard way to see how migrant outcomes change with time in the country. High and low values are checked against the form image and the stated age is tested for compatibility with the claimed period of residence.
value_definition: A four-digit year running from 1905 to the Census year, with &&&& not stated, @@@@ not applicable and VVVV overseas visitor.
limitation: It records the first arrival, not the current stay: a person who arrived in 1998, left for a decade and returned in 2015 still reads 1998, so years of residence computed from it can be far too long for return migrants. It is also not a visa or citizenship record and says nothing about how the person entered — CITP holds Australian citizenship and the Census carries no visa field. Non-response was 2.4% in 2021.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page for YARP gives the definition, the overseas-born scope set by country of birth, the 1905-to-Census-year range with supplementary codes, the editing checks and the non-response rate.
evidence_quote: This variable is applicable to persons born overseas and records the year they first arrived in Australia to live for one year or more.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Year of Arrival in Australia' with the generic no-finite-list sentence twice, so it did not state the bounded year range, the country-of-birth scope, or the first-arrival rule that makes the variable mismeasure return migrants.

value_domain: Banded year of first arrival in Australia
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (ranges) (YARRP)
variable_description: The banded arrival year for overseas-born people, running in decades from 1905-1950 to 2011-2020 with a final part-year band to Census Night. The ABS says it "is applicable to persons born overseas and records the year in ranges when they first arrived in Australia to live for one year or more" and that it "is derived from Year of arrival in Australia (YARP)". Use it where a banded output is wanted; YARP holds the exact year for anything that needs years of residence computed.
value_definition: Nine bands: 1905-1950, then each decade to 2011-2020, and a final band covering 1 January to 10 August 2021, plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor.
limitation: The band edges are fixed against the Census year, so the same person falls in a differently defined top band in the 2016 and 2021 files and the two vintages cannot be compared without going back to YARP. The last band also covers only part of a year, so a recent-arrival share read from it is not annualised and understates arrivals per year.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page for YARRP gives the definition, the band list including the part-year final band, and the statement that it is derived from YARP.
evidence_quote: This variable is applicable to persons born overseas and records the year in ranges when they first arrived in Australia to live for one year or more.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Year of Arrival in Australia (ranges)' with the generic sentence twice, which withheld the published band list and the part-year final band that breaks naive rate calculations.

value_domain: Census Year 12 or Certificate II attainment flag
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Attainment of Year 12 or Certificate II or higher (YR12C2P)
variable_description: A yes-or-no attainment flag set at the Year 12 or Certificate II threshold, for people aged 15 and over. The ABS says it "indicates whether a person has attained Year 12 or equivalent or Certificate II or higher" and that it "is used for national reporting purposes" — Closing the Gap Target 6 and Report on Government Services indicator BA.10 on 20 to 24 year olds. It is a recode built during processing from HSCP, the highest year of school completed, and QALLP, the level of non-school qualification, rather than a question in its own right. YR12C3P sets the same test one certificate level higher.
value_definition: Four categories: 1 attained Year 12 or equivalent or Certificate II or higher, 2 has not attained, @ not applicable, and V overseas visitor.
limitation: It cannot say which route a person took to clear the bar: Year 12 with no qualification and a Certificate II with no Year 12 both read code 1, so the flag will not support any claim about schooling specifically. For national reporting the ABS further excludes records with missing or inadequate responses, so a published proportion rests on a smaller denominator than a straight count of codes 1 and 2 in this file.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page for YR12C2P gives the definition, the four codes, the derivation from HSCP and QALLP, the 15-and-over scope and the national reporting exclusions and targets.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates whether a person has attained Year 12 or equivalent or Certificate II or higher.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Attainment of year 12 or certificate ii or higher' with the generic no-finite-list sentence twice, although the domain is four published codes, and it did not say the column is a recode of two other variables.

value_domain: Census Year 12 or Certificate III attainment flag
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Attainment of Year 12 or Certificate III or higher (YR12C3P)
variable_description: The same attainment flag as YR12C2P with the bar set one level higher, at Year 12 or Certificate III. The ABS says it "indicates whether a person has attained Year 12 or equivalent or Certificate III or higher", built during processing by running HSCP and QALLP through a matrix. This is the threshold behind Closing the Gap Target 5, which aims for 96% of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people aged 20 to 24 by 2031, and behind Report on Government Services indicators BA.12, BA.14 and BA.15. It applies to people aged 15 and over.
value_definition: Four categories: 1 attained Year 12 or equivalent or Certificate III or higher, 2 has not attained, @ not applicable, and V overseas visitor.

Neither column dates the attainment, so it cannot show whether a qualification was gained since the previous Census.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page for YR12C3P gives the definition, the four codes, the matrix derivation from HSCP and QALLP, the 15-and-over scope and the Closing the Gap and RoGS indicators it supports.
evidence_quote: This variable indicates whether a person has attained Year 12 or equivalent or Certificate III or higher.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Attainment of year 12 or certificate iii or higher' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not publish the four-code domain nor flag that this variable is a strict subset of YR12C2P.
